attendance_data = [
    ("EMP001", "2024-01-15", "09:00:00", "17:30:00", "present"),
    ("EMP001", "2024-01-16", "09:15:00", "17:00:00", "present"),
    ("EMP001", "2024-01-17", None, None, "sick_leave"),
    ("EMP001", "2024-01-18", "09:00:00", "17:30:00", "present"),
    ("EMP002", "2024-01-15", "08:45:00", "18:00:00", "present"),
    ("EMP002", "2024-01-16", "09:30:00", "17:30:00", "present"),
]

attendance_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    attendance_data,
    ["employee_id", "date", "check_in", "check_out", "status"]
) \
    .withColumn("attendance_date", to_date(col("date"), "yyyy-MM-dd")) \
    .withColumn("check_in_time", 
                when(col("check_in").isNotNull(),
                     to_timestamp(concat_ws(" ", col("date"), col("check_in")), 
                                 "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"))
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("check_out_time",
                when(col("check_out").isNotNull(),
                     to_timestamp(concat_ws(" ", col("date"), col("check_out")), 
                                 "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"))
                .otherwise(None))

# Calculate work hours and attendance metrics
attendance_metrics = attendance_df \
    .withColumn("work_hours",
                when(col("check_in_time").isNotNull() & col("check_out_time").isNotNull(),
                     (unix_timestamp(col("check_out_time")) - 
                      unix_timestamp(col("check_in_time"))) / 3600)
                .otherwise(0)) \
    .withColumn("is_late",
                when(col("check_in_time").isNotNull(),
                     hour(col("check_in_time")) * 60 + minute(col("check_in_time")) > 9 * 60)
                .otherwise(False)) \
    .withColumn("is_early_departure",
                when(col("check_out_time").isNotNull(),
                     hour(col("check_out_time")) * 60 + minute(col("check_out_time")) < 17 * 60)
                .otherwise(False)) \
    .withColumn("is_overtime",
                col("work_hours") > 8) \
    .withColumn("overtime_hours",
                when(col("work_hours") > 8, col("work_hours") - 8)
                .otherwise(0))

print("\nAttendance Metrics:")
attendance_metrics.select(
    "employee_id",
    "attendance_date",
    "status",
    "check_in_time",
    "check_out_time",
    "work_hours",
    "is_late",
    "overtime_hours"
).show(truncate=False)

# Aggregate by employee
employee_summary = attendance_metrics.groupBy("employee_id") \
    .agg(
        expr("COUNT(*) as total_days"),
        expr("SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'present' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as days_present"),
        expr("SUM(CASE WHEN status LIKE '%leave%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as days_on_leave"),
        expr("SUM(CASE WHEN is_late THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as late_arrivals"),
        expr("SUM(work_hours) as total_work_hours"),
        expr("AVG(work_hours) as avg_work_hours"),
        expr("SUM(overtime_hours) as total_overtime_hours")
    ) \
    .withColumn("attendance_rate",
                (col("days_present") / col("total_days") * 100))

print("\nEmployee Summary:")
employee_summary.show(truncate=False)


# Scenario 3: Time Series Data with Gaps Detection
print("\nScenario 3: Time Series Gap Detection")
print("-" * 80)

timeseries_data = [
    ("2024-01-01", 100),
    ("2024-01-02", 105),
    ("2024-01-03", 110),
    # Gap: 2024-01-04 missing
    ("2024-01-05", 115),
    ("2024-01-06", 120),
    # Gap: 2024-01-07, 2024-01-08 missing
    ("2024-01-09", 125),
]

timeseries_df = spark.createDataFrame(timeseries_data, ["date_str", "value"]) \
    .withColumn("date", to_date(col("date_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))

print("\nOriginal Time Series (with gaps):")
timeseries_df.show(truncate=False)

# Detect gaps using window functions
timeseries_window = Window.orderBy("date")

gaps_detected = timeseries_df \
    .withColumn("prev_date", 
                expr("LAG(date) OVER (ORDER BY date)")) \
    .withColumn("days_gap",
                when(col("prev_date").isNotNull(),
                     datediff(col("date"), col("prev_date")))
                .otherwise(0)) \
    .withColumn("has_gap", col("days_gap") > 1) \
    .withColumn("gap_size", col("days_gap") - 1)

print("\nGap Detection:")
gaps_detected.select(
    "date",
    "value",
    "prev_date",
    "days_gap",
    "has_gap",
    "gap_size"
).show(truncate=False)

# Fill gaps with complete date range
min_date = timeseries_df.agg(expr("MIN(date)").alias("min_date")).collect()[0]["min_date"]
max_date = timeseries_df.agg(expr("MAX(date)").alias("max_date")).collect()[0]["max_date"]

complete_date_range = spark.sql(f"""
    SELECT explode(sequence(
        to_date('{min_date}'),
        to_date('{max_date}'),
        interval 1 day
    )) as date
""")

# Left join to show missing dates
complete_timeseries = complete_date_range.join(
    timeseries_df,
    "date",
    "left"
) \
    .withColumn("is_missing", col("value").isNull()) \
    .withColumn("filled_value",
                when(col("value").isNotNull(), col("value"))
                .otherwise(None))  # Could use forward fill or interpolation

print("\nComplete Time Series (gaps identified):")
complete_timeseries.orderBy("date").show(truncate=False)

                .when(hour(col("shift_start")).between(14, 21), "Afternoon")
                .otherwise("Night"))

    ticket_data,
    ["ticket_id", "created_at", "resolved_at", "priority", "status"]
) \
    .withColumn("created_ts", to_timestamp(col("created_at"), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss")) \
    .withColumn("resolved_ts", 
                when(col("resolved_at").isNotNull(),
                     to_timestamp(col("resolved_at"), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"))
                .otherwise(None))

# Define SLA targets (in hours)
sla_targets = {
    "high": 4,
    "medium": 24,
    "low": 72
```python
}

# Calculate SLA metrics
sla_monitoring = ticket_df \
    .withColumn("current_time", current_timestamp()) \
    .withColumn("resolution_time_hours",
                when(col("resolved_ts").isNotNull(),
                     (unix_timestamp(col("resolved_ts")) - 
                      unix_timestamp(col("created_ts"))) / 3600)
                .otherwise(
                     (unix_timestamp(col("current_time")) - 
                      unix_timestamp(col("created_ts"))) / 3600
                )) \
    .withColumn("sla_target_hours",
                when(col("priority") == "high", lit(4))
                .when(col("priority") == "medium", lit(24))
                .otherwise(lit(72))) \
    .withColumn("sla_met",
                col("resolution_time_hours") <= col("sla_target_hours")) \
    .withColumn("sla_breach_hours",
                when(~col("sla_met"),
                     col("resolution_time_hours") - col("sla_target_hours"))
                .otherwise(0)) \
    .withColumn("sla_status",
                when(col("status") == "open",
                     when(col("resolution_time_hours") > col("sla_target_hours"), "Breached")
                     .when(col("resolution_time_hours") > col("sla_target_hours") * 0.8, "At Risk")
                     .otherwise("On Track"))
                .when(col("sla_met"), "Met")
                .otherwise("Breached")) \
    .withColumn("time_remaining_hours",
                when(col("status") == "open",
                     col("sla_target_hours") - col("resolution_time_hours"))
                .otherwise(None))

print("\nSLA Monitoring Dashboard:")
sla_monitoring.select(
    "ticket_id",
    "priority",
    "status",
    "created_ts",
    "resolved_ts",
    "resolution_time_hours",
    "sla_target_hours",
    "sla_status",
    "sla_breach_hours",
    "time_remaining_hours"
).show(truncate=False)

# SLA Summary by Priority
sla_summary = sla_monitoring.groupBy("priority") \
    .agg(
        expr("COUNT(*) as total_tickets"),
        expr("SUM(CASE WHEN sla_met THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as tickets_met_sla"),
        expr("SUM(CASE WHEN NOT sla_met THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as tickets_breached_sla"),
        expr("AVG(resolution_time_hours) as avg_resolution_hours"),
        expr("MAX(resolution_time_hours) as max_resolution_hours"),
        expr("AVG(sla_breach_hours) as avg_breach_hours")
    ) \
    .withColumn("sla_compliance_rate",
                (col("tickets_met_sla") / col("total_tickets") * 100))

print("\nSLA Summary by Priority:")
sla_summary.show(truncate=False)

```python
                when(col("hours_since_update") > col("sla_hours") * 2, "Critical")
                .when(col("hours_since_update") > col("sla_hours"), "Warning")

def validate_date_range(df, date_col, min_date=None, max_date=None):
    """
    Validate that dates fall within expected range
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame to validate
        date_col: Name of date column
        min_date: Minimum allowed date (optional)
        max_date: Maximum allowed date (optional)
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with validation results
    """
    validated_df = df.withColumn("is_valid", lit(True))
    
    if min_date:
        validated_df = validated_df.withColumn(
            "is_valid",
            col("is_valid") & (col(date_col) >= lit(min_date))
        )
    
    if max_date:
        validated_df = validated_df.withColumn(
            "is_valid",
            col("is_valid") & (col(date_col) <= lit(max_date))
        )
    
    return validated_df

# Example usage
print("\nDate Range Validation Example:")
validation_data = [
    ("2024-01-15",),
    ("2024-06-20",),
    ("2023-12-31",),
    ("2025-01-01",),
]

validation_df = spark.createDataFrame(validation_data, ["date_str"]) \
    .withColumn("date", to_date(col("date_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))

validated_result = validate_date_range(
    validation_df, 
    "date", 
    min_date="2024-01-01", 
    max_date="2024-12-31"
)

validated_result.show(truncate=False)

# Count invalid records
invalid_count = validated_result.filter(~col("is_valid")).count()
print(f"Invalid records found: {invalid_count}")


def detect_date_anomalies(df, date_col):
    """
    Detect anomalies in date sequences
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame with dates
        date_col: Name of date column
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with anomaly flags
    """
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    window_spec = Window.orderBy(date_col)
    
    anomaly_df = df \
        .withColumn("prev_date", expr(f"LAG({date_col}) OVER (ORDER BY {date_col})")) \
        .withColumn("next_date", expr(f"LEAD({date_col}) OVER (ORDER BY {date_col})")) \
        .withColumn("gap_from_prev", 
                    when(col("prev_date").isNotNull(),
                         datediff(col(date_col), col("prev_date")))
                    .otherwise(None)) \
        .withColumn("gap_to_next",
                    when(col("next_date").isNotNull(),
                         datediff(col("next_date"), col(date_col)))
                    .otherwise(None)) \
        .withColumn("has_large_gap_before", col("gap_from_prev") > 7) \
        .withColumn("has_large_gap_after", col("gap_to_next") > 7) \
        .withColumn("is_duplicate",
                    col("gap_from_prev") == 0) \
        .withColumn("anomaly_type",
                    when(col("is_duplicate"), "Duplicate")
                    .when(col("has_large_gap_before") | col("has_large_gap_after"), "Large Gap")
                    .otherwise("Normal"))
    
    return anomaly_df

# Example usage
print("\nDate Anomaly Detection Example:")
anomaly_data = [
    ("2024-01-01",),
    ("2024-01-02",),
    ("2024-01-02",),  # Duplicate
    ("2024-01-03",),
    ("2024-01-15",),  # Large gap
    ("2024-01-16",),
]

anomaly_test_df = spark.createDataFrame(anomaly_data, ["date_str"]) \
    .withColumn("date", to_date(col("date_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))

anomaly_results = detect_date_anomalies(anomaly_test_df, "date")

anomaly_results.select(
    "date",
    "prev_date",
    "gap_from_prev",
    "anomaly_type"
).show(truncate=False)

# Comprehensive date/time analytics
ecommerce_analytics = ecommerce_df \
    .withColumn("current_time", current_timestamp()) \
    .withColumn("order_date", to_date(col("order_placed_ts"))) \
    .withColumn("order_year", year(col("order_placed_ts"))) \
    .withColumn("order_month", month(col("order_placed_ts"))) \
    .withColumn("order_month_name", date_format(col("order_placed_ts"), "MMMM")) \
    .withColumn("order_day_name", date_format(col("order_placed_ts"), "EEEE")) \
    .withColumn("order_hour", hour(col("order_placed_ts"))) \
    .withColumn("is_weekend_order", dayofweek(col("order_placed_ts")).isin([1, 7])) \
    .withColumn("time_of_day",
                when(hour(col("order_placed_ts")).between(6, 11), "Morning")
                .when(hour(col("order_placed_ts")).between(12, 17), "Afternoon")
                .when(hour(col("order_placed_ts")).between(18, 21), "Evening")
                .otherwise("Night")) \
    .withColumn("payment_processing_time_minutes",
                when(col("payment_confirmed_ts").isNotNull(),
                     (unix_timestamp(col("payment_confirmed_ts")) - 
                      unix_timestamp(col("order_placed_ts"))) / 60)
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("time_to_ship_hours",
                when(col("shipped_ts").isNotNull(),
                     (unix_timestamp(col("shipped_ts")) - 
                      unix_timestamp(col("payment_confirmed_ts"))) / 3600)
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("delivery_time_days",
                when(col("delivered_ts").isNotNull(),
                     datediff(to_date(col("delivered_ts")), to_date(col("shipped_ts"))))
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("total_fulfillment_time_days",
                when(col("delivered_ts").isNotNull(),
                     datediff(to_date(col("delivered_ts")), to_date(col("order_placed_ts"))))
                .otherwise(
                     datediff(to_date(col("current_time")), to_date(col("order_placed_ts")))
                )) \
    .withColumn("order_age_days",
                datediff(to_date(col("current_time")), to_date(col("order_placed_ts")))) \
    .withColumn("is_delayed",
                when(col("status") == "delivered",
                     col("total_fulfillment_time_days") > 5)
                .when(col("status") == "in_transit",
                     col("order_age_days") > 3)
                .when(col("status") == "processing",
                     col("order_age_days") > 1)
                .otherwise(False)) \
    .withColumn("estimated_delivery",
                when(col("status") != "delivered",
                     date_add(col("order_date"), 5))
                .otherwise(to_date(col("delivered_ts"))))

# Customer analytics
customer_analytics = ecommerce_analytics.groupBy("customer_id") \
    .agg(
        expr("COUNT(*) as total_orders"),
        expr("SUM(amount) as total_spent"),
        expr("AVG(amount) as avg_order_value"),
        expr("MIN(order_placed_ts) as first_order_date"),
        expr("MAX(order_placed_ts) as last_order_date"),
        expr("AVG(total_fulfillment_time_days) as avg_fulfillment_days"),
        expr("SUM(CASE WHEN is_delayed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as delayed_orders")
    ) \
    .withColumn("customer_lifetime_days",
                datediff(col("last_order_date"), col("first_order_date"))) \
    .withColumn("avg_days_between_orders",
                when(col("total_orders") > 1,
                     col("customer_lifetime_days") / (col("total_orders") - 1))
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("customer_segment",
                when(col("total_spent") >= 500, "VIP")
                .when(col("total_spent") >= 200, "Premium")
                .otherwise("Regular"))

print("\nCustomer Analytics:")
customer_analytics.show(truncate=False)

    ) \
    .orderBy("order_hour")

def save_with_date_partition(df, base_path, date_column, partition_format="yyyy-MM-dd"):
    """
    Save DataFrame partitioned by date
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame to save
        base_path: Base path for output
        date_column: Column to partition by
        partition_format: Date format for partition folders
    """
    # Add partition columns
    partitioned_df = df \
        .withColumn("partition_year", year(col(date_column))) \
        .withColumn("partition_month", month(col(date_column))) \
        .withColumn("partition_day", dayofmonth(col(date_column)))
    
    # Write partitioned data
    # partitioned_df.write \
    #     .partitionBy("partition_year", "partition_month", "partition_day") \
    #     .mode("overwrite") \
    #     .parquet(base_path)
    
    print(f"Data would be saved to: {base_path}")
    print(f"Partitioned by: year={col('partition_year')}, month={col('partition_month')}, day={col('partition_day')}")
    
    return partitioned_df

# Example usage

    ecommerce_analytics,
    "/data/orders",
    "order_date"
)

# Running totals and moving averages

# Create window specifications
cumulative_window = Window.orderBy("order_date").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
rolling_7day_window = Window.orderBy("order_date").rangeBetween(-6 * 86400, 0)

# Daily aggregation first
daily_orders = ecommerce_analytics.groupBy("order_date") \
    .agg(
        expr("COUNT(*) as daily_orders"),
        expr("SUM(amount) as daily_revenue")
    ) \
    .orderBy("order_date")

# Apply window functions
windowed_analysis = daily_orders \
    .withColumn("cumulative_orders", 
                expr("SUM(daily_orders) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)")) \
    .withColumn("cumulative_revenue",
                expr("SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)")) \
    .withColumn("rolling_7day_orders",
                expr("SUM(daily_orders) OVER (ORDER BY order_date RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 6 DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)")) \
    .withColumn("rolling_7day_revenue",
                expr("SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 6 DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)")) \
    .withColumn("rolling_7day_avg_revenue",
                expr("AVG(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 6 DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)"))

print("\nWindow Function Results:")
windowed_analysis.show(truncate=False)

# Year-over-Year comparison (simulated with same year data)
print("\nPeriod-over-Period Comparison:")

period_comparison = daily_orders \
    .withColumn("prev_day_revenue",
                expr("LAG(daily_revenue, 1) OVER (ORDER BY order_date)")) \
    .withColumn("prev_week_revenue",
                expr("LAG(daily_revenue, 7) OVER (ORDER BY order_date)")) \
    .withColumn("day_over_day_change",
                when(col("prev_day_revenue").isNotNull(),
                     ((col("daily_revenue") - col("prev_day_revenue")) / col("prev_day_revenue") * 100))
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("week_over_week_change",
                when(col("prev_week_revenue").isNotNull(),
                     ((col("daily_revenue") - col("prev_week_revenue")) / col("prev_week_revenue") * 100))
                .otherwise(None))

period_comparison.show(truncate=False)

def generate_complete_date_dimension(start_date, end_date, spark):
    """
    Generate a comprehensive date dimension table
    
    Args:
        start_date: Start date (yyyy-MM-dd)
        end_date: End date (yyyy-MM-dd)
        spark: SparkSession
    
    Returns:
        Complete date dimension DataFrame
    """
    date_dim = spark.sql(f"""
        WITH date_sequence AS (
            SELECT explode(sequence(
                to_date('{start_date}'),
                to_date('{end_date}'),
                interval 1 day
            )) as date
        )
        SELECT
            -- Primary key
            date,
            date_format(date, 'yyyyMMdd') as date_key,
            
            -- Year attributes
            year(date) as year,
            date_format(date, 'yyyy') as year_name,
            CASE WHEN month(date) >= 4 THEN year(date) ELSE year(date) - 1 END as fiscal_year,
            
            -- Quarter attributes
            quarter(date) as quarter,
            CONCAT('Q', quarter(date)) as quarter_name,
            CASE 
                WHEN month(date) IN (4,5,6) THEN 1
                WHEN month(date) IN (7,8,9) THEN 2
                WHEN month(date) IN (10,11,12) THEN 3
                ELSE 4
            END as fiscal_quarter,
            
            -- Month attributes
            month(date) as month,
            date_format(date, 'MMMM') as month_name,
            date_format(date, 'MMM') as month_name_short,
            CONCAT(year(date), '-', LPAD(month(date), 2, '0')) as year_month,
            
            -- Week attributes
            weekofyear(date) as week_of_year,
            CONCAT(year(date), '-W', LPAD(weekofyear(date), 2, '0')) as year_week,
            
            -- Day attributes
            dayofmonth(date) as day_of_month,
            dayofyear(date) as day_of_year,
            dayofweek(date) as day_of_week,
            date_format(date, 'EEEE') as day_name,
            date_format(date, 'EEE') as day_name_short,
            
            -- Week indicators
            CASE WHEN dayofweek(date) IN (1, 7) THEN true ELSE false END as is_weekend,
            CASE WHEN dayofweek(date) NOT IN (1, 7) THEN true ELSE false END as is_weekday,
            
            -- Month indicators
            CASE WHEN dayofmonth(date) = 1 THEN true ELSE false END as is_first_day_of_month,
            CASE WHEN date = last_day(date) THEN true ELSE false END as is_last_day_of_month,
            
            -- Period boundaries
            trunc(date, 'month') as first_day_of_month,
            last_day(date) as last_day_of_month,
            trunc(date, 'quarter') as first_day_of_quarter,
            trunc(date, 'year') as first_day_of_year,
            
            -- Special dates
            CASE 
                WHEN month(date) = 1 AND dayofmonth(date) = 1 THEN true 
                ELSE false 
            END as is_new_year,
            CASE 
                WHEN month(date) = 12 AND dayofmonth(date) = 25 THEN true 
                ELSE false 
            END as is_christmas,
            
            -- Relative dates
            datediff(date, current_date()) as days_from_today,
            CASE 
                WHEN date = current_date() THEN 'Today'
                WHEN date = date_add(current_date(), -1) THEN 'Yesterday'
                WHEN date = date_add(current_date(), 1) THEN 'Tomorrow'
                WHEN date > current_date() THEN 'Future'
                ELSE 'Past'
            END as relative_to_today
            
        FROM date_sequence
    """)
    
    return date_dim

# Generate sample date dimension
print("\nGenerating Date Dimension (2024):")
date_dimension_2024 = generate_complete_date_dimension('2024-01-01', '2024-12-31', spark)

print("\nSample Date Dimension Records:")
date_dimension_2024.show(10, truncate=False)

print("\nDate Dimension Schema:")
date_dimension_2024.printSchema()

print(f"\nTotal records in date dimension: {date_dimension_2024.count()}")

# Show specific examples
print("\nWeekend Dates:")
date_dimension_2024.filter(col("is_weekend")).select(
    "date", "day_name", "week_of_year"
).show(10, truncate=False)

print("\nFirst and Last Days of Month:")
date_dimension_2024.filter(
    col("is_first_day_of_month") | col("is_last_day_of_month")
).select(
    "date", "month_name", "is_first_day_of_month", "is_last_day_of_month"
).show(10, truncate=False)

templates = """
# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 1: DATE PARSING WITH ERROR HANDLING
# ============================================================================

def safe_parse_date(df, date_col, formats, output_col="parsed_date"):
    \"\"\"Safely parse dates with multiple format attempts\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import coalesce, to_date
    
    parsed_cols = [to_date(date_col, fmt) for fmt in formats]
    return df.withColumn(output_col, coalesce(*parsed_cols))

# Usage:
# df = safe_parse_date(df, "date_string", 
#                      ["yyyy-MM-dd", "MM/dd/yyyy", "dd-MMM-yyyy"])


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 2: BUSINESS DAYS CALCULATION
# ============================================================================

def calculate_business_days_between(df, start_col, end_col, holidays_df=None):
    \"\"\"Calculate business days excluding weekends and holidays\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import expr, datediff, floor
    
    result_df = df.withColumn(
        "total_days", 
        datediff(end_col, start_col)
    ).withColumn(
        "total_weeks",
        expr(f"FLOOR(total_days / 7)")
    ).withColumn(
        "weekend_days",
        expr("total_weeks * 2")
    ).withColumn(
        "business_days_estimate",
        expr("total_days - weekend_days")
    )
    
    # TODO: Subtract holidays if holidays_df provided
    
    return result_df


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 3: DATE DIMENSION GENERATOR
# ============================================================================

def create_date_dimension(spark, start_date, end_date):
    \"\"\"Generate comprehensive date dimension table\"\"\"
    
    query = f\"\"\"
        SELECT
            date,
            year(date) as year,
            quarter(date) as quarter,
            month(date) as month,
            dayofmonth(date) as day,
            weekofyear(date) as week_of_year,
            dayofweek(date) as day_of_week,
            date_format(date, 'EEEE') as day_name,
            date_format(date, 'MMMM') as month_name,
            CASE WHEN dayofweek(date) IN (1, 7) THEN true ELSE false END as is_weekend
        FROM (
            SELECT explode(sequence(
                to_date('{start_date}'),
                to_date('{end_date}'),
                interval 1 day
            )) as date
        )
    \"\"\"
    
    return spark.sql(query)


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 4: TIME SERIES GAP DETECTION
# ============================================================================

def detect_time_series_gaps(df, date_col, expected_frequency_days=1):
    \"\"\"Detect gaps in time series data\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import lag, datediff, when
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    window_spec = Window.orderBy(date_col)
    
    return df.withColumn(
        "prev_date",
        lag(date_col).over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "days_gap",
        when(
            col("prev_date").isNotNull(),
            datediff(col(date_col), col("prev_date"))
        ).otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "has_gap",
        col("days_gap") > expected_frequency_days
    )


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 5: SLA MONITORING
# ============================================================================

def monitor_sla(df, created_col, resolved_col, priority_col, sla_map):
    \"\"\"Monitor SLA compliance for tickets/orders\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import when, unix_timestamp, current_timestamp
    
    result_df = df.withColumn("current_time", current_timestamp())
    
    # Add SLA target based on priority
    for priority, hours in sla_map.items():
        result_df = result_df.withColumn(
            "sla_hours",
            when(col(priority_col) == priority, hours)
            .otherwise(col("sla_hours") if "sla_hours" in result_df.columns else None)
        )
    
    # Calculate resolution time
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "resolution_hours",
        when(
            col(resolved_col).isNotNull(),
            (unix_timestamp(col(resolved_col)) - unix_timestamp(col(created_col))) / 3600
        ).otherwise(
            (unix_timestamp(col("current_time")) - unix_timestamp(col(created_col))) / 3600
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "sla_met",
        col("resolution_hours") <= col("sla_hours")
    )
    
    return result_df


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 6: ROLLING WINDOW CALCULATIONS
# ============================================================================

def add_rolling_metrics(df, date_col, value_col, window_days=7):
    \"\"\"Add rolling window calculations\"\"\"
    
    return df.withColumn(
        f"rolling_{window_days}d_sum",
        expr(f"SUM({value_col}) OVER (ORDER BY {date_col} " +
             f"RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL {window_days-1} DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)")
    ).withColumn(
        f"rolling_{window_days}d_avg",
        expr(f"AVG({value_col}) OVER (ORDER BY {date_col} " +
             f"RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL {window_days-1} DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)")
    )


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 7: AGE CALCULATION
# ============================================================================

def calculate_age(df, birth_date_col, reference_date=None):
    \"\"\"Calculate age from birth date\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import current_date, months_between, floor
    
    ref_date = reference_date if reference_date else current_date()
    
    return df.withColumn(
        "age_years",
        floor(months_between(ref_date, col(birth_date_col)) / 12)
    ).withColumn(
        "age_months_total",
        floor(months_between(ref_date, col(birth_date_col)))
    )


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 8: TIMEZONE CONVERSION
# ============================================================================

def convert_to_multiple_timezones(df, timestamp_col, timezones):
    \"\"\"Convert UTC timestamp to multiple timezones\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import from_utc_timestamp
    
    result_df = df
    for tz_name, tz_string in timezones.items():
        result_df = result_df.withColumn(
            f"time_{tz_name}",
            from_utc_timestamp(col(timestamp_col), tz_string)
        )
    
    return result_df

# Usage:
# timezones = {
#     'ny': 'America/New_York',
#     'london': 'Europe/London',
#     'tokyo': 'Asia/Tokyo'
# }
# df = convert_to_multiple_timezones(df, 'utc_timestamp', timezones)


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 9: DATA FRESHNESS CHECK
# ============================================================================

def check_data_freshness(df, last_updated_col, sla_hours):
    \"\"\"Check if data is fresh based on SLA\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import current_timestamp, unix_timestamp, when
    
    return df.withColumn(
        "current_time", current_timestamp()
    ).withColumn(
        "hours_since_update",
        (unix_timestamp(col("current_time")) - 
         unix_timestamp(col(last_updated_col))) / 3600
    ).withColumn(
        "is_stale",
        col("hours_since_update") > sla_hours
    ).withColumn(
        "freshness_status",
        when(col("hours_since_update") > sla_hours * 2, "Critical")
        .when(col("hours_since_update") > sla_hours, "Warning")
        .otherwise("Healthy")
    )


# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 10: FISCAL PERIOD CALCULATION
# ============================================================================

def add_fiscal_periods(df, date_col, fiscal_year_start_month=4):
    \"\"\"Add fiscal year and quarter columns\"\"\"
    from pyspark.sql.functions import year, month, when
    
    return df.withColumn(
        "fiscal_year",
        when(
            month(col(date_col)) >= fiscal_year_start_month,
            year(col(date_col))
        ).otherwise(year(col(date_col)) - 1)
    ).withColumn(
        "month_in_fiscal_year",
        when(
            month(col(date_col)) >= fiscal_year_start_month,
            month(col(date_col)) - fiscal_year_start_month + 1
        ).otherwise(
            month(col(date_col)) + (12 - fiscal_year_start_month + 1)
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "fiscal_quarter",
        when(col("month_in_fiscal_year").between(1, 3), "FQ1")
        .when(col("month_in_fiscal_year").between(4, 6), "FQ2")
        .when(col("month_in_fiscal_year").between(7, 9), "FQ3")
        .otherwise("FQ4")
    )

"""

print(templates)

Performance Optimization Checklist:

□ Use DATE type for dates (not STRING or TIMESTAMP)
□ Use TIMESTAMP type for datetime (not STRING)

□ Cache intermediate results with complex date calculations
□ Use broadcast joins for small date dimension tables
□ Avoid UDFs - use built-in Spark SQL functions
□ Use columnar format (Parquet) for better compression
□ Bucket tables on date columns for join optimization
□ Use date_trunc for grouping instead of extracting components
□ Minimize timezone conversions - store in UTC
□ Use RANGE BETWEEN for time-based windows (not ROWS BETWEEN)
□ Coalesce small partitions after date filtering
□ Use explain() to verify predicate pushdown

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("END-TO-END PIPELINE EXAMPLE")
print("=" * 80)

print("\nBuilding Complete Date Analytics Pipeline...")

# Simulate raw data with various date issues
raw_data = [
    ("1", "2024-01-15 09:30:00", "150.00", "completed", "2024-01-15", "NY"),
    ("2", "01/16/2024 14:20:00", "89.99", "completed", None, "LA"),
    ("3", "2024-01-20", "220.50", "pending", "2024-01-22", "CHI"),
    ("4", None, "75.00", "cancelled", "2024-01-23", "SF"),
    ("5", "2024-01-25 11:30:00", "320.00", "completed", "2024-01-28", "NY"),
]

raw_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    raw_data,
    ["order_id", "order_timestamp", "amount", "status", "delivery_date", "location"]
)

print("\n1. RAW DATA (with issues):")
raw_df.show(truncate=False)

# Step 1: Parse dates with error handling
print("\n2. PARSING DATES:")
parsed_df = raw_df \
    .withColumn("order_ts_parsed",
                coalesce(
                    to_timestamp(col("order_timestamp"), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"),
                    to_timestamp(col("order_timestamp"), "MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss"),
                    to_timestamp(col("order_timestamp"), "yyyy-MM-dd")
                )) \
    .withColumn("delivery_date_parsed",
                to_date(col("delivery_date"), "yyyy-MM-dd")) \
    .withColumn("has_valid_order_date", col("order_ts_parsed").isNotNull()) \
    .withColumn("has_valid_delivery_date", col("delivery_date_parsed").isNotNull())

parsed_df.select(
    "order_id", "order_timestamp", "order_ts_parsed", "has_valid_order_date"
).show(truncate=False)

# Step 2: Extract date components
print("\n3. EXTRACTING DATE COMPONENTS:")
enriched_df = parsed_df \
    .withColumn("order_date", to_date(col("order_ts_parsed"))) \
    .withColumn("order_year", year(col("order_ts_parsed"))) \
    .withColumn("order_month", month(col("order_ts_parsed"))) \
    .withColumn("order_day", dayofmonth(col("order_ts_parsed"))) \
    .withColumn("order_hour", hour(col("order_ts_parsed"))) \
    .withColumn("order_day_name", date_format(col("order_ts_parsed"), "EEEE")) \
    .withColumn("is_weekend", dayofweek(col("order_ts_parsed")).isin([1, 7]))

enriched_df.select(
    "order_id", "order_date", "order_day_name", "order_hour", "is_weekend"
).show(truncate=False)

# Step 3: Calculate durations and metrics
print("\n4. CALCULATING METRICS:")
metrics_df = enriched_df \
    .withColumn("current_date", current_date()) \
    .withColumn("delivery_time_days",
                when(col("delivery_date_parsed").isNotNull() & col("order_date").isNotNull(),
                     datediff(col("delivery_date_parsed"), col("order_date")))
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("order_age_days",
                when(col("order_date").isNotNull(),
                     datediff(col("current_date"), col("order_date")))
                .otherwise(None)) \
    .withColumn("is_delayed",
                when(col("status") == "completed",
                     col("delivery_time_days") > 5)
                .when(col("status") == "pending",
                     col("order_age_days") > 3)
                .otherwise(False))

metrics_df.select(
    "order_id", "status", "delivery_time_days", "order_age_days", "is_delayed"
).show(truncate=False)

# Step 4: Aggregate and summarize
print("\n5. AGGREGATIONS:")
summary_df = metrics_df \
    .filter(col("has_valid_order_date")) \
    .groupBy("order_day_name", "is_weekend") \
    .agg(
        expr("COUNT(*) as total_orders"),
        expr("SUM(CAST(amount AS DOUBLE)) as total_revenue"),
        expr("AVG(CAST(amount AS DOUBLE)) as avg_order_value"),
        expr("AVG(delivery_time_days) as avg_delivery_days"),
        expr("SUM(CASE WHEN is_delayed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as delayed_orders")
    ) \
    .withColumn("delay_rate_pct",
                (col("delayed_orders") / col("total_orders") * 100))

summary_df.show(truncate=False)

# Step 5: Data quality report
print("\n6. DATA QUALITY REPORT:")
quality_report = parsed_df.agg(
    expr("COUNT(*) as total_records"),
    expr("SUM(CASE WHEN has_valid_order_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as valid_order_dates"),
    expr("SUM(CASE WHEN has_valid_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as valid_delivery_dates"),
    expr("SUM(CASE WHEN NOT has_valid_order_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as invalid_order_dates"),
    expr("SUM(CASE WHEN NOT has_valid_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as invalid_delivery_dates")
) \
    .withColumn("order_date_quality_pct",
                (col("valid_order_dates") / col("total_records") * 100)) \
    .withColumn("delivery_date_quality_pct",
                (col("valid_delivery_dates") / col("total_records") * 100))

quality_report.show(truncate=False)


# ============================================================================
# FINAL SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("EXECUTION SUMMARY")
print("=" * 80)

# PySpark Numeric Processing Patterns - Comprehensive Guide

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, DoubleType, IntegerType
import math

# Initialize Spark Session
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("Numeric Processing Patterns") \
    .config("spark.driver.memory", "4g") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Sample dataset for demonstration
data = [
    ("Product_A", 123.456, 100.25, 15.789, 200.5, 1),
    ("Product_B", 456.789, 250.75, -23.456, 350.8, 2),
    ("Product_C", 789.123, 175.50, 45.678, 150.3, 3),
    ("Product_D", 234.567, 425.25, -67.890, 500.9, 4),
    ("Product_E", 567.890, 325.00, 89.012, 275.6, 5),
    ("Product_F", 890.234, 150.75, -12.345, 425.2, 6),
    ("Product_G", 345.678, 500.50, 34.567, 180.7, 7),
    ("Product_H", 678.901, 275.25, -45.678, 600.1, 8),
    ("Product_I", 901.234, 380.00, 78.901, 320.4, 9),
    ("Product_J", 123.789, 225.75, -89.123, 450.8, 10)
]

schema = StructType([
    StructField("product_name", StringType(), True),
    StructField("price", DoubleType(), True),
    StructField("cost", DoubleType(), True),
    StructField("profit_margin", DoubleType(), True),
    StructField("revenue", DoubleType(), True),
    StructField("id", IntegerType(), True)
])

df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)

print("=" * 80)
print("ORIGINAL DATASET")
print("=" * 80)
df.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: ROUNDING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 1: ROUNDING PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Round numeric values to specified decimal places")

# Different rounding strategies
df_rounded = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Round to 2 decimal places
    F.round("price", 2).alias("price_round_2"),
    # Round to 1 decimal place
    F.round("price", 1).alias("price_round_1"),
    # Round to nearest integer
    F.round("price", 0).alias("price_round_0"),
    # Round using bround (banker's rounding - rounds to nearest even)
    F.bround("price", 2).alias("price_bround_2"),
    # Custom rounding to nearest 5
    (F.round(F.col("price") / 5) * 5).alias("price_round_to_5"),
    # Custom rounding to nearest 10
    (F.round(F.col("price") / 10) * 10).alias("price_round_to_10")
)

df_rounded.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 2: CEILING/FLOOR PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 2: CEILING/FLOOR PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Apply ceiling (round up) or floor (round down) operations")

df_ceil_floor = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "profit_margin",
    # Ceiling - round up to nearest integer
    F.ceil("price").alias("price_ceiling"),
    # Floor - round down to nearest integer
    F.floor("price").alias("price_floor"),
    # Ceiling for negative numbers
    F.ceil("profit_margin").alias("margin_ceiling"),
    # Floor for negative numbers
    F.floor("profit_margin").alias("margin_floor"),
    # Custom ceiling to nearest 100
    (F.ceil(F.col("price") / 100) * 100).alias("price_ceil_100"),
    # Custom floor to nearest 50
    (F.floor(F.col("price") / 50) * 50).alias("price_floor_50")
)

df_ceil_floor.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 3: ABSOLUTE VALUE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 3: ABSOLUTE VALUE PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Convert negative values to positive (magnitude)")

df_absolute = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "profit_margin",
    # Absolute value
    F.abs("profit_margin").alias("abs_profit_margin"),
    # Conditional absolute value (only for negative values)
    F.when(F.col("profit_margin") < 0, F.abs("profit_margin"))
        .otherwise(F.col("profit_margin"))
        .alias("conditional_abs"),
    # Sign function (-1, 0, or 1)
    F.signum("profit_margin").alias("profit_sign"),
    # Distance from zero
    F.abs("profit_margin").alias("distance_from_zero"),
    # Preserve sign separately
    F.struct(
        F.abs("profit_margin").alias("magnitude"),
        F.signum("profit_margin").alias("sign")
    ).alias("separated_sign_magnitude")
)

df_absolute.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: MATHEMATICAL OPERATION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 4: MATHEMATICAL OPERATION PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Perform various mathematical operations")

df_math = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "cost",
    # Basic arithmetic
    (F.col("price") + F.col("cost")).alias("sum"),
    (F.col("price") - F.col("cost")).alias("difference"),
    (F.col("price") * F.col("cost")).alias("product"),
    (F.col("price") / F.col("cost")).alias("division"),
    # Modulo operation
    (F.col("price") % 100).alias("modulo_100"),
    # Power operations
    F.pow("price", 2).alias("price_squared"),
    F.sqrt("price").alias("price_sqrt"),
    # Exponential and logarithmic
    F.exp(F.col("price") / 1000).alias("exp_scaled"),
    F.log("price").alias("natural_log"),
    F.log10("price").alias("log_base_10"),
    # Trigonometric (using radians)
    F.sin(F.col("price") / 100).alias("sin_scaled"),
    F.cos(F.col("price") / 100).alias("cos_scaled")
)

df_math.show(truncate=False)

# Advanced mathematical operations
df_math_advanced = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "cost",
    # Percentage calculations
    ((F.col("price") - F.col("cost")) / F.col("cost") * 100).alias("markup_percentage"),
    # Compound interest formula: A = P(1 + r)^t
    (F.col("price") * F.pow(1.05, 3)).alias("compound_growth_3yr"),
    # Geometric mean (sqrt of product)
    F.sqrt(F.col("price") * F.col("cost")).alias("geometric_mean"),
    # Harmonic mean: 2 / (1/a + 1/b)
    (2 / ((1 / F.col("price")) + (1 / F.col("cost")))).alias("harmonic_mean")
)

print("\nAdvanced Mathematical Operations:")
df_math_advanced.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: STATISTICAL FUNCTION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 5: STATISTICAL FUNCTION PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Calculate statistical metrics on numeric columns")

# Aggregate statistics
print("\nAggregate Statistics:")
df_stats = df.agg(
    # Central tendency
    F.mean("price").alias("mean_price"),
    F.median("price").alias("median_price"),
    F.mode("price").alias("mode_price"),
    
    # Dispersion
    F.stddev("price").alias("stddev_price"),
    F.variance("price").alias("variance_price"),
    F.min("price").alias("min_price"),
    F.max("price").alias("max_price"),
    
    # Range
    (F.max("price") - F.min("price")).alias("range_price"),
    
    # Percentiles
    F.expr("percentile(price, 0.25)").alias("q1_price"),
    F.expr("percentile(price, 0.50)").alias("q2_price"),
    F.expr("percentile(price, 0.75)").alias("q3_price"),
    
    # Count statistics
    F.count("price").alias("count"),
    F.sum("price").alias("sum_price"),
    
    # Coefficient of variation (CV = stddev/mean)
    (F.stddev("price") / F.mean("price") * 100).alias("cv_percentage")
)

df_stats.show(truncate=False)

# Window-based statistics (rolling calculations)
print("\nWindow-based Statistics (Rolling):")
window_spec = Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(-2, 0)  # Current + 2 previous rows

df_window_stats = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Rolling average
    F.avg("price").over(window_spec).alias("rolling_avg_3"),
    # Rolling sum
    F.sum("price").over(window_spec).alias("rolling_sum_3"),
    # Rolling min/max
    F.min("price").over(window_spec).alias("rolling_min_3"),
    F.max("price").over(window_spec).alias("rolling_max_3"),
    # Rolling standard deviation
    F.stddev("price").over(window_spec).alias("rolling_stddev_3"),
    # Cumulative sum
    F.sum("price").over(Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0))
        .alias("cumulative_sum")
)

df_window_stats.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 6: BINNING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 6: BINNING PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Group continuous values into discrete bins/categories")

# Method 1: Manual binning with when/otherwise
df_binning_manual = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Price categories
    F.when(F.col("price") < 200, "Low")
        .when((F.col("price") >= 200) & (F.col("price") < 500), "Medium")
        .when((F.col("price") >= 500) & (F.col("price") < 800), "High")
        .otherwise("Very High")
        .alias("price_category"),
    
    # Revenue tiers
    F.when(F.col("revenue") < 200, "Tier 1")
        .when((F.col("revenue") >= 200) & (F.col("revenue") < 400), "Tier 2")
        .when(F.col("revenue") >= 400, "Tier 3")
        .alias("revenue_tier")
)

df_binning_manual.show(truncate=False)

# Method 2: Equal-width binning using ntile
print("\nEqual-frequency binning (Quantile-based):")
df_binning_ntile = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Divide into 4 equal-frequency bins (quartiles)
    F.ntile(4).over(Window.orderBy("price")).alias("price_quartile"),
    # Divide into 10 equal-frequency bins (deciles)
    F.ntile(10).over(Window.orderBy("price")).alias("price_decile"),
    # Divide into 5 equal-frequency bins (quintiles)
    F.ntile(5).over(Window.orderBy("revenue")).alias("revenue_quintile")
)

df_binning_ntile.show(truncate=False)

# Method 3: Custom binning with bucketizer-like logic
print("\nCustom interval binning:")
df_binning_custom = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Custom bin edges
    F.when(F.col("price") < 250, "0-250")
        .when((F.col("price") >= 250) & (F.col("price") < 500), "250-500")
        .when((F.col("price") >= 500) & (F.col("price") < 750), "500-750")
        .otherwise("750+")
        .alias("price_bin"),
    
    # Bin number (ordinal)
    F.when(F.col("price") < 250, 1)
        .when((F.col("price") >= 250) & (F.col("price") < 500), 2)
        .when((F.col("price") >= 500) & (F.col("price") < 750), 3)
        .otherwise(4)
        .alias("bin_number")
)

df_binning_custom.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 7: NORMALIZATION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 7: NORMALIZATION PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Scale values to a specific range (typically 0-1)")

# Calculate min and max for normalization
stats = df.select(
    F.min("price").alias("min_price"),
    F.max("price").alias("max_price"),
    F.min("revenue").alias("min_revenue"),
    F.max("revenue").alias("max_revenue")
).collect()[0]

min_price = stats["min_price"]
max_price = stats["max_price"]
min_revenue = stats["min_revenue"]
max_revenue = stats["max_revenue"]

# Min-Max Normalization (0-1 range)
df_normalized = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "revenue",
    # Min-Max normalization: (x - min) / (max - min)
    ((F.col("price") - min_price) / (max_price - min_price))
        .alias("price_normalized_0_1"),
    
    ((F.col("revenue") - min_revenue) / (max_revenue - min_revenue))
        .alias("revenue_normalized_0_1"),
    
    # Min-Max normalization to custom range (-1 to 1)
    (2 * ((F.col("price") - min_price) / (max_price - min_price)) - 1)
        .alias("price_normalized_neg1_
```python
1"),
    
    # Min-Max normalization to custom range (0 to 100)
    (100 * ((F.col("price") - min_price) / (max_price - min_price)))
        .alias("price_normalized_0_100"),
    
    # Max absolute scaling (divide by max absolute value)
    (F.col("price") / max_price).alias("price_max_abs_scaled"),
    
    # Robust scaling using percentiles (less sensitive to outliers)
    # Using median and IQR approximation
    ((F.col("price") - F.lit((min_price + max_price) / 2)) / 
     F.lit((max_price - min_price) / 2))
        .alias("price_robust_scaled")
)

df_normalized.show(truncate=False)

# Alternative normalization with window functions
print("\nNormalization using window functions:")
window_all = Window.partitionBy()

df_normalized_window = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Min-Max normalization using window functions
    ((F.col("price") - F.min("price").over(window_all)) / 
     (F.max("price").over(window_all) - F.min("price").over(window_all)))
        .alias("price_minmax_normalized"),
    
    # Decimal scaling (divide by 10^d where d is number of digits)
    (F.col("price") / F.pow(10, F.ceil(F.log10(F.max("price").over(window_all)))))
        .alias("price_decimal_scaled")
)

df_normalized_window.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 8: STANDARDIZATION PATTERN (Z-SCORE)
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 8: STANDARDIZATION PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Transform data to have mean=0 and standard deviation=1")

# Calculate mean and standard deviation
stats_std = df.select(
    F.mean("price").alias("mean_price"),
    F.stddev("price").alias("stddev_price"),
    F.mean("revenue").alias("mean_revenue"),
    F.stddev("revenue").alias("stddev_revenue"),
    F.mean("cost").alias("mean_cost"),
    F.stddev("cost").alias("stddev_cost")
).collect()[0]

mean_price = stats_std["mean_price"]
stddev_price = stats_std["stddev_price"]
mean_revenue = stats_std["mean_revenue"]
stddev_revenue = stats_std["stddev_revenue"]
mean_cost = stats_std["mean_cost"]
stddev_cost = stats_std["stddev_cost"]

# Z-Score Standardization
df_standardized = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "revenue",
    "cost",
    # Z-score: (x - mean) / stddev
    ((F.col("price") - mean_price) / stddev_price).alias("price_zscore"),
    ((F.col("revenue") - mean_revenue) / stddev_revenue).alias("revenue_zscore"),
    ((F.col("cost") - mean_cost) / stddev_cost).alias("cost_zscore"),
    
    # Modified Z-score using median and MAD (Median Absolute Deviation)
    # More robust to outliers
    ((F.col("price") - F.lit((min_price + max_price) / 2)) / 
     F.lit(stddev_price)).alias("price_modified_zscore")
)

df_standardized.show(truncate=False)

# Standardization using window functions
print("\nStandardization using window functions:")
df_standardized_window = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "revenue",
    # Z-score using window functions
    ((F.col("price") - F.mean("price").over(window_all)) / 
     F.stddev("price").over(window_all)).alias("price_zscore_window"),
    
    ((F.col("revenue") - F.mean("revenue").over(window_all)) / 
     F.stddev("revenue").over(window_all)).alias("revenue_zscore_window"),
    
    # Unit variance scaling (divide by stddev only)
    (F.col("price") / F.stddev("price").over(window_all))
        .alias("price_unit_variance")
)

df_standardized_window.show(truncate=False)

# Verify standardization (mean should be ~0, stddev should be ~1)
print("\nVerification of standardization:")
df_standardized.select(
    F.round(F.mean("price_zscore"), 6).alias("mean_zscore"),
    F.round(F.stddev("price_zscore"), 6).alias("stddev_zscore"),
    F.min("price_zscore").alias("min_zscore"),
    F.max("price_zscore").alias("max_zscore")
).show()

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 9: OUTLIER TREATMENT PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 9: OUTLIER TREATMENT PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Purpose: Detect and handle outliers in numeric data")

# Calculate IQR (Interquartile Range) for outlier detection
percentiles = df.select(
    F.expr("percentile(price, 0.25)").alias("q1"),
    F.expr("percentile(price, 0.75)").alias("q3"),
    F.mean("price").alias("mean"),
    F.stddev("price").alias("stddev")
).collect()[0]

q1 = percentiles["q1"]
q3 = percentiles["q3"]
iqr = q3 - q1
mean_val = percentiles["mean"]
stddev_val = percentiles["stddev"]

# Outlier bounds
lower_bound_iqr = q1 - 1.5 * iqr
upper_bound_iqr = q3 + 1.5 * iqr
lower_bound_zscore = mean_val - 3 * stddev_val
upper_bound_zscore = mean_val + 3 * stddev_val

print(f"\nOutlier Detection Thresholds:")
print(f"IQR Method: [{lower_bound_iqr:.2f}, {upper_bound_iqr:.2f}]")
print(f"Z-Score Method (±3σ): [{lower_bound_zscore:.2f}, {upper_bound_zscore:.2f}]")

# Method 1: Outlier Detection
df_outlier_detection = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # IQR-based outlier flag
    F.when((F.col("price") < lower_bound_iqr) | (F.col("price") > upper_bound_iqr), 
           "Outlier").otherwise("Normal").alias("iqr_outlier_flag"),
    
    # Z-score based outlier flag (|z| > 3)
    F.when(F.abs((F.col("price") - mean_val) / stddev_val) > 3, 
           "Outlier").otherwise("Normal").alias("zscore_outlier_flag"),
    
    # Percentile-based outlier (outside 5th and 95th percentile)
    F.when((F.col("price") < F.expr("percentile(price, 0.05)").over(window_all)) | 
           (F.col("price") > F.expr("percentile(price, 0.95)").over(window_all)), 
           "Outlier").otherwise("Normal").alias("percentile_outlier_flag")
)

print("\nOutlier Detection:")
df_outlier_detection.show(truncate=False)

# Method 2: Outlier Treatment - Capping/Winsorization
df_outlier_capping = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Cap outliers at IQR bounds
    F.when(F.col("price") < lower_bound_iqr, lower_bound_iqr)
        .when(F.col("price") > upper_bound_iqr, upper_bound_iqr)
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("price_iqr_capped"),
    
    # Winsorization at 5th and 95th percentile
    F.when(F.col("price") < F.expr("percentile(price, 0.05)").over(window_all),
           F.expr("percentile(price, 0.05)").over(window_all))
        .when(F.col("price") > F.expr("percentile(price, 0.95)").over(window_all),
              F.expr("percentile(price, 0.95)").over(window_all))
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("price_winsorized"),
    
    # Cap at mean ± 3 standard deviations
    F.when(F.col("price") < lower_bound_zscore, lower_bound_zscore)
        .when(F.col("price") > upper_bound_zscore, upper_bound_zscore)
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("price_zscore_capped")
)

print("\nOutlier Treatment - Capping:")
df_outlier_capping.show(truncate=False)

# Method 3: Outlier Treatment - Removal
df_outlier_removal = df.filter(
    (F.col("price") >= lower_bound_iqr) & (F.col("price") <= upper_bound_iqr)
).select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    F.lit("IQR Filter Applied").alias("filter_method")
)

print("\nOutlier Treatment - Removal (IQR method):")
print(f"Original count: {df.count()}, After removal: {df_outlier_removal.count()}")
df_outlier_removal.show(truncate=False)

# Method 4: Outlier Treatment - Transformation
df_outlier_transform = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Log transformation (reduces impact of outliers)
    F.log(F.col("price")).alias("price_log"),
    
    # Square root transformation
    F.sqrt(F.col("price")).alias("price_sqrt"),
    
    # Cube root transformation (handles negative values)
    F.pow(F.col("price"), 1/3).alias("price_cbrt"),
    
    # Box-Cox like transformation (log(1 + x))
    F.log1p(F.col("price")).alias("price_log1p"),
    
    # Reciprocal transformation
    (1 / F.col("price")).alias("price_reciprocal")
)

print("\nOutlier Treatment - Transformation:")
df_outlier_transform.show(truncate=False)

# Method 5: Outlier Treatment - Imputation
df_outlier_imputation = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Replace outliers with mean
    F.when((F.col("price") < lower_bound_iqr) | (F.col("price") > upper_bound_iqr),
           mean_val)
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("price_outlier_to_mean"),
    
    # Replace outliers with median
    F.when((F.col("price") < lower_bound_iqr) | (F.col("price") > upper_bound_iqr),
           F.lit((q1 + q3) / 2))
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("price_outlier_to_median"),
    
    # Replace outliers with nearest bound
    F.when(F.col("price") < lower_bound_iqr, lower_bound_iqr)
        .when(F.col("price") > upper_bound_iqr, upper_bound_iqr)
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("price_outlier_to_bound")
)

print("\nOutlier Treatment - Imputation:")
df_outlier_imputation.show(truncate=False)

# Method 6: Advanced Outlier Detection - Modified Z-Score (MAD-based)
median_price = (q1 + q3) / 2  # Approximation
mad = df.select(F.mean(F.abs(F.col("price") - median_price))).collect()[0][0]

df_outlier_mad = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    # Modified Z-score using MAD
    (0.6745 * (F.col("price") - median_price) / mad).alias("modified_zscore"),
    
    # Flag outliers (|modified z-score| > 3.5)
    F.when(F.abs(0.6745 * (F.col("price") - median_price) / mad) > 3.5,
           "Outlier").otherwise("Normal").alias("mad_outlier_flag")
)

print("\nAdvanced Outlier Detection - MAD-based:")
df_outlier_mad.show(truncate=False)

# COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLE: COMBINING ALL PATTERNS

print("\n" + "=" * 80)

df_comprehensive = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "cost",
    "profit_margin",
    "revenue"
).withColumn(
    # Step 1: Handle outliers (cap at IQR bounds)
    "price_clean",
    F.when(F.col("price") < lower_bound_iqr, lower_bound_iqr)

        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
).withColumn(
    # Step 2: Round to 2 decimal places
    "price_rounded",
    F.round("price_clean", 2)
).withColumn(
    # Step 3: Normalize to 0-1 range

    (F.col("price_rounded") - F.min("price_rounded").over(window_all)) /
    (F.max("price_rounded").over(window_all) - F.min("price_rounded").over(window_all))
).withColumn(
    # Step 4: Standardize (z-score)
    "price_standardized",
    (F.col("price_rounded") - F.mean("price_rounded").over(window_all)) /
    F.stddev("price_rounded").over(window_all)
).withColumn(
    # Step 5: Create bins
    "price_category",
    F.when(F.col("price_normalized") < 0.33, "Low")
        .when((F.col("price_normalized") >= 0.33) & (F.col("price_normalized") < 0.67), "Medium")
        .otherwise("High")
).withColumn(
    # Step 6: Apply mathematical transformation
    "price_log",
    F.log(F.col("price_rounded"))
).withColumn(
    # Step 7: Calculate absolute value of profit margin
    "profit_margin_abs",
    F.abs("profit_margin")
).withColumn(
    # Step 8: Apply ceiling to revenue
    "revenue_ceiling",
    F.ceil("revenue")
).withColumn(
    # Step 9: Calculate
```python
    # Step 9: Calculate statistical measures
    "price_percentile_rank",
    F.percent_rank().over(Window.orderBy("price"))
).withColumn(
    # Step 10: Rolling average
    "price_rolling_avg",
    F.avg("price_rounded").over(Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(-1, 1))
)

print("\nComprehensive Data Preprocessing Pipeline:")
df_comprehensive.show(truncate=False)

# Use Case 1: Financial Data Processing
print("\nUse Case 1: Financial Data Processing")
df_financial = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "cost",
    "revenue",
    # Round currency to 2 decimal places
    F.round("price", 2).alias("price_currency"),
    # Calculate profit
    (F.col("price") - F.col("cost")).alias("profit"),
    # Calculate profit margin percentage
    F.round(((F.col("price") - F.col("cost")) / F.col("cost") * 100), 2)
        .alias("profit_margin_pct"),
    # Normalize revenue for comparison
    ((F.col("revenue") - F.min("revenue").over(window_all)) /
     (F.max("revenue").over(window_all) - F.min("revenue").over(window_all)))
        .alias("revenue_score"),
    # Categorize by profit margin
    F.when(((F.col("price") - F.col("cost")) / F.col("cost") * 100) < 10, "Low Margin")
        .when(((F.col("price") - F.col("cost")) / F.col("cost") * 100) < 30, "Medium Margin")
        .otherwise("High Margin")
        .alias("margin_category")
)

df_financial.show(truncate=False)

# Use Case 2: Scoring and Ranking System
print("\nUse Case 2: Product Scoring and Ranking System")
df_scoring = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "revenue",
    "cost"
).withColumn(
    # Normalize price (lower is better, so invert)
    "price_score",
    1 - ((F.col("price") - F.min("price").over(window_all)) /
         (F.max("price").over(window_all) - F.min("price").over(window_all)))
).withColumn(
    # Normalize revenue (higher is better)
    "revenue_score",
    (F.col("revenue") - F.min("revenue").over(window_all)) /
    (F.max("revenue").over(window_all) - F.min("revenue").over(window_all))
).withColumn(
    # Calculate efficiency score
    "efficiency_score",
    F.col("revenue") / F.col("cost")
).withColumn(
    # Normalize efficiency score
    "efficiency_normalized",
    (F.col("efficiency_score") - F.min("efficiency_score").over(window_all)) /
    (F.max("efficiency_score").over(window_all) - F.min("efficiency_score").over(window_all))
).withColumn(
    # Composite score (weighted average)
    "composite_score",
    F.round(
        (F.col("price_score") * 0.3 +
         F.col("revenue_score") * 0.4 +
         F.col("efficiency_normalized") * 0.3) * 100,
        2
    )
).withColumn(
    # Rank products
    "rank",
    F.rank().over(Window.orderBy(F.desc("composite_score")))
).withColumn(
    # Assign grade
    "grade",
    F.when(F.col("composite_score") >= 80, "A")
        .when(F.col("composite_score") >= 60, "B")
        .when(F.col("composite_score") >= 40, "C")
        .when(F.col("composite_score") >= 20, "D")
        .otherwise("F")
)

df_scoring.orderBy("rank").show(truncate=False)

# Use Case 3: Time Series Analysis with Statistical Patterns
print("\nUse Case 3: Time Series Statistical Analysis")
df_timeseries = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "id",
    "price"
).withColumn(
    # Moving average (3-period)
    "ma_3",
    F.round(F.avg("price").over(
        Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    ), 2)
).withColumn(
    # Exponential moving average approximation
    "ema_approx",
    F.round(F.avg("price").over(
        Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    ) * 0.5 + F.col("price") * 0.5, 2)
).withColumn(
    # Price change
    "price_change",
    F.col("price") - F.lag("price", 1).over(Window.orderBy("id"))
).withColumn(
    # Price change percentage
    "price_change_pct",
    F.round(
        ((F.col("price") - F.lag("price", 1).over(Window.orderBy("id"))) /
         F.lag("price", 1).over(Window.orderBy("id")) * 100),
        2
    )
).withColumn(
    # Cumulative sum
    "cumulative_price",
    F.sum("price").over(Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0))
).withColumn(
    # Rolling standard deviation
    "rolling_std",
    F.round(F.stddev("price").over(
        Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    ), 2)
).withColumn(
    # Volatility indicator (CV)
    "volatility",
    F.round(
        (F.stddev("price").over(Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(-2, 0)) /
         F.avg("price").over(Window.orderBy("id").rowsBetween(-2, 0)) * 100),
        2
    )
)

df_timeseries.show(truncate=False)

# Use Case 4: Quality Control with Outlier Detection
print("\nUse Case 4: Quality Control System")
df_quality = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "cost"
).withColumn(
    # Calculate z-score
    "price_zscore",
    (F.col("price") - F.mean("price").over(window_all)) /
    F.stddev("price").over(window_all)
).withColumn(
    # Quality flag based on z-score
    "quality_flag",
    F.when(F.abs(F.col("price_zscore")) > 2, "Review Required")
        .when(F.abs(F.col("price_zscore")) > 1, "Monitor")
        .otherwise("Normal")
).withColumn(
    # Control limits (mean ± 3 sigma)
    "upper_control_limit",
    F.mean("price").over(window_all) + 3 * F.stddev("price").over(window_all)
).withColumn(
    "lower_control_limit",
    F.mean("price").over(window_all) - 3 * F.stddev("price").over(window_all)
).withColumn(
    # Out of control flag
    "out_of_control",
    F.when(
        (F.col("price") > F.col("upper_control_limit")) |
        (F.col("price") < F.col("lower_control_limit")),
        "YES"
    ).otherwise("NO")
).withColumn(
    # Distance from mean in standard deviations
    "sigma_distance",
    F.round(F.abs(F.col("price_zscore")), 2)
)

df_quality.show(truncate=False)

# Use Case 5: Data Binning for Machine Learning
print("\nUse Case 5: Feature Engineering for ML")
df_ml_features = df.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "cost",
    "revenue"
).withColumn(
    # Create price bins for categorical features
    "price_bin",
    F.ntile(5).over(Window.orderBy("price"))
).withColumn(
    # One-hot encoding preparation
    "is_high_price",
    F.when(F.col("price") > F.expr("percentile(price, 0.75)").over(window_all), 1)
        .otherwise(0)
).withColumn(
    "is_low_price",
    F.when(F.col("price") < F.expr("percentile(price, 0.25)").over(window_all), 1)
        .otherwise(0)
).withColumn(
    # Polynomial features
    "price_squared",
    F.pow("price", 2)
).withColumn(
    "price_cubed",
    F.pow("price", 3)
).withColumn(
    # Interaction features
    "price_cost_interaction",
    F.col("price") * F.col("cost")
).withColumn(
    # Log transformation for skewed data
    "price_log",
    F.log("price")
).withColumn(
    "revenue_log",
    F.log("revenue")
).withColumn(
    # Standardized features
    "price_standardized",
    (F.col("price") - F.mean("price").over(window_all)) /
    F.stddev("price").over(window_all)
).withColumn(
    # Ratio features
    "price_to_cost_ratio",
    F.col("price") / F.col("cost")
).withColumn(
    # Binned ratio
    "efficiency_category",
    F.when(F.col("price_to_cost_ratio") < 1.5, "Low")
        .when((F.col("price_to_cost_ratio") >= 1.5) & (F.col("price_to_cost_ratio") < 2.5), "Medium")
        .otherwise("High")
)

df_ml_features.show(truncate=False)

df_test1.count()

# Test 2: Normalization
start = time.time()
stats_perf = df_large.select(
    F.min("price").alias("min_p"),
    F.max("price").alias("max_p")
).collect()[0]
df_test2 = df_large.select(
    ((F.col("price") - stats_perf["min_p"]) /

best_practices = """
1. ROUNDING PATTERN:
   - Use round() for financial calculations
   - Use bround() for statistical calculations (banker's rounding)
   - Always specify decimal places explicitly
   - Be aware of floating-point precision issues

2. CEILING/FLOOR PATTERN:
   - Use for inventory calculations (can't have partial units)
   - Useful for pagination and batch processing
   - Consider business rules (round up for safety margins)

3. ABSOLUTE VALUE PATTERN:
   - Essential for distance calculations
   - Use with profit/loss analysis
   - Helpful for error magnitude calculations

4. MATHEMATICAL OPERATIONS:
   - Cache intermediate results for complex calculations
   - Use built-in functions (faster than UDFs)
   - Handle division by zero explicitly
   - Consider numerical stability for large computations

5. STATISTICAL FUNCTIONS:
   - Use window functions for rolling statistics
   - Cache data when calculating multiple statistics
   - Consider approximate functions for large datasets
   - Use appropriate aggregation levels

6. BINNING PATTERN:
   - Choose bin count based on data distribution
   - Use ntile() for equal-frequency bins
   - Use when/otherwise for equal-width bins
   - Consider business meaning of bins

7. NORMALIZATION PATTERN:
   - Use for features with different scales
   - Min-Max for bounded ranges (0-1)
   - Robust scaling for data with outliers
   - Document the scaling parameters

8. STANDARDIZATION PATTERN:
   - Use for normally distributed data
   - Essential for many ML algorithms
   - Preserve mean and stddev for inverse transform
   - Handle zero variance columns

9. OUTLIER TREATMENT:
   - Always investigate outliers before removing
   - Use multiple detection methods
   - Document outlier handling decisions
```python
   - Document outlier handling decisions
   - Consider domain knowledge
   - Use robust methods (IQR, MAD) for skewed data
   - Keep original values for audit trail

PERFORMANCE TIPS:
   - Cache DataFrames used multiple times
   - Use broadcast variables for lookup tables
   - Minimize shuffles with proper partitioning
   - Use approximation functions for large datasets
   - Combine multiple operations in single select()
   - Use window functions efficiently (same partition/order)
"""

# Create dataset with edge cases
edge_case_data = [
    ("Edge_1", 0.0, 100.0, 0.0, 200.0, 1),
    ("Edge_2", None, 200.0, None, 300.0, 2),
    ("Edge_3", float('inf'), 150.0, 50.0, 400.0, 3),
    ("Edge_4", -100.0, 175.0, -25.0, 150.0, 4),
    ("Edge_5", 0.00001, 225.0, 0.00001, 250.0, 5),
    ("Edge_6", 999999.99, 125.0, 75.0, 500.0, 6),
]

df_edge = spark.createDataFrame(edge_case_data, schema)

print("\nEdge Case Dataset:")
df_edge.show(truncate=False)

# Handle edge cases
print("\nHandling Edge Cases:")
df_edge_handled = df_edge.select(
    "product_name",
    "price",
    "cost",
    # Handle null values
    F.coalesce("price", F.lit(0.0)).alias("price_no_null"),
    
    # Handle infinite values
    F.when(F.col("price").isNull(), F.lit(0.0))
        .when(F.col("price") == float('inf'), F.lit(999999.99))
        .when(F.col("price") == float('-inf'), F.lit(0.0))
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("price_no_inf"),
    
    # Handle division by zero
    F.when(F.col("cost") == 0, F.lit(None))
        .otherwise(F.col("price") / F.col("cost"))
        .alias("safe_division"),
    
    # Handle very small numbers
    F.when(F.abs(F.col("price")) < 0.01, F.round(F.col("price"), 4))
        .otherwise(F.round(F.col("price"), 2))
        .alias("adaptive_rounding"),
    
    # Handle negative values in log
    F.when(F.col("price") > 0, F.log(F.col("price")))
        .otherwise(F.lit(None))
        .alias("safe_log"),
    
    # Handle negative values in sqrt
    F.when(F.col("profit_margin") >= 0, F.sqrt(F.col("profit_margin")))
        .otherwise(F.lit(None))
        .alias("safe_sqrt"),
    
    # Clamp values to valid range
    F.when(F.col("price") < 0, F.lit(0.0))
        .when(F.col("price") > 10000, F.lit(10000.0))
        .otherwise(F.col("price"))
        .alias("clamped_price")
)

df_edge_handled.show(truncate=False)
