# 7. PARTITION COMPACTION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Compact small files within partitions for better performance

class PartitionCompactionPattern:
    """
    Handles compacting small files within partitions.
    Useful for reducing file count and improving read performance.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
    
    def compact_partition(self, source_path, target_path, 
                         target_file_size_mb=128):
        """
        Compact small files into larger files
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            target_file_size_mb: Target file size in MB
        """
        print(f"\n=== Partition Compaction Pattern ===")
        print(f"Target file size: {target_file_size_mb} MB")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Calculate optimal number of partitions based on data size
        total_records = df.count()
        
        # Estimate records per file (adjust based on your data)
        estimated_record_size_kb = 1  # 1 KB per record (adjust as needed)
        records_per_file = (target_file_size_mb * 1024) // estimated_record_size_kb
        
        optimal_partitions = max(1, total_records // records_per_file)
        
        print(f"Total records: {total_records}")
        print(f"Optimal partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
        
        # Repartition and write
        compacted_df = df.repartition(int(optimal_partitions), "date", "country")
        
        compacted_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date", "country") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .option("maxRecordsPerFile", records_per_file) \
            .parquet(target_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Partitions compacted successfully")
    
    def compact_with_coalesce(self, source_path, target_path, files_per_partition=1):
        """
        Compact using coalesce to reduce file count
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            files_per_partition: Target number of files per partition
        """
        print(f"\n=== Compaction with Coalesce ===")
        print(f"Target files per partition: {files_per_partition}")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Get unique partitions
        partitions = df.select("date", "country").distinct().collect()
        
        print(f"Processing {len(partitions)} partitions")
        
        # Process each partition separately for better control
        for partition in partitions:
            date_val = partition["date"]
            country_val = partition["country"]
            
            partition_df = df.filter(
                (col("date") == date_val
```python
) & 
                (col("country") == country_val)
            )
            
            # Coalesce to target file count
            compacted_partition = partition_df.coalesce(files_per_partition)
            
            # Write this partition
            compacted_partition.write \
                .partitionBy("date", "country") \
                .mode("append") \
                .parquet(target_path)
            
            print(f"✓ Compacted partition: date={date_val}, country={country_val}")
        
        print(f"✓ All partitions compacted")
    
    def optimize_file_sizes(self, source_path, target_path, 
                           min_file_size_mb=64, max_file_size_mb=256):
        """
        Optimize file sizes within acceptable range
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            min_file_size_mb: Minimum file size in MB
            max_file_size_mb: Maximum file size in MB
        """
        print(f"\n=== Optimizing File Sizes ===")
        print(f"Target range: {min_file_size_mb}MB - {max_file_size_mb}MB")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Use adaptive query execution for automatic optimization
        optimized_df = df.repartition("date", "country")
        
        # Write with file size constraints
        optimized_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date", "country") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .option("maxRecordsPerFile", 100000) \
            .parquet(target_path)
        
        print(f"✓ File sizes optimized")
    
    def compact_with_z_ordering(self, source_path, target_path, z_order_cols):
        """
        Compact with Z-ordering for better query performance
        Note: Requires Delta Lake or similar format
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            z_order_cols: Columns to use for Z-ordering
        """
        print(f"\n=== Compaction with Z-Ordering ===")
        print(f"Z-order columns: {z_order_cols}")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Sort by Z-order columns for better data locality
        sorted_df = df.sortWithinPartitions(*z_order_cols)
        
        # Compact and write
        sorted_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date", "country") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(target_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Data compacted with Z-ordering")


# ============================================================================
# 8. PARTITION REBALANCING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Rebalance data across partitions for even distribution

class PartitionRebalancingPattern:
    """
    Handles rebalancing data across partitions.
    Useful for handling skewed data and improving parallelism.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
    
    def detect_skew(self, table_path, partition_cols):
        """
        Detect partition skew
        
        Args:
            table_path: Table path
            partition_cols: Partition columns to analyze
        """
        print(f"\n=== Detecting Partition Skew ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Analyze partition distribution
        partition_stats = df.groupBy(*partition_cols) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                sum("sales").alias("total_sales")
            ) \
            .orderBy(col("record_count").desc())
        
        print("Partition distribution:")
        partition_stats.show()
        
        # Calculate skew metrics
        stats_df = partition_stats.select("record_count")
        
        avg_records = stats_df.agg(avg("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        max_records = stats_df.agg(max("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        min_records = stats_df.agg(min("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        
        skew_ratio = max_records / avg_records if avg_records > 0 else 0
        
        print(f"\nSkew Analysis:")
        print(f"Average records per partition: {avg_records:.2f}")
        print(f"Max records: {max_records}")
        print(f"Min records: {min_records}")
        print(f"Skew ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
        
        if skew_ratio > 2.0:
            print("⚠ Significant skew detected - rebalancing recommended")
        else:
            print("✓ Partitions are relatively balanced")
        
        return skew_ratio
    
    def rebalance_with_salting(self, source_path, target_path, 
                              skewed_col, salt_range=10):
        """
        Rebalance using salting technique
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            skewed_col: Column with skewed distribution
            salt_range: Number of salt values to use
        """
        print(f"\n=== Rebalancing with Salting ===")
        print(f"Salting column '{skewed_col}' with range {salt_range}")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Add salt to skewed column
        salted_df = df.withColumn(
            "salt",
            (rand() * salt_range).cast("int").cast("string")
        ).withColumn(
            f"{skewed_col}_salted",
            concat(col(skewed_col), lit("_"), col("salt"))
        )
        
        # Write with salted partition
        salted_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date", f"{skewed_col}_salted") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(target_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Data rebalanced with salting")
        
        # Verify distribution
        result_df = self.spark.read.parquet(target_path)
        new_dist = result_df.groupBy("date", f"{skewed_col}_salted") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("record_count")) \
            .orderBy(col("record_count").desc())
        
        print("New distribution (top 10):")
        new_dist.show(10)
    
    def rebalance_with_repartition(self, source_path, target_path, 
                                   num_partitions=None):
        """
        Rebalance using repartition
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            num_partitions: Target number of partitions (None for auto)
        """
        print(f"\n=== Rebalancing with Repartition ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        original_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        print(f"Original partitions: {original_partitions}")
        
        # Repartition for even distribution
        if num_partitions:
            rebalanced_df = df.repartition(num_partitions, "date", "country")
            print(f"Target partitions: {num_partitions}")
        else:
            rebalanced_df = df.repartition("date", "country")
            print(f"Auto-determined partitions: {rebalanced_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        # Write rebalanced data
        rebalanced_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date", "country") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(target_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Data rebalanced successfully")
    
    def adaptive_rebalancing(self, source_path, target_path, 
                            target_records_per_partition=1000):
        """
        Adaptive rebalancing based on partition size
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            target_records_per_partition: Target records per partition
        """
        print(f"\n=== Adaptive Rebalancing ===")
        print(f"Target: {target_records_per_partition} records/partition")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Analyze current distribution
        partition_stats = df.groupBy("date", "country") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("record_count"))
        
        # Identify partitions needing rebalancing
        large_partitions = partition_stats.filter(
            col("record_count") > target_records_per_partition * 1.5
        )
        
        small_partitions = partition_stats.filter(
            col("record_count") < target_records_per_partition * 0.5
        )
        
        print(f"Large partitions: {large_partitions.count()}")
        print(f"Small partitions: {small_partitions.count()}")
        
        # Process large partitions - split them
        large_partition_keys = large_partitions.select("date", "country").collect()
        
        rebalanced_parts = []
        
        for key in large_partition_keys:
            partition_df = df.filter(
                (col("date") == key["date"]) & 
                (col("country") == key["country"])
            )
            
            # Add sub-partition based on row number
            from pyspark.sql.window import Window
            window = Window.partitionBy("date", "country").orderBy("sales")
            
            split_partition = partition_df.withColumn(
                "sub_partition",
                ((row_number().over(window) - 1) / target_records_per_partition)
                .cast("int").cast("string")
            )
            
            rebalanced_parts.append(split_partition)
        
        # Process small partitions - keep as is
        small_partition_keys = small_partitions.select("date", "country").collect()
        
        for key in small_partition_keys:
            partition_df = df.filter(
                (col("date") == key["date"]) & 
                (col("country") == key["country"])
            ).withColumn("sub_partition", lit("0"))
            
            rebalanced_parts.append(partition_df)
        
        # Process normal partitions
        normal_partitions = partition_stats.filter(
            (col("record_count") >= target_records_per_partition * 0.5) &
            (col("record_count") <= target_records_per_partition * 1.5)
        )
        
        normal_partition_keys = normal_partitions.select("date", "country").collect()
        
        for key in normal_partition_keys:
            partition_df = df.filter(
                (col("date") == key["date"]) & 
                (col("country") == key["country"])
            ).withColumn("sub_partition", lit("0"))
            
            rebalanced_parts.append(partition_df)
        
        # Combine all rebalanced partitions
        if rebalanced_parts:
            from functools import reduce
            final_df = reduce(lambda df1, df2: df1.union(df2), rebalanced_parts)
            
            # Write rebalanced data
            final_df.write \
                .partitionBy("date", "country", "sub_partition") \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .parquet(target_path)
            
            print(f"✓ Adaptive rebalancing completed")
            
            # Verify new distribution
            result_df = self.spark.read.parquet(target_path)
            new_stats = result_df.groupBy("date", "country", "sub_partition") \
                .agg(count("*").alias("record_count"))
            
            print("New partition distribution:")
            new_stats.orderBy(col("record_count").desc()).show(10)
    
    def rebalance_by_size(self, source_path, target_path, 
                         target_partition_size_mb=128):
        """
        Rebalance based on target partition size
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
            target_partition_size_mb: Target size per partition in MB
        """
        print(f"\n=== Rebalancing by Size ===")
        print(f"Target partition size: {target_partition_size_mb} MB")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Estimate data size and calculate partitions
        total_records = df.count()
        estimated_record_size_kb = 1  # Adjust based on your data
        total_size_mb = (total_records * estimated_record_size_kb) / 1024
        
        optimal_partitions = max(1, int(total_size_mb / target_partition_size_mb))
        
        print(f"Estimated total size: {total_size_mb:.2f} MB")
        print(f"Optimal partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
        
        # Repartition to target size
        rebalanced_df = df.repartition(optimal_partitions, "date", "country")
        
        # Write with size optimization
        rebalanced_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date", "country") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(target_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Data rebalanced by size")

def cleanup_test_data(base_path):
    """
    Clean up test data directories
    
    Args:
        base_path: Base path to clean
    """
    import shutil
    
    try:
        if os.path.exists(base_path):
            shutil.rmtree(base_path)
            print(f"✓ Cleaned up test data at {base_path}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Error during cleanup: {str(e)}")


def analyze_partition_metrics(table_path):
    """
    Analyze and report partition metrics
    
    Args:
        table_path: Path to partitioned table
    """
    print("\n=== Partition Metrics Analysis ===")
    
    try:
        df = spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Basic metrics
        total_records = df.count()
        total_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        print(f"Total records: {total_records}")
        print(f"Total Spark partitions: {total_partitions}")
        print(f"Avg records per partition: {total_records / total_partitions:.2f}")
        
        # Partition distribution
        partition_cols = ["date", "country"]
        
        if all(col in df.columns for col in partition_cols):
            partition_dist = df.groupBy(*partition_cols) \
                .agg(
                    count("*").alias("record_count"),
                    sum("sales").alias("total_sales"),
                    avg("sales").alias("avg_sales")
                ) \
                .orderBy(col("record_count").desc())
            
            print("\nPartition distribution:")
            partition_dist.show()
            
            # Statistics
            stats = partition_dist.select("record_count").describe()
            print("\nPartition size statistics:")
            stats.show()
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Error analyzing metrics: {str(e)}")


def compare_partition_strategies(source_path, strategies):
    """
    Compare different partition strategies
    
    Args:
        source_path: Source data path
        strategies: List of (strategy_name, partition_cols) tuples
    """
    print("\n=== Comparing Partition Strategies ===")
    
    df = spark.read.parquet(source_path)
    
    results = []
    
    for strategy_name, partition_cols in strategies:
        print(f"\nTesting strategy: {strategy_name}")
        print(f"Partition columns: {partition_cols}")
        
        # Count unique partitions
        unique_partitions = df.select(*partition_cols).distinct().count()
        
        # Calculate partition distribution
        partition_dist = df.groupBy(*partition_cols) \
            .agg(count("*").alias("count"))
        
        avg_records = partition_dist.agg(avg("count")).collect()[0][0]
        max_records = partition_dist.agg(max("count")).collect()[0][0]
        min_records = partition_dist.agg(min("count")).collect()[0][0]
        
        skew_ratio = max_records / avg_records if avg_records > 0 else 0
        
        results.append({
            "strategy": strategy_name,
            "unique_partitions": unique_partitions,
            "avg_records": avg_records,
            "max_records": max_records,
            "min_records": min_records,
            "skew_ratio": skew_ratio
        })
        
        print(f"  Unique partitions: {unique_partitions}")
        print(f"  Avg records/partition: {avg_records:.2f}")
        print(f"  Skew ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
    
    # Create comparison DataFrame
    comparison_df = spark.createDataFrame(results)
    
    print("\n=== Strategy Comparison Summary ===")
    comparison_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    return comparison_df


def create_partition_report(table_path, output_path):
    """
    Create comprehensive partition report
    
    Args:
        table_path: Path to partitioned table
        output_path: Path to save report
    """
    print("\n=== Generating Partition Report ===")
    
    df = spark.read.parquet(table_path)
    
    # Gather metrics
    report_data = []
    
    # Overall metrics
    total_records = df.count()
    total_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    
    # Per-partition metrics
    partition_metrics = df.groupBy("date", "country") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("record_count"),
            sum("sales").alias("total_sales"),
            avg("sales").alias("avg_sales"),
            min("sales").alias("min_sales"),
            max("sales").alias("max_sales")
        )
    
    # Add metadata
    partition_metrics = partition_metrics.withColumn(
        "report_date", current_timestamp()
    ).withColumn(
        "total_records", lit(total_records)
    ).withColumn(
        "total_partitions", lit(total_partitions)
    )
    
    # Save report
    partition_metrics.write \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .parquet(output_path)
    
    print(f"✓ Partition report saved to: {output_path}")
    
    # Display summary
    print("\nReport Summary:")
    partition_metrics.show()
    
    return partition_metrics

class AdvancedPartitionPatterns:
    """
    Advanced partition management patterns and best practices
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
    
    def dynamic_partition_pruning(self, fact_table_path, dim_table_path):
        """
        Demonstrate dynamic partition pruning for query optimization
        
        Args:
            fact_table_path: Path to fact table
            dim_table_path: Path to dimension table
        """
        print("\n=== Dynamic Partition Pruning ===")
        
        # Read tables
        fact_df = self.spark.read.parquet(fact_table_path)
        
        # Create dimension data
        dim_data = [
            ("USA", "North America"),
            ("Canada", "North America"),
        ]
        dim_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(dim_data, ["country", "region"])
        
        # Join with partition pruning
        result = fact_df.join(
            broadcast(dim_df),
            "country",
            "inner"
        )
        
        print(f"Records after join: {result.count()}")
        result.show()
        
        print("✓ Dynamic partition pruning applied")
    
    def partition_evolution_strategy(self, source_path, target_path):
        """
        Handle partition schema evolution
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source table path
            target_path: Target table path
        """
        print("\n=== Partition Evolution Strategy ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
        
        # Add new partition column based on existing data
        evolved_df = df.withColumn(
            "year",
            year(to_date(col("date")))
        ).withColumn(
            "month",
            month(to_date(col("date")))
        )
        
        # Write with evolved partition structure
        evolved_df.write \
            .partitionBy("year", "month", "country") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(target_path)
        
        print("✓ Partition schema evolved")
        
        # Show new structure
        result_df = self.spark.read.parquet(target_path)
        result_df.select("year", "month", "country").distinct().show()
    
    def partition_metadata_management(self, table_path):
        """
        Manage partition metadata efficiently
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
        """
        print("\n=== Partition Metadata Management ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Extract partition information
        partition_info = df.
```python
select("date", "country") \
            .distinct() \
            .withColumn("partition_path", 
                       concat(lit("date="), col("date"), 
                              lit("/country="), col("country")))
        
        # Add metadata
        partition_metadata = partition_info.join(
            df.groupBy("date", "country").agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                sum("sales").alias("total_sales"),
                min("sales").alias("min_sales"),
                max("sales").alias("max_sales")
            ),
            ["date", "country"]
        ).withColumn(
            "last_updated", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "partition_size_estimate_mb",
            (col("record_count") * lit(1.0) / lit(1024)).cast("decimal(10,2)")
        )
        
        print("Partition Metadata:")
        partition_metadata.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Save metadata catalog
        metadata_path = f"{self.base_path}/partition_metadata"
        partition_metadata.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(metadata_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Partition metadata saved to: {metadata_path}")
        
        return partition_metadata

# PERFORMANCE MONITORING AND OPTIMIZATION
# ============================================================================

class PartitionPerformanceMonitor:
    """
    Monitor and optimize partition performance
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def benchmark_partition_strategy(self, table_path, query_filter):
        """
        Benchmark query performance with current partition strategy
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
            query_filter: Filter condition to test
        """
        print("\n=== Benchmarking Partition Strategy ===")
        
        import time
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Warm up
        df.filter(query_filter).count()
        
        # Benchmark
        start_time = time.time()
        result_count = df.filter(query_filter).count()
        end_time = time.time()
        
        execution_time = end_time - start_time
        
        print(f"Query filter: {query_filter}")
        print(f"Results: {result_count} records")
        print(f"Execution time: {execution_time:.3f} seconds")
        
        # Analyze query plan
        print("\nQuery Plan:")
        df.filter(query_filter).explain(True)
        
        return execution_time
    
    def analyze_partition_skew_impact(self, table_path):
        """
        Analyze impact of partition skew on performance
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
        """
        print("\n=== Analyzing Partition Skew Impact ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Get partition statistics
        partition_stats = df.groupBy("date", "country") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                sum("sales").alias("total_sales")
            )
        
        # Calculate skew metrics
        stats_summary = partition_stats.select("record_count").summary()
        
        print("Partition Size Distribution:")
        stats_summary.show()
        
        # Identify problematic partitions
        avg_records = partition_stats.agg(avg("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        
        skewed_partitions = partition_stats.filter(
            col("record_count") > avg_records * 2
        )
        
        print(f"\nAverage records per partition: {avg_records:.2f}")
        print(f"Skewed partitions (>2x average): {skewed_partitions.count()}")
        
        if skewed_partitions.count() > 0:
            print("\nSkewed Partitions:")
            skewed_partitions.orderBy(col("record_count").desc()).show()
            
            print("\n⚠ Recommendation: Consider rebalancing or splitting large partitions")
        else:
            print("\n✓ No significant skew detected")
    
    def estimate_partition_overhead(self, table_path):
        """
        Estimate overhead from partition structure
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
        """
        print("\n=== Estimating Partition Overhead ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Count total partitions
        partition_count = df.select("date", "country").distinct().count()
        total_records = df.count()
        
        avg_records_per_partition = total_records / partition_count
        
        print(f"Total partitions: {partition_count}")
        print(f"Total records: {total_records}")
        print(f"Avg records per partition: {avg_records_per_partition:.2f}")
        
        # Evaluate partition granularity
        if avg_records_per_partition < 1000:
            print("\n⚠ Warning: Very small partitions detected")
            print("   Recommendation: Consider merging partitions")
        elif avg_records_per_partition > 1000000:
            print("\n⚠ Warning: Very large partitions detected")
            print("   Recommendation: Consider splitting partitions")
        else:
            print("\n✓ Partition granularity is reasonable")
        
        # Calculate partition overhead ratio
        overhead_ratio = partition_count / total_records * 100
        print(f"\nPartition overhead ratio: {overhead_ratio:.4f}%")
        
        if overhead_ratio > 1:
            print("⚠ High partition overhead - too many small partitions")
        else:
            print("✓ Partition overhead is acceptable")

# PRODUCTION-READY UTILITIES

class PartitionMaintenanceScheduler:
    """
    Schedule and automate partition maintenance tasks
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
    
    def daily_partition_maintenance(self, table_path):
        """
        Perform daily partition maintenance
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
        """
        print("\n=== Daily Partition Maintenance ===")
        
        # 1. Validate partition integrity
        print("\n1. Validating partition integrity...")
        repair_pattern = PartitionRepairPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
        repair_pattern.validate_partition_integrity(table_path)
        
        # 2. Compact small files
        print("\n2. Compacting small files...")
        compaction_pattern = PartitionCompactionPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
        compacted_path = f"{table_path}_compacted"
        compaction_pattern.compact_partition(
            table_path,
            compacted_path,
            target_file_size_mb=128
        )
        
        # 3. Check for skew
        print("\n3. Checking for partition skew...")
        rebalancing_pattern = PartitionRebalancingPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
        skew_ratio = rebalancing_pattern.detect_skew(
            table_path,
            ["date", "country"]
        )
        
        if skew_ratio > 2.0:
            print("   Skew detected - rebalancing recommended")
        
        print("\n✓ Daily maintenance completed")
    
    def weekly_partition_cleanup(self, table_path, retention_days=90):
        """
        Perform weekly partition cleanup
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
            retention_days: Days to retain data
        """
        print("\n=== Weekly Partition Cleanup ===")
        
        # Drop old partitions
        print(f"\n1. Dropping partitions older than {retention_days} days...")
        dropping_pattern = PartitionDroppingPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
        dropping_pattern.drop_old_partitions(table_path, retention_days)
        
        # Remove empty partitions
        print("\n2. Removing empty partitions...")
        dropping_pattern.drop_empty_partitions(table_path)
        
        print("\n✓ Weekly cleanup completed")
    
    def monthly_partition_optimization(self, table_path):
        """
        Perform monthly partition optimization
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
        """
        print("\n=== Monthly Partition Optimization ===")
        
        # 1. Analyze partition metrics
        print("\n1. Analyzing partition metrics...")
        analyze_partition_metrics(table_path)
        
        # 2. Rebalance if needed
        print("\n2. Performing adaptive rebalancing...")
        rebalancing_pattern = PartitionRebalancingPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
        optimized_path = f"{table_path}_optimized"
        rebalancing_pattern.adaptive_rebalancing(
            table_path,
            optimized_path,
            target_records_per_partition=10000
        )
        
        # 3. Generate report
        print("\n3. Generating optimization report...")
        report_path = f"{self.base_path}/monthly_report"
        create_partition_report(table_path, report_path)
        
        print("\n✓ Monthly optimization completed")

# ADDITIONAL REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

class RealWorldPartitionScenarios:
    """
    Real-world partition management scenarios and solutions
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
    
    def scenario_1_daily_etl_pipeline(self):
        """
        Scenario: Daily ETL pipeline with incremental partition loading
        Solution: Add new daily partitions without affecting existing data
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("SCENARIO 1: Daily ETL Pipeline")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Simulate existing data
        existing_data = [
            ("2024-01-01", "USA", "Product A", 1000),
            ("2024-01-02", "USA", "Product B", 1500),
        ]
        
        # New daily data
        new_data = [
            ("2024-01-03", "USA", "Product A", 1200),
            ("2024-01-03", "UK", "Product B", 800),
            ("2024-01-03", "Canada", "Product C", 600),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("country", StringType(), True),
            StructField("product", StringType(), True),
            StructField("revenue", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Write existing data
        existing_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(existing_data, schema)
        table_path = f"{self.base_path}/daily_sales"
        
        existing_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(table_path)
        
        print("✓ Existing data loaded")
        
        # Add new daily partition
        new_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(new_data, schema)
        
        new_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .mode("append") \
            .parquet(table_path)
        
        print("✓ New daily partition added")
        
        # Verify
        result_df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        print(f"\nTotal records: {result_df.count()}")
        
        daily_summary = result_df.groupBy("date") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue")
            ) \
            .orderBy("date")
        
        print("\nDaily Summary:")
        daily_summary.show()
        
        return table_path
    
    def scenario_2_historical_data_archival(self, table_path):
        """
        Scenario: Archive historical data older than retention period
        Solution: Move old partitions to archive location before deletion
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("SCENARIO 2: Historical Data Archival")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Define retention policy
        retention_days = 2
        cutoff_date = "2024-01-02"
        
        print(f"Retention policy: {retention_days} days")
        print(f"Cutoff date: {cutoff_date}")
        
        # Identify data to archive
        archive_df = df.filter(col("date") < cutoff_date)
        active_df = df.filter(col("date") >= cutoff_date)
        
        print(f"\nRecords to archive: {archive_df.count()}")
        print(f"Records to keep active: {active_df.count()}")
        
        # Archive old data
        archive_path = f"{self.base_path}/archived_sales"
        
        archive_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(archive_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Data archived to: {archive_path}")
        
        # Update active table
        active_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(table_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Active table updated")
        
        # Verify
        active_result = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        archive_result = self.spark.read.parquet(archive_path)
        
        print(f"\nActive records: {active_result.count()}")
        print(f"Archived records: {archive_result.count()}")
    
    def scenario_3_partition_skew_resolution(self):
        """
        Scenario: Handle partition skew in production data
        Solution: Identify and rebalance skewed partitions
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("SCENARIO 3: Partition Skew Resolution")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create skewed data
        skewed_data = []
        
        # Create normal partitions
        for date in ["2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"]:
            for i in range(100):
                skewed_data.append((date, f"Customer_{i}", 100))
        
        # Create skewed partition (10x larger)
        for i in range(1000):
            skewed_data.append(("2024-01-03", f"Customer_{i}", 100))
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("amount", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        skewed_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(skewed_data, schema)
        skewed_path = f"{self.base_path}/skewed_transactions"
        
        # Write skewed data
        skewed_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(skewed_path)
        
        print("✓ Skewed data created")
        
        # Detect skew
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(skewed_path)
        
        partition_stats = df.groupBy("date") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("record_count")) \
            .orderBy(col("record_count").desc())
        
        print("\nPartition Distribution:")
        partition_stats.show()
        
        # Calculate skew
        stats = partition_stats.select("record_count")
        avg_count = stats.agg(avg("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        max_count = stats.agg(max("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        
        skew_ratio = max_count / avg_count
        print(f"\nSkew Ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
        
        if skew_ratio > 2.0:
            print("⚠ Significant skew detected - applying resolution")
            
            # Solution: Add sub-partitioning to large partition
            from pyspark.sql.window import Window
            
            rebalanced_df = df.withColumn(
                "partition_size",
                count("*").over(Window.partitionBy("date"))
            )
            
            # Add sub-partition only for large partitions
            rebalanced_df = rebalanced_df.withColumn(
                "sub_partition",
                when(col("partition_size") > avg_count * 1.5,
                     (hash(col("customer_id")) % 5).cast("string"))
                .otherwise(lit("0"))
            )
            
            # Write rebalanced data
            rebalanced_path = f"{self.base_path}/rebalanced_transactions"
            
            rebalanced_df.drop("partition_size").write \
                .partitionBy("date", "sub_partition") \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .parquet(rebalanced_path)
            
            print(f"✓ Data rebalanced to: {rebalanced_path}")
            
            # Verify rebalancing
            result_df = self.spark.read.parquet(rebalanced_path)
            new_stats = result_df.groupBy("date", "sub_partition") \
                .agg(count("*").alias("record_count")) \
                .orderBy("date", "sub_partition")
            
            print("\nRebalanced Distribution:")
            new_stats.show()
    
    def scenario_4_multi_level_partitioning(self):
        """
        Scenario: Implement multi-level partitioning for large datasets
        Solution: Use hierarchical partitioning (year/month/day/hour)
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("SCENARIO 4: Multi-Level Partitioning")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create time-series data
        from datetime import datetime, timedelta
        
        time_series_data = []
        base_date = datetime(2024, 1, 1)
        
        for day in range(3):
            for hour in range(24):
                timestamp = base_date + timedelta(days=day, hours=hour)
                for i in range(10):
                    time_series_data.append((
                        timestamp.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                        f"sensor_{i}",
                        float(100 + i)
                    ))
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True),
            StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("value", FloatType(), True)
        ])
        
        ts_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(time_series_data, schema)
        
        # Add partition columns
        multi_level_df = ts_df.withColumn(
            "ts", to_timestamp(col("timestamp"))
        ).withColumn(
            "year", year(col("ts"))
        ).withColumn(
            "month", month(col("ts"))
        ).withColumn(
            "day", dayofmonth(col("ts"))
        ).withColumn(
            "hour", hour(col("ts"))
        )
        
        # Write with multi-level partitioning
        multi_level_path = f"{self.base_path}/sensor_data"
        
        multi_level_df.write \
            .partitionBy("year", "month", "day", "hour") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(multi_level_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Multi-level partitioned data written to: {multi_level_path}")
        
        # Show partition structure
        result_df = self.spark.read.parquet(multi_level_path)
        
        partition_summary = result_df.groupBy("year", "month", "day") \
            .agg(
                countDistinct("hour").alias("hour_count"),
                count("*").alias("record_count")
            ) \
            .orderBy("year", "month", "day")
        
        print("\nPartition Structure:")
        partition_summary.show()
        
        # Demonstrate partition pruning
        print("\nQuerying specific partition:")
        filtered_df = result_df.filter(
            (col("year") == 2024) &
            (col("month") == 1) &
            (col("day") == 2) &
            (col("hour") == 10)
        )
        
        print(f"Records in specific partition: {filtered_df.count()}")
        filtered_df.show(5)
    
    def scenario_5_partition_migration(self):
        """
        Scenario: Migrate from one partition strategy to another
        Solution: Safely migrate data with zero downtime
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("SCENARIO 5: Partition Strategy Migration")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create data with old partition strategy
        old_data = [
            ("2024-01-01", "USA", "Product A", 1000),
            ("2024-01-01", "UK", "Product B", 800),
            ("2024-01-02", "USA", "Product A", 1200),
            ("2024-01-02", "Canada", "Product C", 600),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("country", StringType(), True),
            StructField("product", StringType(), True),
            StructField("revenue", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        old_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(old_data, schema)
        
        # Old strategy: partition by date only
        old_path = f"{self.base_path}/sales_old_strategy"
        
        old_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(old_path)
        
        print("✓ Old partition strategy (date only)")
        
        # New strategy: partition by date and country
        new_path = f"{self.base_path}/sales_new_strategy"
        
        print("\nMigrating to new strategy (date + country)...")
        
        # Read from old location
        migration_df = self.spark.read.parquet(old_path)
        
        # Write to new location with new strategy
        migration_df.write \
            .partitionBy("date", "country") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(new_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Data migrated to: {new_path}")
        
        # Verify migration
        old_result = self.spark.read.parquet(old_path)
        new_result = self.spark.read.parquet(new_path)
        
        print(f"\nOld strategy records: {old_result.count()}")
        print(f"New strategy records: {new_result.count()}")
        
        # Compare partition counts
        old_partitions = old_result.select("date").distinct().count()
        new_partitions = new_result.select("date", "country").distinct().count()
        
        print(f"\nOld partitions: {old_partitions}")
        print(f"New partitions: {new_partitions}")
        
        print("\n✓ Migration completed successfully")
        print("  Next step: Update applications to use new path")
        print("  Then: Archive or delete old partition structure")

# PARTITION MONITORING DASHBOARD
# ============================================================================

class PartitionMonitoringDashboard:
    """
    Create monitoring dashboard for partition health
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
    
    def generate_health_report(self, table_path):
        """
        Generate
```python
 comprehensive partition health report
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PARTITION HEALTH DASHBOARD")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # 1. Overall Statistics
        print("\n1. OVERALL STATISTICS")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        total_records = df.count()
        total_partitions = df.select("date").distinct().count()
        
        print(f"Total Records: {total_records:,}")
        print(f"Total Partitions: {total_partitions}")
        print(f"Avg Records/Partition: {total_records / total_partitions:,.2f}")
        
        # 2. Partition Size Distribution
        print("\n2. PARTITION SIZE DISTRIBUTION")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        partition_sizes = df.groupBy("date") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("size")) \
            .select("size")
        
        size_stats = partition_sizes.describe()
        size_stats.show()
        
        # 3. Skew Analysis
        print("\n3. SKEW ANALYSIS")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        partition_dist = df.groupBy("date") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("record_count")) \
            .orderBy(col("record_count").desc())
        
        avg_size = partition_dist.agg(avg("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        max_size = partition_dist.agg(max("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        min_size = partition_dist.agg(min("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        
        skew_ratio = max_size / avg_size if avg_size > 0 else 0
        
        print(f"Average Size: {avg_size:,.2f}")
        print(f"Maximum Size: {max_size:,}")
        print(f"Minimum Size: {min_size:,}")
        print(f"Skew Ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
        
        if skew_ratio > 3.0:
            health_status = "🔴 CRITICAL"
        elif skew_ratio > 2.0:
            health_status = "🟡 WARNING"
        else:
            health_status = "🟢 HEALTHY"
        
        print(f"Skew Status: {health_status}")
        
        # 4. Top and Bottom Partitions
        print("\n4. LARGEST PARTITIONS (Top 5)")
        print("-" * 80)
        partition_dist.show(5)
        
        print("\n5. SMALLEST PARTITIONS (Bottom 5)")
        print("-" * 80)
        partition_dist.orderBy(col("record_count").asc()).show(5)
        
        # 5. Growth Trend
        print("\n6. PARTITION GROWTH TREND")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        growth_trend = df.groupBy("date") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue") if "revenue" in df.columns else count("*").alias("total_revenue")
            ) \
            .orderBy("date")
        
        growth_trend.show()
        
        # 6. Recommendations
        print("\n7. RECOMMENDATIONS")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        recommendations = []
        
        if skew_ratio > 2.0:
            recommendations.append("⚠ High skew detected - consider rebalancing")
        
        if avg_size < 1000:
            recommendations.append("⚠ Small partitions - consider merging")
        
        if avg_size > 1000000:
            recommendations.append("⚠ Large partitions - consider splitting")
        
        if total_partitions > 10000:
            recommendations.append("⚠ Too many partitions - review partition strategy")
        
        if not recommendations:
            recommendations.append("✓ Partition health is good")
        
        for rec in recommendations:
            print(f"  {rec}")
        
        # 7. Summary Metrics
        print("\n8. SUMMARY METRICS")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        summary_data = [{
            "metric": "Total Records",
            "value": total_records,
            "status": "✓"
        }, {
            "metric": "Total Partitions",
            "value": total_partitions,
            "status": "✓" if total_partitions < 10000 else "⚠"
        }, {
            "metric": "Skew Ratio",
            "value": f"{skew_ratio:.2f}",
            "status": "✓" if skew_ratio < 2.0 else "⚠"
        }, {
            "metric": "Avg Partition Size",
            "value": f"{avg_size:.0f}",
            "status": "✓" if 1000 <= avg_size <= 1000000 else "⚠"
        }]
        
        summary_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(summary_data)
        summary_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        return {
            "total_records": total_records,
            "total_partitions": total_partitions,
            "skew_ratio": skew_ratio,
            "avg_size": avg_size,
            "health_status": health_status
        }
    
    def create_visual_report(self, table_path, output_path):
        """
        Create visual partition report with charts
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
            output_path: Path to save report
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("CREATING VISUAL PARTITION REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Prepare visualization data
        viz_data = df.groupBy("date") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue") if "revenue" in df.columns else lit(0).alias("total_revenue")
            ) \
            .withColumn("report_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
            .orderBy("date")
        
        # Save visualization data
        viz_data.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(output_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Visual report data saved to: {output_path}")
        print("\nReport Data Preview:")
        viz_data.show()
        
        # Generate ASCII chart
        self._generate_ascii_chart(viz_data)
    
    def _generate_ascii_chart(self, df):
        """
        Generate simple ASCII bar chart
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with partition statistics
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PARTITION SIZE CHART")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        data = df.select("date", "record_count").collect()
        
        if not data:
            print("No data to display")
            return
        
        max_count = max(row["record_count"] for row in data)
        scale = 50 / max_count if max_count > 0 else 1
        
        for row in data:
            date = row["date"]
            count = row["record_count"]
            bar_length = int(count * scale)
            bar = "█" * bar_length
            print(f"{date} | {bar} {count:,}")
        
        print("=" * 80)

# PARTITION AUTOMATION FRAMEWORK
# ============================================================================

class PartitionAutomationFramework:
    """
    Automated partition management framework
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.config = {
            "retention_days": 90,
            "compaction_threshold_mb": 128,
            "skew_threshold": 2.0,
            "min_partition_size": 1000,
            "max_partition_size": 1000000
        }
    
    def auto_optimize_table(self, table_path):
        """
        Automatically optimize table based on configuration
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("AUTOMATIC PARTITION OPTIMIZATION")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(table_path)
        
        # Analyze current state
        print("\nAnalyzing partition state...")
        
        partition_stats = df.groupBy("date") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("record_count"))
        
        avg_size = partition_stats.agg(avg("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        max_size = partition_stats.agg(max("record_count")).collect()[0][0]
        skew_ratio = max_size / avg_size if avg_size > 0 else 0
        
        print(f"Current skew ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
        print(f"Average partition size: {avg_size:.0f}")
        
        actions_taken = []
        
        # Action 1: Rebalance if skewed
        if skew_ratio > self.config["skew_threshold"]:
            print(f"\n⚡ Action: Rebalancing (skew > {self.config['skew_threshold']})")
            
            rebalanced_path = f"{table_path}_rebalanced"
            
            rebalancing = PartitionRebalancingPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
            rebalancing.adaptive_rebalancing(
                table_path,
                rebalanced_path,
                target_records_per_partition=int(avg_size)
            )
            
            actions_taken.append("Rebalanced skewed partitions")
        
        # Action 2: Compact if needed
        small_partitions = partition_stats.filter(
            col("record_count") < self.config["min_partition_size"]
        ).count()
        
        if small_partitions > 0:
            print(f"\n⚡ Action: Compacting {small_partitions} small partitions")
            
            compacted_path = f"{table_path}_compacted"
            
            compaction = PartitionCompactionPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
            compaction.compact_partition(
                table_path,
                compacted_path,
                target_file_size_mb=self.config["compaction_threshold_mb"]
            )
            
            actions_taken.append(f"Compacted {small_partitions} small partitions")
        
        # Action 3: Split large partitions
        large_partitions = partition_stats.filter(
            col("record_count") > self.config["max_partition_size"]
        ).count()
        
        if large_partitions > 0:
            print(f"\n⚡ Action: Splitting {large_partitions} large partitions")
            
            split_path = f"{table_path}_split"
            
            splitting = PartitionSplittingPattern(self.spark, self.base_path)
            splitting.split_large_partition(
                table_path,
                split_path,
                "date",
                max_records_per_partition=self.config["max_partition_size"]
            )
            
            actions_taken.append(f"Split {large_partitions} large partitions")
        
        # Summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("OPTIMIZATION SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        if actions_taken:
            print("\nActions Taken:")
            for i, action in enumerate(actions_taken, 1):
                print(f"  {i}. {action}")
        else:
            print("\n✓ No optimization needed - partitions are healthy")
        
        return actions_taken
    
    def schedule_maintenance(self, table_path, schedule_type="daily"):
        """
        Schedule partition maintenance tasks
        
        Args:
            table_path: Path to partitioned table
            schedule_type: Type of schedule (daily/weekly/monthly)
        """
        print(f"\n=== Scheduling {schedule_type.upper()} Maintenance ===")
        
        scheduler = PartitionMaintenanceScheduler(self.spark, self.base_path)
        
        if schedule_type == "daily":
            scheduler.daily_partition_maintenance(table_path)
        elif schedule_type == "weekly":
            scheduler.weekly_partition_cleanup(table_path)
        elif schedule_type == "monthly":
            scheduler.monthly_partition_optimization(table_path)
        else:
            print(f"Unknown schedule type: {schedule_type}")

"""
PySpark Cache Management Patterns
Comprehensive examples demonstrating various caching strategies

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *

import time

from functools import wraps

# Initialize Spark Session with cache configurations

    .appName("Cache Management Patterns") \

# 1. SELECTIVE CACHING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Cache only frequently accessed or expensive-to-compute datasets
Use Case: Optimize memory usage by caching strategically
"""

class SelectiveCachingPattern:
    """
    Implements selective caching based on access frequency and computation cost
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.access_counter = {}
        self.cache_threshold = 3  # Cache after 3 accesses
        
    def should_cache(self, df_name, computation_time=None):
        """
        Determine if a DataFrame should be cached based on access patterns
        
        Args:
            df_name: Name identifier for the DataFrame
            computation_time: Time taken to compute the DataFrame
            
        Returns:
            Boolean indicating whether to cache
        """
        # Track access count
        self.access_counter[df_name] = self.access_counter.get(df_name, 0) + 1
        
        # Cache if frequently accessed or expensive to compute
        if self.access_counter[df_name] >= self.cache_threshold:
            return True
        if computation_time and computation_time > 5:  # 5 seconds threshold
            return True
        return False
    
    def smart_cache(self, df, df_name, force_cache=False):
        """
        Intelligently cache DataFrame based on usage patterns
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Perform a lightweight action to measure computation time
        count = df.count()
        computation_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        if force_cache or self.should_cache(df_name, computation_time):
            print(f"Caching {df_name} (accessed {self.access_counter.get(df_name, 0)} times, "
                  f"computation time: {computation_time:.2f}s)")
            return df.cache()
        else:
            print(f"Not caching {df_name} yet (accessed {self.access_counter.get(df_name, 0)} times)")
            return df
    
    def example(self):
        """Demonstrate selective caching"""
        print("\n=== SELECTIVE CACHING PATTERN ===\n")
        
        # Create sample data
        data = [(i, f"user_{i % 100}", i * 10) for i in range(10000)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "user", "value"])
        
        # Expensive transformation
        expensive_df = df.groupBy("user").agg(
            sum("value").alias("total_value"),
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        )
        
        # First access - measure and decide
        cached_df = self.smart_cache(expensive_df, "user_aggregates")
        result1 = cached_df.collect()
        
        # Second access
        cached_df = self.smart_cache(cached_df, "user_aggregates")
        result2 = cached_df.collect()
        
        # Third access - should cache now
        cached_df = self.smart_cache(cached_df, "user_aggregates")
        result3 = cached_df.collect()
        
        return cached_df

# 2. MULTI-LEVEL CACHING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Use different storage levels for different data access patterns
Use Case: Optimize for memory, disk, and serialization trade-offs
"""

class MultiLevelCachingPattern:
    """
    Implements multi-level caching with different storage strategies
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.cache_registry = {}
    
    def cache_by_priority(self, df, df_name, priority="high"):
        """
        Cache DataFrame with appropriate storage level based on priority
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to cache
            df_name: Identifier for the DataFrame
            priority: 'critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low'
        """
        storage_levels = {
            'critical': StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY,  # Fast, memory only
            'high': StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK,  # Memory preferred, disk fallback
            'medium': StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER,  # Serialized, saves memory
            'low': StorageLevel.DISK_ONLY  # Disk only, saves memory
        }
        
        storage_level = storage_levels.get(priority, StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        
        print(f"Caching {df_name} with {priority} priority using {storage_level}")
        cached_df = df.persist(storage_level)
        
        self.cache_registry[df_name] = {
            'df': cached_df,
            'priority': priority,
            'storage_level': storage_level,
            'cached_at': datetime.now()
        }
        
        return cached_df
    
    def get_cache_info(self):
        """Get information about all cached DataFrames"""
        info = []
        for name, details in self.cache_registry.items():
            info.append({
                'name': name,
                'priority': details['priority'],
                'storage_level': str(details['storage_level']),
                'cached_at': details['cached_at']
            })
        return info
    
    def example(self):
        """Demonstrate multi-level caching"""
        print("\n=== MULTI-LEVEL CACHING PATTERN ===\n")
        
        # Create different datasets with different priorities
        
        # Critical: Frequently accessed lookup table
        lookup_data = [(i, f"category_{i}") for i in range(100)]
        lookup_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(lookup_data, ["id", "category"])
        cached_lookup = self.cache_by_priority(lookup_df, "lookup_table", "critical")
        
        # High: Main transaction data
        transaction_data = [(i, i % 100, i * 10) for i in range(10000)]
        transaction_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            transaction_data, ["transaction_id", "category_id", "amount"]
        )
        cached_transactions = self.cache_by_priority(
            transaction_df, "transactions", "high"
        )
        
        # Medium: Aggregated data
        aggregated_df = cached_transactions.groupBy("category_id").agg(
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            count("*").alias("transaction_count")
        )
        cached_aggregated = self.cache_by_priority(
            aggregated_df, "aggregated_data", "medium"
        )
        
        # Low: Historical archive data
        archive_data = [(i, f"archive_{i}", i * 5) for i in range(50000)]
        archive_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            archive_data, ["id", "description", "value"]
        )
        cached_archive = self.cache_by_priority(archive_df, "archive", "low")
        
        # Display cache information
        print("\nCache Registry:")
        for info in self.get_cache_info():
            print(f"  {info['name']}: {info['priority']} priority, "
                  f"{info['storage_level']}, cached at {info['cached_at']}")
        
        return self.cache_registry

# 3. CACHE EVICTION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Implement strategies to evict cached data based on policies
Use Case: Manage memory efficiently by removing stale or less important caches
"""

class CacheEvictionPattern:
    """
    Implements various cache eviction strategies (LRU, TTL, Size-based)
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session, max_cache_size=5):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.cache_registry = {}
        self.max_cache_size = max_cache_size
        self.access_times = {}
    
    def cache_with_ttl(self, df, df_name, ttl_seconds=300):
        """
        Cache with Time-To-Live eviction policy
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to cache
            df_name: Identifier
            ttl_seconds: Time to live in seconds
        """
        cached_df = df.cache()
        
        self.cache_registry[df_name] = {
            'df': cached_df,
            'cached_at': datetime.now(),
            'ttl_seconds': ttl_seconds,
            'eviction_policy': 'TTL'
        }
        self.access_times[df_name] = datetime.now()
        
        print(f"Cached {df_name} with TTL of {ttl_seconds} seconds")
        return cached_df
    
    def cache_with_lru(self, df, df_name):
        """
        Cache with Least Recently Used eviction policy
        """
        # Evict if cache is full
        if len(self.cache_registry) >= self.max_cache_size:
            self._evict_lru()
        
        cached_df = df.cache()
        
        self.cache_registry[df_name] = {
            'df': cached_df,
            'cached_at': datetime.now(),
            'eviction_policy': 'LRU'
        }
        self.access_times[df_name] = datetime.now()
        
        print(f"Cached {df_name} with LRU policy")
        return cached_df
    
    def access_cache(self, df_name):
        """
        Access cached DataFrame and update access time
        """
        if df_name in self.cache_registry:
            self.access_times[df_name] = datetime.now()
            return self.cache_registry[df_name]['df']
        return None
    
    def _evict_lru(self):
        """Evict least recently used cache"""
        if not self.access_times:
            return
        
        # Find least recently used
        lru_name = min(self.access_times.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])[0]
        self.evict_cache(lru_name)
    
    def evict_expired_caches(self):
        """Evict caches that have exceeded their TTL"""
        current_time = datetime.now()
        expired = []
        
        for name, details in self.cache_registry.items():
            if 'ttl_seconds' in details:
                age = (current_time - details['cached_at']).total_seconds()
                if age > details['ttl_seconds']:
                    expired.append(name)
        
        for name in expired:
            self.evict_cache(name)
        
        return expired
    
    def evict_cache(self, df_name):
        """Manually evict a specific cache"""
        if df_name in self.cache_registry:
            self.cache_registry[df_name]['df'].unpersist()
            del self.cache_registry[df_name]
            if df_name in self.access_times:
                del self.access_times[df_name]
            print(f"Evicted cache: {df_name}")
            return True
        return False
    
    def get_cache_status(self):
        """Get status of all caches"""
        current_time = datetime.now()
        status = []
        
        for name, details in self.cache_registry.items():
            age = (current_time - details['cached_at']).total_seconds()
            last_access = (current_time - self.access_times.get(name, details['cached_at'])).total_seconds()
            
            status.append({
                'name': name,
                'policy': details['eviction_policy'],
                'age_seconds': age,
                'last_access_seconds': last_access,
                'ttl_seconds': details.get('ttl_seconds', 'N/A')
            })
        
        return status
    
    def example(self):
        """Demonstrate cache eviction patterns"""
        print("\n=== CACHE EVICTION PATTERN ===\n")
        
        # Create sample data
        for i in range(7):
            data = [(j, f"data_{i}_{j}") for j in range(1000)]
            df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "value"])
            
            if i < 3:
                # Cache with TTL
                self.cache_with_ttl(df, f"df_ttl_{i}", ttl_seconds=10)
            else:
                # Cache with LRU
                self.cache_with_lru(df, f"df_lru_{i}")
            
            time.sleep(0.1)  # Simulate time passing
        
        # Display initial cache status
        print("\nInitial Cache Status:")
        for status in self.get_cache_status():
            print(f"  {status['name']}: {status['policy']}, "
                  f"age={status['age_seconds']:.2f}s, "
                  f"last_access={status['last_access_seconds']:.2f}s")
        
        # Simulate some accesses
        print("\nAccessing some caches...")
        self.access_cache("df_lru_3")
        self.access_cache("df_lru_4")
        
        # Evict expired caches
        print("\nEvicting expired caches...")
        time.sleep(11)  # Wait for TTL to expire
        expired = self.evict_expired_caches()
        print(f"Evicted: {expired}")
        
        # Display final cache status
        print("\nFinal Cache Status:")
        for status in self.get_cache_status():
            print(f"  {status['name']}: {status['policy']}, "
                  f"age={status['age_seconds']:.2f}s")
        
        return self.cache_registry

"""

class CacheWarmingPattern:

    def warm_cache_sequential(self, dataframes_dict):
        """
        Warm multiple caches sequentially
        
        Args:
            dataframes_dict: Dictionary of {name: dataframe}
        """
        print("Starting sequential cache warming...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        for name, df in dataframes_dict.items():
            print(f"  Warming cache: {name}")
            cached_df = df.cache()
```python
            # Force materialization with count
            count = cached_df.count()
            self.warmed_caches[name] = {
                'df': cached_df,
                'warmed_at': datetime.now(),
                'row_count': count
            }
            print(f"    Cached {count} rows")
        
        elapsed = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"Sequential warming completed in {elapsed:.2f} seconds")
        return self.warmed_caches
    
    def warm_cache_parallel(self, dataframes_dict, parallelism=4):
        """
        Warm multiple caches in parallel using Spark's parallel collections
        
        Args:
            dataframes_dict: Dictionary of {name: dataframe}
            parallelism: Number of parallel warming operations
        """
        print(f"Starting parallel cache warming (parallelism={parallelism})...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
        
        def warm_single_cache(name, df):
            """Helper function to warm a single cache"""
            cached_df = df.cache()
            count = cached_df.count()
            return name, {
                'df': cached_df,
                'warmed_at': datetime.now(),
                'row_count': count
            }
        
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallelism) as executor:
            futures = {
                executor.submit(warm_single_cache, name, df): name 
                for name, df in dataframes_dict.items()
            }
            
            for future in as_completed(futures):
                name, cache_info = future.result()
                self.warmed_caches[name] = cache_info
                print(f"  Warmed cache: {name} ({cache_info['row_count']} rows)")
        
        elapsed = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"Parallel warming completed in {elapsed:.2f} seconds")
        return self.warmed_caches
    
    def warm_cache_predictive(self, historical_access_patterns):

        Predictively warm caches based on historical access patterns

        print("Starting predictive cache warming...")
        
        # Sort by access probability
        sorted_patterns = sorted(

        for df_name, probability in sorted_patterns:
