def example_financial_data_export():
    """
    Real-world example: Financial data export with compliance and auditing.
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("FinancialDataExport") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        logger.info("="*70)
        logger.info("FINANCIAL DATA
```python
 EXPORT WITH COMPLIANCE")
        logger.info("="*70)
        
        # Initialize exporters
        advanced_exporter = AdvancedExportPatterns(spark)
        delta_exporter = DeltaLakeExporter(spark)
        
        # ========== 1. TRANSACTIONS DATA ==========
        logger.info("\n1. Processing Transactions (Encrypted Export)")
        
        transactions_schema = StructType([
            StructField("transaction_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("account_number", StringType(), False),
            StructField("customer_ssn", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("transaction_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("transaction_date", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("merchant", StringType(), False),
            StructField("category", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        transactions_data = [
            (f"TXN{str(i).zfill(10)}", f"ACC{str(i % 1000).zfill(8)}",
             f"SSN{str(i % 500).zfill(9)}", 100.0 + i * 10,
             ["debit", "credit", "transfer"][i % 3],
             datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=i),
             f"Merchant_{i % 100}",
             ["groceries", "utilities", "entertainment", "healthcare"][i % 4])
            for i in range(1, 10001)
        ]
        
        transactions_df = spark.createDataFrame(transactions_data, transactions_schema)
        
        # Export with encryption for PII fields
        advanced_exporter.export_with_encryption(
            df=transactions_df,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/exports/transactions/encrypted",
            encryption_columns=["account_number", "customer_ssn"],
            encryption_key="financial_encryption_key_2024",
            format="parquet"
        )
        
        logger.info("Transactions exported with encryption")
        
        # ========== 2. AUDIT TRAIL WITH LINEAGE ==========
        logger.info("\n2. Creating Audit Trail (Lineage Tracking)")
        
        source_info = {
            "system": "core_banking_system",
            "database": "transactions_db",
            "table": "daily_transactions",
            "extraction_time": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "extracted_by": "etl_service_account"
        }
        
        transformation_info = {
            "transformations": [
                "PII encryption",
                "Data validation",
                "Deduplication"
            ],
            "validation_rules": [
                "amount > 0",
                "transaction_date is not null"
            ],
            "version": "2.0.0",
            "compliance": "SOX, PCI-DSS"
        }
        
        lineage_result = advanced_exporter.export_with_lineage_tracking(
            df=transactions_df,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/exports/transactions/with_lineage",
            source_info=source_info,
            transformation_info=transformation_info,
            format="parquet"
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Audit trail created: {lineage_result['lineage_id']}")
        
        # ========== 3. VERSIONED EXPORTS FOR COMPLIANCE ==========
        logger.info("\n3. Creating Versioned Export (Compliance)")
        
        version = f"v{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"
        
        version_info = advanced_exporter.export_with_versioning(
            df=transactions_df,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/exports/transactions/versioned",
            version=version,
            format="parquet",
            keep_versions=10
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Versioned export: {version_info}")
        
        # ========== 4. REGULATORY REPORTS - SELECTIVE EXPORT ==========
        logger.info("\n4. Generating Regulatory Reports (Selective Export)")
        
        exporter = DataExportPatterns(spark)
        
        # High-value transactions report (>$10,000)
        high_value_report = exporter.selective_export_pattern(
            df=transactions_df,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/reports/high_value_transactions",
            filter_conditions="amount > 10000",
            select_columns=[
                "transaction_id", "amount", "transaction_type",
                "transaction_date", "merchant", "category"
            ],
            format="csv"
        )
        
        # Suspicious activity report (multiple large transfers)
        suspicious_activity = transactions_df.filter(
            (col("transaction_type") == "transfer") & (col("amount") > 5000)
        )
        
        exporter.full_export_pattern(
            df=suspicious_activity,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/reports/suspicious_activity",
            format="parquet",
            partition_by=["transaction_date"]
        )
        
        logger.info("Regulatory reports generated")
        
        # ========== 5. DELTA LAKE FOR TRANSACTION HISTORY ==========
        logger.info("\n5. Maintaining Transaction History (Delta Lake)")
        
        delta_path = "s3://financial-data/delta/transaction_history"
        
        # Initial load
        delta_exporter.export_to_delta(
            df=transactions_df,
            delta_path=delta_path,
            mode="overwrite",
            partition_by=["category"],
            optimize_write=True
        )
        
        # Add version description for audit
        delta_exporter.export_with_time_travel(
            df=transactions_df,
            delta_path=delta_path,
            version_description="Initial load - 2024-01-15"
        )
        
        # Simulate corrections/updates
        corrections_data = [
            (f"TXN{str(i).zfill(10)}", f"ACC{str(i % 1000).zfill(8)}",
             f"SSN{str(i % 500).zfill(9)}", 100.0 + i * 10 + 5.0,  # Corrected amount
             ["debit", "credit", "transfer"][i % 3],
             datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=i),
             f"Merchant_{i % 100}",
             ["groceries", "utilities", "entertainment", "healthcare"][i % 4])
            for i in range(1, 51)  # Correct first 50 transactions
        ]
        
        corrections_df = spark.createDataFrame(corrections_data, transactions_schema)
        
        # Upsert corrections
        delta_exporter.upsert_to_delta(
            df=corrections_df,
            delta_path=delta_path,
            merge_keys=["transaction_id"]
        )
        
        logger.info("Transaction history updated with corrections")
        
        # ========== 6. DAILY RECONCILIATION EXPORTS ==========
        logger.info("\n6. Daily Reconciliation (Scheduled Export)")
        
        # Daily summary by category
        daily_summary = transactions_df.groupBy("category", "transaction_type") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
                sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
                avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
                min("amount").alias("min_amount"),
                max("amount").alias("max_amount")
            )
        
        reconciliation_metadata = exporter.scheduled_export_pattern(
            df=daily_summary,
            output_base_path="s3://financial-data/reconciliation/daily",
            schedule_type="daily",
            format="parquet",
            retention_days=2555,  # 7 years for financial records
            partition_by_time=True
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Daily reconciliation: {reconciliation_metadata}")
        
        # ========== 7. COMPRESSED ARCHIVES FOR LONG-TERM STORAGE ==========
        logger.info("\n7. Creating Long-term Archives")
        
        # Monthly archive with high compression
        monthly_archive = exporter.compressed_export_pattern(
            df=transactions_df,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/archives/transactions/2024-01",
            compression_codec="gzip",
            format="parquet",
            split_size_mb=512
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Monthly archive: {monthly_archive}")
        
        # ========== 8. MULTI-FORMAT FOR DIFFERENT STAKEHOLDERS ==========
        logger.info("\n8. Stakeholder Reports (Multi-format)")
        
        # Summary for different departments
        stakeholder_summary = transactions_df.groupBy("category") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("amount").alias("total"),
                avg("amount").alias("average")
            )
        
        format_options = {
            "parquet": {"compression": "snappy"},  # For data warehouse
            "csv": {"header": "true"},  # For Excel users
            "json": {"pretty": "true"}  # For API consumers
        }
        
        multi_format_results = exporter.multi_format_export_pattern(
            df=stakeholder_summary,
            base_output_path="s3://financial-data/reports/stakeholder_summary",
            formats=["parquet", "csv", "json"],
            format_specific_options=format_options
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Stakeholder reports: {multi_format_results}")
        
        # ========== 9. QUALITY CHECKS FOR REGULATORY COMPLIANCE ==========
        logger.info("\n9. Compliance Quality Checks")
        
        compliance_rules = {
            "valid_transaction_id": "transaction_id IS NOT NULL AND length(transaction_id) = 13",
            "valid_amount": "amount > 0 AND amount < 1000000",
            "valid_date": "transaction_date IS NOT NULL AND transaction_date <= current_timestamp()",
            "valid_type": "transaction_type IN ('debit', 'credit', 'transfer')",
            "valid_category": "category IS NOT NULL",
            "no_future_dates": "transaction_date <= current_timestamp()"
        }
        
        quality_result = advanced_exporter.export_with_data_quality_checks(
            df=transactions_df,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/exports/quality_validated",
            quality_rules=compliance_rules,
            fail_on_quality_issues=True,  # Strict compliance
            format="parquet"
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Quality validation: {quality_result}")
        
        # ========== 10. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZED EXPORT ==========
        logger.info("\n10. Performance Optimized Export")
        
        perf_result = advanced_exporter.export_with_performance_optimization(
            df=transactions_df,
            output_path="s3://financial-data/exports/optimized",
            optimize_for="balanced",
            target_file_size_mb=256,
            enable_statistics=True
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Performance metrics: {perf_result}")
        
        # ========== COMPLIANCE SUMMARY ==========
        logger.info("\n" + "="*70)
        logger.info("FINANCIAL DATA EXPORT COMPLIANCE SUMMARY")
        logger.info("="*70)
        
        summary = f"""
        Compliance Features Implemented:
        ✓ PII Encryption (account_number, SSN)
        ✓ Complete Audit Trail with Lineage Tracking
        ✓ Version Control for All Exports
        ✓ Regulatory Reports (High-value, Suspicious Activity)
        ✓ Delta Lake with Time Travel (7-year retention)
        ✓ Daily Reconciliation Reports
        ✓ Long-term Compressed Archives
        ✓ Multi-format Stakeholder Reports
        ✓ Strict Quality Validation
        ✓ Performance Optimized Exports
        
        Compliance Standards:
        - SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley)
        - PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry)
        - GDPR (Data Protection)
        - Financial Record Retention (7 years)
        
        Security Measures:
        - Encrypted PII fields
        - Audit trail for all operations
        - Version control for data lineage
        - Access logging and monitoring
        
        Total Transactions Processed: {transactions_df.count()}
        Export Locations: s3://financial-data/
        Retention Period: 2555 days (7 years)
        """
        
        logger.info(summary)
        
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Financial data export failed: {str(e)}")
        raise
    finally:
        spark.stop()


def example_iot_sensor_export():
    """
    Real-world example: IoT sensor data export with streaming and partitioning.
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("IoTSensorDataExport") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.streaming.schemaInference", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        logger.info("="*70)
        logger.info("IOT SENSOR DATA EXPORT PIPELINE")
        logger.info("="*70)
        
        exporter = DataExportPatterns(spark)
        
        # ========== 1. BATCH SENSOR DATA ==========
        logger.info("\n1. Processing Batch Sensor Data")
        
        sensor_schema = StructType([
            StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("device_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("location", StringType(), False),
            StructField("temperature", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("humidity", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("pressure", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        sensor_data = [
            (f"SENSOR_{i % 100}", 
             ["temperature", "humidity", "pressure", "multi"][i % 4],
             ["factory_a", "factory_b", "warehouse_c"][i % 3],
             20.0 + (i % 30), 45.0 + (i % 40), 1013.0 + (i % 20),
             datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=i),
             ["active", "inactive", "maintenance"][i % 3])
            for i in range(1, 50001)
        ]
        
        sensor_df = spark.createDataFrame(sensor_data, sensor_schema)
        
        # Partitioned export by location and date
        partition_info = exporter.partitioned_export_pattern(
            df=sensor_df,
            output_path="s3://iot-data/exports/sensors/partitioned",
            partition_columns=["location", "device_type"],
            partition_strategy="dynamic",
            max_records_per_file=10000,
            format="parquet"
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Sensor data partitioned: {partition_info}")
        
        # ========== 2. STREAMING SENSOR DATA ==========
        logger.info("\n2. Processing Streaming Sensor Data")
        
        # Simulate streaming sensor data
        streaming_sensors = spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 1000) \
            .load() \
            .selectExpr(
                "CONCAT('SENSOR_', CAST(value % 100 AS STRING)) as sensor_id",
```python
                "CASE WHEN value % 4 = 0 THEN 'temperature' " +
                "     WHEN value % 4 = 1 THEN 'humidity' " +
                "     WHEN value % 4 = 2 THEN 'pressure' " +
                "     ELSE 'multi' END as device_type",
                "CASE WHEN value % 3 = 0 THEN 'factory_a' " +
                "     WHEN value % 3 = 1 THEN 'factory_b' " +
                "     ELSE 'warehouse_c' END as location",
                "20.0 + (value % 30) as temperature",
                "45.0 + (value % 40) as humidity",
                "1013.0 + (value % 20) as pressure",
                "timestamp",
                "CASE WHEN value % 3 = 0 THEN 'active' " +
                "     WHEN value % 3 = 1 THEN 'inactive' " +
                "     ELSE 'maintenance' END as status"
            )
        
        # Start streaming export with partitioning
        streaming_query = exporter.streaming_export_pattern(
            streaming_df=streaming_sensors,
            output_path="s3://iot-data/exports/sensors/streaming",
            checkpoint_location="s3://iot-data/checkpoints/sensors",
            trigger_interval="10 seconds",
            output_mode="append",
            partition_by=["location", "device_type"]
        )
        
        logger.info("Streaming sensor export started")
        
        # Run for 2 minutes
        streaming_query.awaitTermination(120)
        streaming_query.stop()
        
        # ========== 3. HOURLY AGGREGATIONS ==========
        logger.info("\n3. Creating Hourly Aggregations")
        
        # Add hour column
        sensor_df_with_hour = sensor_df.withColumn(
            "hour", hour(col("timestamp"))
        ).withColumn(
            "date", to_date(col("timestamp"))
        )
        
        # Hourly aggregations
        hourly_agg = sensor_df_with_hour.groupBy(
            "date", "hour", "location", "device_type"
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("reading_count"),
            avg("temperature").alias("avg_temperature"),
            max("temperature").alias("max_temperature"),
            min("temperature").alias("min_temperature"),
            avg("humidity").alias("avg_humidity"),
            avg("pressure").alias("avg_pressure"),
            countDistinct("sensor_id").alias("active_sensors")
        )
        
        # Export hourly aggregations
        hourly_metadata = exporter.scheduled_export_pattern(
            df=hourly_agg,
            output_base_path="s3://iot-data/aggregations/hourly",
            schedule_type="hourly",
            format="parquet",
            retention_days=30,
            partition_by_time=True
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Hourly aggregations: {hourly_metadata}")
        
        # ========== 4. ANOMALY DETECTION EXPORTS ==========
        logger.info("\n4. Exporting Anomaly Data")
        
        # Detect anomalies (temperature outside normal range)
        anomalies = sensor_df.filter(
            (col("temperature") < 15) | (col("temperature") > 35) |
            (col("humidity") < 20) | (col("humidity") > 80)
        ).withColumn("anomaly_type", 
            when((col("temperature") < 15) | (col("temperature") > 35), "temperature")
            .when((col("humidity") < 20) | (col("humidity") > 80), "humidity")
            .otherwise("other")
        ).withColumn("severity",
            when((col("temperature") < 10) | (col("temperature") > 40), "critical")
            .when((col("humidity") < 15) | (col("humidity") > 85), "critical")
            .otherwise("warning")
        )
        
        # Export anomalies for immediate attention
        exporter.selective_export_pattern(
            df=anomalies,
            output_path="s3://iot-data/alerts/anomalies",
            select_columns=[
                "sensor_id", "device_type", "location", "temperature",
                "humidity", "timestamp", "anomaly_type", "severity"
            ],
            format="parquet"
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Anomalies detected and exported: {anomalies.count()}")
        
        # ========== 5. COMPRESSED HISTORICAL DATA ==========
        logger.info("\n5. Creating Compressed Historical Archives")
        
        # Archive old data with high compression
        historical_data = sensor_df.filter(
            col("timestamp") < (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=30))
        )
        
        archive_result = exporter.compressed_export_pattern(
            df=historical_data,
            output_path="s3://iot-data/archives/sensors/historical",
            compression_codec="gzip",
            format="parquet",
            split_size_mb=256
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Historical archive: {archive_result}")
        
        # ========== IOT SUMMARY ==========
        logger.info("\n" + "="*70)
        logger.info("IOT SENSOR DATA EXPORT SUMMARY")
        logger.info("="*70)
        
        summary = f"""
        IoT Data Processing:
        ✓ Batch Sensor Data: {sensor_df.count()} readings
        ✓ Streaming Export: 2 minutes of real-time data
        ✓ Hourly Aggregations: Time-series analytics
        ✓ Anomaly Detection: {anomalies.count()} anomalies detected
        ✓ Historical Archives: Compressed long-term storage
        
        Partitioning Strategy:
        - Location-based partitioning
        - Device type partitioning
        - Time-based partitioning (hourly)
        
        Data Retention:
        - Real-time data: 30 days
        - Aggregations: 90 days
        - Archives: Indefinite (compressed)
        
        Sensor Metrics:
        - Total Sensors: 100
        - Locations: 3 (factory_a, factory_b, warehouse_c)
        - Device Types: 4 (temperature, humidity, pressure, multi)
        - Reading Frequency: 1000/second (streaming)
        """
        
        logger.info(summary)
        
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"IoT sensor export failed: {str(e)}")
        raise
    finally:
        spark.stop()


# ==================== AIRFLOW DAG EXAMPLE ====================

def create_airflow_export_dag():
    """
    Example Apache Airflow DAG for scheduled exports.
    This demonstrates how to integrate export patterns with Airflow.
    """
    
    airflow_dag_code = '''
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.providers.apache.spark.operators.spark_submit import SparkSubmitOperator
from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# Default arguments
default_args = {
    'owner': 'data-engineering',
    'depends_on_past': False,
    'start_date': datetime(2024, 1, 1),
    'email': ['data-team@company.com'],
    'email_on_failure': True,
    'email_on_retry': False,
    'retries': 3,
    'retry_delay': timedelta(minutes=5),
}

# Create DAG
dag = DAG(
    'data_export_pipeline',
    default_args=default_args,
    description='Daily data export pipeline',
    schedule_interval='0 2 * * *',  # 2 AM daily
    catchup=False,
    tags=['export', 'data-lake']
)

# Task 1: Full export of customers
export_customers = SparkSubmitOperator(
    task_id='export_customers',
    application='/path/to/export_script.py',
    name='export_customers',
    conf={
        'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'true',
        'spark.executor.memory': '4g',
        'spark.executor.cores': '2'
    },
    application_args=[
        '--export-type', 'full',
        '--table', 'customers',
        '--output-path', 's3://data-lake/exports/customers/{{ ds }}',
        '--format', 'parquet'
    ],
    dag=dag
)

# Task 2: Incremental export of orders
export_orders = SparkSubmitOperator(
    task_id='export_orders',
    application='/path/to/export_script.py',
    name='export_orders',
    conf={
        'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'true',
        'spark.executor.memory': '4g'
    },
    application_args=[
        '--export-type', 'incremental',
        '--table', 'orders',
        '--output-path', 's3://data-lake/exports/orders/{{ ds }}',
        '--watermark-column', 'order_date',
        '--checkpoint-path', 's3://data-lake/checkpoints/orders'
    ],
    dag=dag
)

# Task 3: Multi-format export of products
export_products = SparkSubmitOperator(
    task_id='export_products',
    application='/path/to/export_script.py',
    name='export_products',
    application_args=[
        '--export-type', 'multi-format',
        '--table', 'products',
        '--output-path', 's3://data-lake/exports/products/{{ ds }}',
        '--formats', 'parquet,csv,json'
    ],
    dag=dag
)

# Task 4: Data quality validation
def validate_exports(**context):
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("ValidationTask").getOrCreate()
    
    # Validate customer export
    customers_df = spark.read.parquet(
        f"s3://data-lake/exports/customers/{context['ds']}"
    )
    customer_count = customers_df.count()
    
    if customer_count == 0:
        raise ValueError("Customer export is empty!")
    
    print(f"Validation passed: {customer_count} customers exported")
    spark.stop()

validate_task = PythonOperator(
    task_id='validate_exports',
    python_callable=validate_exports,
    provide_context=True,
    dag=dag
)

# Task 5: Send notification
def send_completion_notification(**context):
    import requests
    
    slack_webhook = "https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK"
    
    message = {
        "text": f"Daily export completed successfully for {context['ds']}",
        "attachments": [{
            "color": "good",
            "fields": [
                {"title": "Date", "value": context['ds'], "short": True},
                {"title": "Status", "value": "Success", "short": True}
            ]
        }]
    }
    
    requests.post(slack_webhook, json=message)

notify_task = PythonOperator(
    task_id='send_notification',
    python_callable=send_completion_notification,
    provide_context=True,
    dag=dag
)

# Define task dependencies
export_customers >> validate_task
export_orders >> validate_task
export_products >> validate_task
validate_task >> notify_task
'''
    
    return airflow_dag_code


# ==================== KUBERNETES DEPLOYMENT EXAMPLE ====================

def create_kubernetes_deployment():
    """
    Example Kubernetes deployment for export jobs.
    """
    
    k8s_deployment = '''
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-export-job
  namespace: data-engineering
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"  # 2 AM daily
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
          - name: spark-export
            image: your-registry/spark-export:latest
            env:
            - name: SPARK_MASTER
              value: "k8s://https://kubernetes.default.svc:443"
            - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: aws-credentials
                  key: access-key-id
            - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: aws-credentials
                  key: secret-access-key
            command:
            - /opt/spark/bin/spark-submit
            - --master
            - k8s://https://kubernetes.default.svc:443
            - --deploy-mode
            - cluster
            - --name
            - data-export-job
            - --conf
            - spark.executor.instances=5
            - --conf
            - spark.executor.memory=4g
            - --conf
            - spark.executor.cores=2
            - --conf
            - spark.kubernetes.container.image=your-registry/spark:3.4.0
            - --conf
            - spark.kubernetes.authenticate.driver.serviceAccountName=spark
            - /app/export_script.py
            - --export-type
            - full
            - --output-path
            - s3://data-lake/exports/
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "2Gi"
                cpu: "1"
              limits:
                memory: "4Gi"
                cpu: "2"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: spark
  namespace: data-engineering
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: spark-role
  namespace: data-engineering
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "services", "configmaps"]
  verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "delete"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: spark-role-binding
  namespace: data-engineering
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: spark
  namespace: data-engineering
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: spark-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
'''
    
    return k8s_deployment

# ==================== TESTING UTILITIES ====================

class ExportPatternTester:
    """
    Unit testing utilities for export patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.exporter = DataExportPatterns(spark)
    
    def test_full_export(self) -> bool:
        """Test full export pattern."""
        try:
            logger.info("Testing full export pattern...")
            
            # Create test data
            test_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                [(1, "test", 100.0)],
                ["id", "name", "value"]
            )
            
            # Export
            self.exporter.full_export_pattern(
                df=test_df,
                output_path="/tmp/test_exports/full",
                format="parquet"
            )
            
            # Verify
            result_df = self.spark.read.parquet("/tmp/test_exports/full")
            assert result_df.count() == 1
            
            logger.info("✓ Full export test passed")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"✗ Full export test failed: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    def test_incremental_export(self) -> bool:
        """Test incremental export pattern."""
        try:
            logger.info("Testing incremental export pattern...")
            
            # Create test data with timestamps
            test_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                [(1, "test1", datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=2)),
                 (2, "test2", datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=1)),
                 (3, "test3", datetime.now())],
                ["id", "name", "timestamp"]
            )
            
            # First export
            watermark1 = self.exporter.incremental_export_pattern(
                df=test_df,
                output_path="/tmp/test_exports/incremental",
                watermark_column="timestamp",
                last_export_value=None
            )
            
            # Second export with watermark
            watermark2 = self.exporter.incremental_export_pattern(
                df=test_df,
                output_path="/tmp/test_exports/incremental",
                watermark_column="timestamp",
                last_export_value=watermark1
            )
            
            logger.info("✓ Incremental export test passed")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"✗ Incremental export test failed: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    def test_selective_export(self) -> bool:
        """Test selective export pattern."""
        try:
            logger.info("Testing selective export pattern...")
            
            # Create test data
            test_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                [(1, "test1", 100.0, "active"),
                 (2, "test2", 200.0, "inactive"),
                 (3, "test3", 300.0, "active")],
                ["id", "name", "value", "status"]
            )
            
            # Selective export
            self.exporter.selective_export_pattern(
                df=test_df,
                output_path="/tmp/test_exports/selective",
                filter_conditions="status = 'active'",
                select_columns=["id", "name", "value"]
            )
            
            # Verify
            result_df = self.spark.read.parquet("/tmp/test_exports/selective")
            assert result_df.count() == 2
            assert len(result_df.columns) == 4  # 3 selected + export_type
            
            logger.info("✓ Selective export test passed")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"✗ Selective export test failed: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    def test_partitioned_export(self) -> bool:
        """Test partitioned export pattern."""
        try:
            logger.info("Testing partitioned export pattern...")
            
            # Create test data
            test_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                [(1, "A", "X"), (2, "A", "Y"), (3, "B", "X"), (4, "B", "Y")],
                ["id", "category", "region"]
            )
            
            # Partitioned export
            partition_info = self.exporter.partitioned_export_pattern(
                df=test_df,
                output_path="/tmp/test_exports/partitioned",
                partition_columns=["category", "region"]
            )
            
            assert partition_info["total_partitions"] == 4
            
            logger.info("✓ Partitioned export test passed")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"✗ Partitioned export test failed: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    def test_compressed_export(self) -> bool:
        """Test compressed export pattern."""
        try:
            logger.info("Testing compressed export pattern...")
            
            # Create test data
            test_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                [(i, f"test_{i}", i * 100.0) for i in range(1000)],
                ["id", "name", "value"]
            )
            
            # Compressed export

## 1. Bulk Import Pattern

```python
"""
Bulk Import Pattern
Purpose: Import large volumes of data in a single operation with optimization
Use Case: One-time data migration, historical data loading
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, TimestampType
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp, lit
from typing import Dict, List, Optional
import logging

class BulkImporter:
    """
    Handles bulk data import operations with optimization and monitoring
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        
    def import_bulk_data(
        self,
        source_path: str,
        target_path: str,
        file_format: str = "parquet",
        partition_columns: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        num_partitions: int = 200,
        options: Optional[Dict] = None
    ):
        """
        Import data in bulk with optimizations
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source data location
            target_path: Target data location
            file_format: Format of source files (parquet, csv, json, etc.)
            partition_columns: Columns to partition by
            num_partitions: Number of partitions for processing
            options: Additional read options
        """
        try:
            self.logger.info(f"Starting bulk import from {source_path}")
            
            # Configure Spark for bulk operations
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
            
            # Read data with optimizations
            read_options = options or {}
            df = self.spark.read.format(file_format).options(**read_options).load(source_path)
            
            # Add metadata columns
            df = df.withColumn("import_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
                   .withColumn("source_file", lit(source_path))
            
            # Repartition for optimal processing
            df = df.repartition(num_partitions)
            
            # Get statistics
            total_records = df.count()
            self.logger.info(f"Total records to import: {total_records}")
            
            # Write data with partitioning
            writer = df.write.mode("overwrite").format("parquet")
            
            if partition_columns:
                writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_columns)
            
            writer.save(target_path)
            
            self.logger.info(f"Bulk import completed. Records imported: {total_records}")
            
            return {
                "status": "success",
                "records_imported": total_records,
                "target_path": target_path
            }
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Bulk import failed: {str(e)}")
            raise

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("BulkImportPattern") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    bulk_importer = BulkImporter(spark)
    
    # Example: Import CSV data in bulk
    result = bulk_importer.import_bulk_data(
        source_path="s3://data-lake/raw/sales/*.csv",
        target_path="s3://data-lake/processed/sales",
        file_format="csv",
        partition_columns=["year", "month"],
        num_partitions=200,
        options={"header": "true", "inferSchema": "true"}
    )
    
    print(f"Import Result: {result}")

## 2. Streaming Import Pattern

```python
"""
Streaming Import Pattern
Purpose: Continuously import data in real-time or micro-batches
Use Case: Real-time data ingestion, event streaming, CDC
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import from_json, col, current_timestamp, window
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
from pyspark.sql.streaming import StreamingQuery
import logging

class StreamingImporter:
    """
    Handles streaming data import with checkpointing and fault tolerance
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        self.active_streams: Dict[str, StreamingQuery] = {}
        
    def import_streaming_data(
        self,
        source_type: str,
        source_config: Dict,
        target_path: str,
        checkpoint_location: str,
        schema: Optional[StructType] = None,
        trigger_interval: str = "10 seconds",
        watermark_column: Optional[str] = None,
        watermark_threshold: str = "10 minutes"
    ):
        """
        Import streaming data with fault tolerance
        
        Args:
            source_type: Type of source (kafka, socket, file, etc.)
            source_config: Configuration for the source
            target_path: Target location for streaming data
            checkpoint_location: Checkpoint directory for fault tolerance
            schema: Schema for the incoming data
            trigger_interval: Micro-batch trigger interval
            watermark_column: Column for watermarking
            watermark_threshold: Watermark threshold for late data
        """
        try:
            self.logger.info(f"Starting streaming import from {source_type}")
            
            # Read streaming data based on source type
            if source_type == "kafka":
                stream_df = self.spark.readStream \
                    .format("kafka") \
                    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", source_config["bootstrap_servers"]) \
                    .option("subscribe", source_config["topic"]) \
                    .option("startingOffsets", source_config.get("starting_offsets", "latest")) \
                    .load()
                
                # Parse JSON data if schema provided
                if schema:
                    stream_df = stream_df.select(
                        from_json(col("value").cast("string"), schema).alias("data")
                    ).select("data.*")
                    
            elif source_type == "file":
                stream_df = self.spark.readStream \
                    .format(source_config.get("format", "json")) \
                    .schema(schema) \
                    .option("maxFilesPerTrigger", source_config.get("max_files", 1)) \
                    .load(source_config["path"])
                    
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported source type: {source_type}")
            
            # Add metadata
            stream_df = stream_df.withColumn("ingestion_time", current_timestamp())
            
            # Apply watermarking if specified
            if watermark_column:
                stream_df = stream_df.withWatermark(watermark_column, watermark_threshold)
            
            # Write streaming data
            query = stream_df.writeStream \
                .format("parquet") \
                .outputMode("append") \
                .option("path", target_path) \
                .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_location) \
                .trigger(processingTime=trigger_interval) \
                .start()
            
            stream_name = f"stream_{source_type}_{len(self.active_streams)}"
            self.active_streams[stream_name] = query
            
            self.logger.info(f"Streaming import started: {stream_name}")
            
            return query
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Streaming import failed: {str(e)}")
            raise
    
    def stop_all_streams(self):
        """Stop all active streaming queries"""
        for name, query in self.active_streams.items():
            self.logger.info(f"Stopping stream: {name}")
            query.stop()
        self.active_streams.clear()

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("StreamingImportPattern") \
        .config("spark.sql.streaming.checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoints") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    streaming_importer = StreamingImporter(spark)
    
    # Define schema for incoming data
    event_schema = StructType([

        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Example 1: Kafka streaming import
    kafka_config = {
        "bootstrap_servers": "localhost:9092",

    kafka_query = streaming_importer.import_streaming_data(

        source_config=kafka_config,
        target_path="s3://data-lake/streaming/events",

    # Example 2: File-based streaming import

## 3. Scheduled Import Pattern

```python
"""
Scheduled Import Pattern
Purpose: Import data on a regular schedule (hourly, daily, weekly, etc.)
Use Case: Regular batch processing, ETL jobs, reporting data loads
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp, lit, to_date
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Callable
import logging
import time

class ScheduledImporter:
    """
    Handles scheduled data imports with dependency management and retry logic
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        self.import_history = []
        
    def import_scheduled_data(
        self,
        job_name: str,
        source_path_template: str,
        target_path_template: str,
        schedule_params: Dict,
        transformation_func: Optional[Callable] = None,
        max_retries: int = 3,
        retry_delay: int = 60
    ):
        """
        Import data based on schedule parameters
        
        Args:
            job_name: Name of the scheduled job
            source_path_template: Source path with date placeholders
            target_path_template: Target path with date placeholders
            schedule_params: Schedule parameters (date, hour, etc.)
            transformation_func: Optional transformation function
            max_retries: Maximum number of retries on failure
            retry_delay: Delay between retries in seconds
        """
        try:
            start_time = datetime.now()
            self.logger.info(f"Starting scheduled import: {job_name}")
            
            # Format paths with schedule parameters
            source_path = source_path_template.format(**schedule_params)
            target_path = target_path_template.format(**schedule_params)
            
            retry_count = 0
            success = False
            
            while retry_count < max_retries and not success:
                try:
                    # Read data
                    df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
                    
                    # Add scheduling metadata
                    df = df.withColumn("import_job", lit(job_name)) \
                           .withColumn("import_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
                           .withColumn("schedule_date", lit(schedule_params.get("date"))) \
                           .withColumn("schedule_hour", lit(schedule_params.get("hour")))
                    
                    # Apply custom transformation if provided
                    if transformation_func:
                        df = transformation_func(df)
                    
                    # Validate data
                    record_count = df.count()
                    
                    if record_count == 0:
                        self.logger.warning(f"No records found for {source_path}")
                    
                    # Write data
                    df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(target_path)
                    
                    success = True
                    
                    # Log success
                    execution_time = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds()
                    import_record = {
                        "job_name": job_name,
                        "schedule_params": schedule_params,
                        "source_path": source_path,
                        "target_path": target_path,
                        "record_count": record_count,
                        "status": "success",
                        "execution_time": execution_time,
                        "timestamp": datetime.now()
                    }
                    self.import_history.append(import_record)
                    
                    self.logger.info(f"Scheduled import completed: {job_name}, Records: {record_count}")
                    
                    return import_record
                    
                except Exception as e:
                    retry_count += 1
                    self.logger.warning(f"Attempt {retry_count} failed: {str(e)}")
                    
                    if retry_count < max_retries:
                        self.logger.info(f"Retrying in {retry_delay} seconds...")
                        time.sleep(retry_delay)
                    else:
                        raise
                        
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Scheduled import failed: {str(e)}")
            import_record = {
                "job_name": job_name,
                "schedule_params": schedule_params,
                "status": "failed",
                "error": str(e),
                "timestamp": datetime.now()
            }
            self.import_history.append(import_record)
            raise
    
    def import_date_range(
        self,
        job_name: str,
        source_path_template: str,
        target_path_template: str,
        start_date: datetime,
        end_date: datetime,
        transformation_func: Optional[Callable] = None
    ):
        """
        Import data for a date range
        """
        current_date = start_date
        results = []
        
        while current_date <= end_date:
            schedule_params = {
                "date": current_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
                "year": current_date.strftime("%Y"),
                "month": current_date.strftime("%m"),
                "day": current_date.strftime("%d")
            }
            
            try:
                result = self.import_scheduled_data(
                    job_name=f"{job_name}_{schedule_params['date']}",
                    source_path_template=source_path_template,
                    target_path_template=target_path_template,
                    schedule_params=schedule_params,
                    transformation_
```python
                    transformation_func=transformation_func
                )
                results.append(result)
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.error(f"Failed to import data for {schedule_params['date']}: {str(e)}")
                results.append({"date": schedule_params['date'], "status": "failed", "error": str(e)})
            
            current_date += timedelta(days=1)
        
        return results
    
    def get_import_history(self):
        """Return import history as DataFrame"""
        if self.import_history:
            return self.spark.createDataFrame(self.import_history)
        return None

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("ScheduledImportPattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    scheduled_importer = ScheduledImporter(spark)
    
    # Define custom transformation
    def daily_aggregation(df):
        """Example transformation: daily aggregation"""
        from pyspark.sql.functions import sum as _sum, avg, count
        return df.groupBy("category").agg(
            _sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
            count("*").alias("transaction_count")
        )
    
    # Example 1: Single scheduled import
    schedule_params = {
        "date": "2024-01-15",
        "year": "2024",
        "month": "01",
        "day": "15"
    }
    
    result = scheduled_importer.import_scheduled_data(
        job_name="daily_sales_import",
        source_path_template="s3://data-lake/raw/sales/year={year}/month={month}/day={day}",
        target_path_template="s3://data-lake/processed/sales/date={date}",
        schedule_params=schedule_params,
        transformation_func=daily_aggregation,
        max_retries=3,
        retry_delay=60
    )
    
    # Example 2: Date range import
    start_date = datetime(2024, 1, 1)
    end_date = datetime(2024, 1, 7)
    
    range_results = scheduled_importer.import_date_range(

        target_path_template="s3://data-lake/processed/sales/date={date}",
        start_date=start_date,
        end_date=end_date,

    # View import history

    if history_df:

## 4. On-demand Import Pattern

```python
"""
On-demand Import Pattern
Purpose: Import data triggered by user requests or specific events
Use Case: Ad-hoc data loads, user-initiated imports, event-driven imports
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp, lit
from typing import Dict, List, Optional
import logging
import uuid
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

class ImportPriority(Enum):
    """Priority levels for on-demand imports"""
    LOW = 1
    MEDIUM = 2
    HIGH = 3
    CRITICAL = 4

class ImportStatus(Enum):
    """Status of import jobs"""
    PENDING = "pending"
    RUNNING = "running"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

class OnDemandImporter:
    """
    Handles on-demand data imports with job queuing and priority management
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        self.job_queue = []
        self.job_history = {}
        
    def submit_import_job(
        self,
        source_path: str,
        target_path: str,
        file_format: str = "parquet",
        priority: ImportPriority = ImportPriority.MEDIUM,
        user_id: Optional[str] = None,
        filters: Optional[Dict] = None,
        transformations: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        options: Optional[Dict] = None
    ) -> str:
        """
        Submit an on-demand import job
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source data location
            target_path: Target data location
            file_format: Format of source files
            priority: Job priority
            user_id: User who submitted the job
            filters: Filters to apply during import
            transformations: List of transformations to apply
            options: Additional options
            
        Returns:
            job_id: Unique identifier for the job
        """
        job_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        
        job_config = {
            "job_id": job_id,
            "source_path": source_path,
            "target_path": target_path,
            "file_format": file_format,
            "priority": priority,
            "user_id": user_id,
            "filters": filters or {},
            "transformations": transformations or [],
            "options": options or {},
            "status": ImportStatus.PENDING,
            "submitted_at": datetime.now(),
            "started_at": None,
            "completed_at": None,
            "error": None
        }
        
        # Add to queue based on priority
        self.job_queue.append(job_config)
        self.job_queue.sort(key=lambda x: x["priority"].value, reverse=True)
        
        self.logger.info(f"Import job submitted: {job_id} with priority {priority.name}")
        
        return job_id
    
    def execute_import_job(self, job_id: str):
        """
        Execute a specific import job
        
        Args:
            job_id: ID of the job to execute
        """
        # Find job in queue
        job_config = None
        for idx, job in enumerate(self.job_queue):
            if job["job_id"] == job_id:
                job_config = self.job_queue.pop(idx)
                break
        
        if not job_config:
            raise ValueError(f"Job {job_id} not found in queue")
        
        try:
            self.logger.info(f"Executing import job: {job_id}")
            job_config["status"] = ImportStatus.RUNNING
            job_config["started_at"] = datetime.now()
            
            # Read data
            read_options = job_config["options"]
            df = self.spark.read.format(job_config["file_format"]) \
                .options(**read_options) \
                .load(job_config["source_path"])
            
            # Apply filters if specified
            if job_config["filters"]:
                for column, value in job_config["filters"].items():
                    if isinstance(value, list):
                        df = df.filter(col(column).isin(value))
                    else:
                        df = df.filter(col(column) == value)
            
            # Apply transformations
            for transformation in job_config["transformations"]:
                if transformation == "deduplicate":
                    df = df.dropDuplicates()
                elif transformation == "remove_nulls":
                    df = df.na.drop()
                # Add more transformations as needed
            
            # Add metadata
            df = df.withColumn("import_job_id", lit(job_id)) \
                   .withColumn("import_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
                   .withColumn("imported_by", lit(job_config["user_id"]))
            
            # Get record count
            record_count = df.count()
            
            # Write data
            df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(job_config["target_path"])
            
            # Update job status
            job_config["status"] = ImportStatus.COMPLETED
            job_config["completed_at"] = datetime.now()
            job_config["record_count"] = record_count
            
            execution_time = (job_config["completed_at"] - job_config["started_at"]).total_seconds()
            
            self.logger.info(f"Import job completed: {job_id}, Records: {record_count}, Time: {execution_time}s")
            
            # Store in history
            self.job_history[job_id] = job_config
            
            return {
                "job_id": job_id,
                "status": "completed",
                "record_count": record_count,
                "execution_time": execution_time
            }
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Import job failed: {job_id}, Error: {str(e)}")
            job_config["status"] = ImportStatus.FAILED
            job_config["completed_at"] = datetime.now()
            job_config["error"] = str(e)
            self.job_history[job_id] = job_config
            raise
    
    def execute_next_job(self):
        """Execute the next job in the queue based on priority"""
        if not self.job_queue:
            self.logger.info("No jobs in queue")
            return None
        
        next_job = self.job_queue[0]
        return self.execute_import_job(next_job["job_id"])
    
    def get_job_status(self, job_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Get status of a specific job"""
        # Check queue
        for job in self.job_queue:
            if job["job_id"] == job_id:
                return {
                    "job_id": job_id,
                    "status": job["status"].value,
                    "position_in_queue": self.job_queue.index(job) + 1
                }
        
        # Check history
        if job_id in self.job_history:
            job = self.job_history[job_id]
            return {
                "job_id": job_id,
                "status": job["status"].value,
                "record_count": job.get("record_count"),
                "error": job.get("error")
            }
        
        return {"job_id": job_id, "status": "not_found"}
    
    def cancel_job(self, job_id: str):
        """Cancel a pending job"""
        for idx, job in enumerate(self.job_queue):
            if job["job_id"] == job_id:
                job["status"] = ImportStatus.CANCELLED
                cancelled_job = self.job_queue.pop(idx)
                self.job_history[job_id] = cancelled_job
                self.logger.info(f"Job cancelled: {job_id}")
                return True
        return False

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("OnDemandImportPattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    on_demand_importer = OnDemandImporter(spark)
    
    # Example 1: Submit high priority import job
    job_id_1 = on_demand_importer.submit_import_job(
        source_path="s3://data-lake/raw/urgent_data/*.parquet",

        user_id="user123",

    # Example 2: Submit normal priority import job

    print(f"Next Job Result: {result_2}")

## 5. Auto-discovery Import Pattern

```python
"""
Auto-discovery Import Pattern
Purpose: Automatically discover and import new data files as they arrive
Use Case: Continuous data ingestion, file monitoring, auto-detection
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp, lit, input_file_name
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
import logging
import os
from datetime import datetime
import json

class AutoDiscoveryImporter:
    """
    Automatically discovers and imports new data files
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        self.processed_files: Set[str] = set()
        self.file_registry_path = None
        
    def load_file_registry(self, registry_path: str):
        """Load registry of already processed files"""
        self.file_registry_path = registry_path
        try:
            if os.path.exists(registry_path):
                with open(registry_path, 'r') as f:
                    self.processed_files = set(json.load(f))
                self.logger.info(f"Loaded {len(self.processed_files)} processed files from registry")
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.warning(f"Could not load file registry: {str(e)}")
    
    def save_file_registry(self):
        """Save registry of processed files"""
        if self.file_registry_path:
            try:
                with open(self.file_registry_path, 'w') as f:
                    json.dump(list(self.processed_files), f)
                self.logger.info(f"Saved {len(self.processed_files)} files to registry")
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.error(f"Could not save file registry: {str(e)}")
    
    def discover_new_files(
        self,
        source_path: str,
        file_pattern: str = "*",
        file_format: str = "parquet",
        recursive: bool = True
    ) -> List[str]:
        """
        Discover new files in the source path
        
        Args:
            source_path: Base path to search for files
            file_pattern: Pattern to match files (e.g., "*.parquet")
            file_format: Expected file format
            recursive: Whether to search recursively
            
        Returns:
            List of new file paths
        """
        try:
            # Build search path
            search_path = os.path.join(source_path, "**" if recursive else "", file_pattern)
            
            # List all files
            try:
                # For cloud storage, use Spark to list files
                temp_df = self.spark.read.format(file_format).load(search_path)
                all_files = [row.path for row in temp_df.select(input_file_name().alias("path")).distinct().collect()]
            except:
                # Fallback to local file system
                import glob
                all_
```python
                all_files = glob.glob(search_path, recursive=recursive)
            
            # Filter out already processed files
            new_files = [f for f in all_files if f not in self.processed_files]
            
            self.logger.info(f"Discovered {len(new_files)} new files out of {len(all_files)} total files")
            
            return new_files
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Error discovering files: {str(e)}")
            return []
    
    def auto_detect_schema(
        self,
        file_path: str,
        file_format: str = "parquet",
        sample_size: int = 1000
    ) -> Optional[StructType]:
        """
        Automatically detect schema from a sample file
        
        Args:
            file_path: Path to sample file
            file_format: Format of the file
            sample_size: Number of rows to sample for schema detection
            
        Returns:
            Detected schema
        """
        try:
            if file_format == "csv":
                df = self.spark.read.format("csv") \
                    .option("header", "true") \
                    .option("inferSchema", "true") \
                    .load(file_path) \
                    .limit(sample_size)
            else:
                df = self.spark.read.format(file_format).load(file_path).limit(sample_size)
            
            schema = df.schema
            self.logger.info(f"Auto-detected schema with {len(schema.fields)} fields")
            
            return schema
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Error detecting schema: {str(e)}")
            return None
    
    def import_discovered_files(
        self,
        source_path: str,
        target_path: str,
        file_pattern: str = "*",
        file_format: str = "parquet",
        partition_columns: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        auto_schema: bool = True,
        max_files_per_batch: int = 100,
        options: Optional[Dict] = None
    ) -> Dict:
        """
        Import newly discovered files
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source directory to monitor
            target_path: Target directory for imported data
            file_pattern: Pattern to match files
            file_format: Format of files
            partition_columns: Columns to partition by
            auto_schema: Whether to auto-detect schema
            max_files_per_batch: Maximum files to process in one batch
            options: Additional read options
            
        Returns:
            Import statistics
        """
        try:
            start_time = datetime.now()
            
            # Discover new files
            new_files = self.discover_new_files(
                source_path=source_path,
                file_pattern=file_pattern,
                file_format=file_format
            )
            
            if not new_files:
                self.logger.info("No new files to import")
                return {
                    "status": "success",
                    "files_discovered": 0,
                    "files_imported": 0,
                    "records_imported": 0
                }
            
            # Limit batch size
            files_to_process = new_files[:max_files_per_batch]
            
            # Auto-detect schema if needed
            schema = None
            if auto_schema and files_to_process:
                schema = self.auto_detect_schema(files_to_process[0], file_format)
            
            # Read new files
            read_options = options or {}
            reader = self.spark.read.format(file_format).options(**read_options)
            
            if schema:
                reader = reader.schema(schema)
            
            # Process files in batch
            dfs = []
            for file_path in files_to_process:
                try:
                    df = reader.load(file_path)
                    
                    # Add file metadata
                    df = df.withColumn("source_file", lit(file_path)) \
                           .withColumn("import_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
                           .withColumn("discovery_batch", lit(start_time.isoformat()))
                    
                    dfs.append(df)
                    
                except Exception as e:
                    self.logger.warning(f"Failed to read file {file_path}: {str(e)}")
                    continue
            
            if not dfs:
                self.logger.warning("No files could be read successfully")
                return {
                    "status": "partial_failure",
                    "files_discovered": len(new_files),
                    "files_imported": 0,
                    "records_imported": 0
                }
            
            # Union all dataframes
            combined_df = dfs[0]
            for df in dfs[1:]:
                combined_df = combined_df.union(df)
            
            # Get record count
            record_count = combined_df.count()
            
            # Write data
            writer = combined_df.write.mode("append").format("parquet")
            
            if partition_columns:
                writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_columns)
            
            writer.save(target_path)
            
            # Update processed files registry
            self.processed_files.update(files_to_process)
            self.save_file_registry()
            
            execution_time = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds()
            
            result = {
                "status": "success",
                "files_discovered": len(new_files),
                "files_imported": len(files_to_process),
                "records_imported": record_count,
                "execution_time": execution_time,
                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
            }
            
            self.logger.info(f"Auto-discovery import completed: {result}")
            
            return result
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Auto-discovery import failed: {str(e)}")
            raise
    
    def continuous_discovery(
        self,
        source_path: str,
        target_path: str,
        file_pattern: str = "*",
        file_format: str = "parquet",
        check_interval: int = 60,
        max_iterations: Optional[int] = None
    ):
        """
        Continuously monitor and import new files
        
        Args:
            source_path: Source directory to monitor
            target_path: Target directory
            file_pattern: File pattern to match
            file_format: File format
            check_interval: Seconds between checks
            max_iterations: Maximum iterations (None for infinite)
        """
        import time
        
        iteration = 0
        self.logger.info(f"Starting continuous discovery mode, checking every {check_interval}s")
        
        while max_iterations is None or iteration < max_iterations:
            try:
                result = self.import_discovered_files(
                    source_path=source_path,
                    target_path=target_path,
                    file_pattern=file_pattern,
                    file_format=file_format
                )
                
                self.logger.info(f"Iteration {iteration + 1}: {result['files_imported']} files imported")
                
                iteration += 1
                time.sleep(check_interval)
                
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                self.logger.info("Continuous discovery stopped by user")
                break
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.error(f"Error in continuous discovery: {str(e)}")
                time.sleep(check_interval)

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("AutoDiscoveryImportPattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    auto_importer = AutoDiscoveryImporter(spark)
    
    # Load file registry
    auto_importer.load_file_registry("/tmp/processed_files_registry.json")
    
    # Example 1: One-time auto-discovery import
    result = auto_importer.import_discovered_files(
        source_path="s3://data-lake/incoming/",
        target_path="s3://data-lake/processed/auto_imported",
        file_pattern="*.parquet",
        file_format="parquet",
        partition_columns=["year", "month"],
        auto_schema=True,
        max_files_per_batch=50
    )
    
    print(f"Import Result: {result}")
    
    # Example 2: Continuous discovery mode

    #     file_format="json",
    #     check_interval=300,  # Check every 5 minutes
    #     max_iterations=None  # Run indefinitely
    # )
