# TESTING AND VALIDATION
# ==================================================================================

class RateLimitingValidator:
    """
    Validates rate limiting implementations for correctness.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_fixed_window(df_limited, window_seconds: int, max_requests: int):
        """
        Validate fixed window rate limiting correctness.
        
        Args:
            df_limited: DataFrame with fixed window limiting applied
            window_seconds: Window size in seconds
            max_requests: Maximum requests per window
            
        Returns:
            Validation results dictionary
        """
        
        print("\nValidating Fixed Window Implementation...")
        
        # Check that no window exceeds the limit
        violations = df_limited.filter(col("accepted") == True).groupBy(
            "user_id", "window_start"
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("accepted_in_window")
        ).filter(col("accepted_in_window") > max_requests)
        
        violation_count = violations.count()
        
        if violation_count > 0:
            print(f"❌ FAILED: Found {violation_count} windows exceeding limit")
            violations.show()
            return {"passed": False, "violations": violation_count}
        else:
            print(f"✓ PASSED: No windows exceed limit of {max_requests} requests")
            return {"passed": True, "violations": 0}
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_sliding_window(df_limited, window_seconds: int, max_requests: int):
        """
        Validate sliding window rate limiting correctness.
        
        Args:
            df_limited: DataFrame with sliding window limiting applied
            window_seconds: Window size in seconds
            max_requests: Maximum requests per window
            
        Returns:
            Validation results dictionary
        """
        
        print("\nValidating Sliding Window Implementation...")
        
        # Check that accepted requests don't exceed limit in any sliding window
        violations = df_limited.filter(
            (col("accepted") == True) & (col("requests_in_window") > max_requests)
        )
        
        violation_count = violations.count()
        
        if violation_count > 0:
            print(f"❌ FAILED: Found {violation_count} requests violating sliding window limit")
            violations.show()
            return {"passed": False, "violations": violation_count}
        else:
            print(f"✓ PASSED: All accepted requests within limit of {max_requests}")
            return {"passed": True, "violations": 0}
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_rate_consistency(df_limited):
        """
        Validate that rate limiting is applied consistently.
        
        Args:
            df_limited: DataFrame with rate limiting applied
            
        Returns:
            Validation results dictionary
        """
        
        print("\nValidating Rate Limiting Consistency...")
        
        # Check for logical inconsistencies
        if "accepted" in df_limited.columns and "rejection_reason" in df_limited.columns:
            # Accepted requests should not have rejection reasons
            inconsistent = df_limited.filter(
                (col("accepted") == True) & (col("rejection_reason").isNotNull())
            )
            
            inconsistent_count = inconsistent.count()
            
            if inconsistent_count > 0:
                print(f"❌ FAILED: Found {inconsistent_count} inconsistent records")
                inconsistent.show()
                return {"passed": False, "inconsistencies": inconsistent_count}
            else:
                print("✓ PASSED: No logical inconsistencies found")
                return {"passed": True, "inconsistencies": 0}
        
        return {"passed": True, "message": "No validation criteria applicable"}

   # Apply rate limiting (requires 'priority' column in DataFrame)
   result_df = priority_limiter.process_with_priority_limiting(input_df)


9. DISTRIBUTED RATE LIMITING - Global Coordination
   ===============================================
   
   from pyspark_rate_limiting import DistributedRateLimiter
   
   # Create distributed limiter
   distributed = DistributedRateLimiter(
       global_limit=10000,
       window_seconds=60
   )
   
   # Apply distributed rate limiting
   result_df = distributed.process_with_distributed_limiting(input_df)
   
   # Get partition statistics
   partition_stats = distributed.get_partition_statistics(result_df)


10. ADAPTIVE RATE LIMITING - System Health Based
    =============================================
    
    from pyspark_rate_limiting import AdaptiveRateLimiter
    
    # Create adaptive limiter
    adaptive = AdaptiveRateLimiter(base_limit=1000, window_seconds=60)
    
    # Apply with historical data for adaptation
    result_df = adaptive.process_with_adaptive_limiting(
        current_df,
        historical_df=historical_data_df
    )


11. USING CONFIGURATION MANAGER - Predefined Scenarios

    from pyspark_rate_limiting import RateLimitingConfigManager

def print_best_practices():
    """
    Print best practices for implementing rate limiting in PySpark.
    """
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("BEST PRACTICES AND RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    best_practices = """

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PATTERN SELECTION GUIDE                                                    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

1. THROTTLING PATTERN
   When to use:
   • Simple rate control needed
   • Protecting downstream systems from overload
   • Batch processing scenarios
   
   Pros: Simple, predictable, easy to implement
   Cons: No burst handling, may waste capacity

2. BACKPRESSURE PATTERN
   When to use:
   • Variable load conditions
   • Need adaptive rate control
   • Streaming data ingestion
   
   Pros: Adaptive, efficient resource usage
   Cons: More complex, requires monitoring

3. TOKEN BUCKET PATTERN
   When to use:
   • Need to allow traffic bursts
   • Variable request patterns
   • API rate limiting with burst allowance
   
   Pros: Handles bursts well, flexible
   Cons: Can allow sudden spikes

4. LEAKY BUCKET PATTERN
   When to use:
   • Need constant output rate
   • Smoothing bursty traffic
   • Network traffic shaping
   
   Pros: Smooth output, predictable
   Cons: May drop requests during bursts

5. FIXED WINDOW PATTERN
   When to use:
   • Simple time-based limits
   • Clear billing/quota periods
   • Easy to understand requirements
   
   Pros: Simple, clear boundaries
   Cons: Edge effects, potential bursts at boundaries

6. SLIDING WINDOW PATTERN
   When to use:
   • Precise rate limiting needed
   • Avoid edge effects
   • Fair distribution over time
   
   Pros: Smooth, fair, no edge effects
   Cons: More computational overhead


┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION                                                   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

1. Partition Strategy
   • Distribute load evenly across partitions
   • Use appropriate partition keys (user_id, tenant_id, etc.)
   • Monitor partition skew

2. Window Sizing
   • Balance between precision and performance
   • Larger windows = better performance, less precision
   • Consider data volume and requirements

3. Caching Strategy
   • Cache frequently accessed DataFrames
   • Use appropriate storage levels
   • Clear cache when no longer needed

4. Broadcast Variables
   • Use for small lookup tables
   • Share configuration across executors
   • Reduce network overhead


┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT CHECKLIST                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

□ Define clear rate limiting requirements
□ Choose appropriate pattern(s) for use case
□ Set realistic limits based on capacity testing
□ Implement comprehensive monitoring
□ Set up alerting for limit violations
□ Plan for limit adjustments
□ Document rate limiting policies
□ Test under load conditions
□ Implement graceful degradation
□ Plan for multi-tenant scenarios
□ Consider geographic distribution
□ Implement audit logging
□ Test failure scenarios
□ Document escalation procedures
□ Plan for capacity scaling


┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MONITORING METRICS                                                         │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Key Metrics to Track:
• Acceptance Rate: % of requests accepted
• Rejection Rate: % of requests rejected
• Average Processing Rate: requests/second
• Peak Processing Rate: maximum sustained rate
• Queue Size (for bucket patterns): current queue depth
• Token Availability (for token bucket): available tokens
• Window Utilization: % of limit used per window
• Per-User/Tenant Metrics: individual usage patterns
• Latency Impact: processing delay introduced
• Resource Utilization: CPU, memory usage


┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID                                                   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

1. Setting Limits Too Low
   • Results in excessive rejections
   • Poor user experience
   • Underutilization of resources

2. Setting Limits Too High
   • Defeats purpose of rate limiting
   • System overload risk
   • Resource exhaustion

3. Ignoring Partition Skew
   • Uneven load distribution
   • Some partitions overloaded
   • Inefficient resource usage

4. Not Monitoring Metrics
   • Can't detect issues
   • Unable to optimize
   • No capacity planning data

5. Fixed Limits Without Adaptation
   • Can't handle growth
   • Inefficient during low load
   • Manual intervention required

6. Insufficient Testing
   • Unexpected behavior in production
   • Performance issues
   • Incorrect limit calculations


┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SCALING CONSIDERATIONS                                                     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Horizontal Scaling:
• Add more executors/workers
• Distribute rate limiting state
• Use distributed coordination (e.g., Redis)
• Partition data effectively

Vertical Scaling:
• Increase executor memory
• Add more CPU cores
• Optimize algorithm efficiency
• Reduce overhead

Multi-Region Deployment:
• Regional rate limiting
• Global coordination mechanisms
• Latency considerations
• Data consistency requirements

    """
    
    print(best_practices)

def integration_with_streaming():
    """
    Example of integrating rate limiting with Spark Structured Streaming.
    """
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("INTEGRATION: SPARK STRUCTURED STREAMING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    example_code = '''
# Example: Rate Limiting in Structured Streaming

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *

# Initialize Spark with streaming support
spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("StreamingRateLimiting") \\
    .config("spark.sql.streaming.checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoint") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# Define schema for streaming data
schema = StructType([
    StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
    StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
    StructField("request", StringType(), False),
    StructField("priority", StringType(), False)
])

# Read streaming data (example: from Kafka)
streaming_df = spark.readStream \\
    .format("kafka") \\
    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \\
    .option("subscribe", "requests") \\
    .load() \\
    .select(from_json(col("value").cast("string"), schema).alias("data")) \\
    .select("data.*")

# Apply rate limiting using foreachBatch
def apply_rate_limiting_batch(batch_df, batch_id):
    """Apply rate limiting to each micro-batch"""
    
    if batch_df.count() > 0:
        # Apply sliding window rate limiting
        limiter = SlidingWindowPattern(window_size_seconds=60, max_requests=1000)
        limited_df = limiter.process_with_sliding_window(batch_df)
        
        # Write accepted requests
        accepted_df = limited_df.filter(col("accepted") == True)
        accepted_df.write.mode("append").parquet("/output/accepted")
        
        # Write rejected requests to dead letter queue
        rejected_df = limited_df.filter(col("accepted") == False)
        rejected_df.write.mode("append").parquet("/output/rejected")
        
        print(f"Batch {batch_id}: Processed {batch_df.count()} requests")

# Start streaming query with rate limiting
query = streaming_df.writeStream \\
    .foreachBatch(apply_rate_limiting_batch) \\
    .outputMode("update") \\
    .start()

query.awaitTermination()
    '''
    
    print(example_code)

        count("*").alias("rejection_count"),
        collect_list("rejection_reason").alias("reasons")
    )

rejection_analysis.show()

# Time travel to analyze historical patterns
historical_df = spark.read.format("delta") \\
    .option("versionAsOf", 10) \\
    .load("/delta/rate_limited_requests")

class RateLimitingAlerts:
    """
    Alert system for rate limiting violations and anomalies.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_threshold_violations(df, acceptance_threshold: float = 0.8):
        """
        Check if acceptance rate falls below threshold.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with rate limiting applied
            acceptance_threshold: Minimum acceptable acceptance rate (0-1)
            
        Returns:
            Alert DataFrame with violations
        """
        
        if "accepted" not in df.columns:
            return None
        
        # Calculate per-user acceptance rates
        user_rates = df.groupBy("user_id").agg(
            count("*").alias("total_requests"),
            sum(when(col("accepted"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("accepted_requests"),
            (sum(when(col("accepted"), 1).otherwise(0)) / count("*")).alias("acceptance_rate")
        )
        
        # Find violations
        violations = user_rates.filter(col("acceptance_rate") < acceptance_threshold)
        
        if violations.count() > 0:
            print(f"\n⚠️  ALERT: {violations.count()} users below {acceptance_threshold*100}% acceptance rate")
            return violations.withColumn(
                "alert_severity",
                when(col("acceptance_rate") < 0.5, lit("CRITICAL"))
                .when(col("acceptance_rate") < 0.7, lit("HIGH"))
                .otherwise(lit("MEDIUM"))
            )
        else:
            print(f"✓ All users above {acceptance_threshold*100}% acceptance rate")
            return None
    
    @staticmethod
    def detect_anomalies(df, std_dev_threshold: float = 3.0):
        """
        Detect anomalous request patterns using statistical methods.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with timestamp column
            std_dev_threshold: Number of standard deviations for anomaly detection
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with detected anomalies
        """
        
        # Calculate request counts per time window
        windowed = df.groupBy(
            "user_id",
            window(col("timestamp"), "1 minute").alias("time_window")
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("request_count")
        )
        
        # Calculate statistics per user
        stats = windowed.groupBy("user_id").agg(
            avg("request_count").alias("avg_requests"),
            stddev("request_count").alias("stddev_requests")
        )
        
        # Join and detect anomalies
        with_stats = windowed.join(stats, "user_id")
        
        anomalies = with_stats.withColumn(
            "z_score",
            (col("request_count") - col("avg_requests")) / col("stddev_requests")
        ).filter(
            abs(col("z_score")) > std_dev_threshold
        ).select(
            "user_id",
            col("time_window.start").alias("window_start"),
            "request_count",
            "avg_requests",
            "z_score"
        ).withColumn(
            "anomaly_type",
            when(col("z_score") > 0, lit("SPIKE")).otherwise(lit("DROP"))
        )
        
        if anomalies.count() > 0:
            print(f"\n⚠️  ANOMALY DETECTED: {anomalies.count()} anomalous patterns found")
            return anomalies.orderBy(desc(abs(col("z_score"))))
        else:
            print("✓ No anomalies detected")
            return None
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_alert_report(df, output_path: str = None):
        """
        Generate comprehensive alert report.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with rate limiting applied
            output_path: Optional path to save report
            
        Returns:
            Alert report DataFrame
        """
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("GENERATING ALERT REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Check threshold violations
        threshold_alerts = RateLimitingAlerts.check_threshold_violations(df)
        
        # Detect anomalies
        anomaly_alerts = RateLimitingAlerts.detect_anomalies(df)
        
        # Compile report
        report_data = []
        
        if threshold_alerts and threshold_alerts.count() > 0:
            for row in threshold_alerts.collect():
                report_data.append({
                    "alert_type": "LOW_ACCEPTANCE_RATE",
                    "user_id": row.user_id,
                    "metric_value": row.acceptance_rate,
                    "severity": row.alert_severity,
                    "timestamp": datetime.now()
                })
        
        if anomaly_alerts and anomaly_alerts.count() > 0:
            for row in anomaly_alerts.collect():
                report_data.append({
                    "alert_type": f"ANOMALY_{row.anomaly_type}",
                    "user_id": row.user_id,
                    "metric_value": row.z_score,
                    "severity": "HIGH" if abs(row.z_score) > 5 else "MEDIUM",
                    "timestamp": row.window_start
                })
        
        if report_data:
            report_schema = StructType([
                StructField("alert_type", StringType(), False),
                StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
                StructField("metric_value", DoubleType(), False),
                StructField("severity", StringType(), False),
                StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False)
            ])
            
            report_df = spark.createDataFrame(report_data, report_schema)
            
            print("\nALERT SUMMARY:")
            report_df.groupBy("alert_type", "severity").agg(
                count("*").alias("count")
            ).orderBy("severity", "alert_type").show()
            
            if output_path:
                report_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
                print(f"\nAlert report saved to: {output_path}")
            
            return report_df
        else:
            print("\n✓ No alerts generated - system operating normally")
            return None


class RateLimitingOptimizer:
    """
    Optimizer for rate limiting configurations based on historical data.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def recommend_limits(historical_df, target_acceptance_rate: float = 0.95):
        """
        Recommend optimal rate limits based on historical data.
        
        Args:
            historical_df: Historical request data
            target_acceptance_rate: Desired acceptance rate (0-1)
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with recommended limits per user
        """
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("CALCULATING OPTIMAL RATE LIMITS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Calculate percentiles of request rates
        user_stats = historical_df.groupBy("user_id").agg(
            count("*").alias("total_requests"),
            countDistinct(
                (unix_timestamp(col("timestamp")) / 60).cast("long")
            ).alias("active_minutes")
        ).withColumn(
            "avg_requests_per_minute",
            col("total_requests") / col("active_minutes")
        )
        
        # Calculate recommended limit based on target acceptance rate
        # Use percentile corresponding to target rate
        percentile_value = target_acceptance_rate
        
        recommendations = user_stats.withColumn(
            "recommended_limit",
            ceil(col("avg_requests_per_minute") / percentile_value)
        ).withColumn(
            "current_avg_rate",
            round(col("avg_requests_per_minute"), 2)
        ).select(
            "user_id",
            "current_avg_rate",
            "recommended_limit",
            lit(target_acceptance_rate * 100).alias("target_acceptance_pct")
        )
        
        print(f"\nRecommendations for {target_acceptance_rate*100}% acceptance rate:")
        recommendations.orderBy(desc("recommended_limit")).show(20)
        
        return recommendations
    
    @staticmethod
    def optimize_window_size(df, min_window: int = 10, max_window: int = 300, step: int = 30):
        """
        Find optimal window size by testing different configurations.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            min_window: Minimum window size in seconds
            max_window: Maximum window size in seconds
            step: Step size for testing
            
        Returns:
            Optimal window size
        """
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("OPTIMIZING WINDOW SIZE")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        results = []
        
        for window_size in range(min_window, max_window + 1, step):
            # Test with sliding window
            limiter = SlidingWindowPattern(
                window_size_seconds=window_size,
                max_requests=100  # Fixed for comparison
            )
            
            limited_df = limiter.process_with_sliding_window(df)
            
            # Calculate metrics
            stats = limited_df.agg(
                (sum(when(col("accepted"), 1).otherwise(0)) / count("*")).alias("acceptance_rate"),
                stddev("requests_in_window").alias("stddev_requests")
            ).collect()[0]
            
            results.append({
                "window_size": window_size,
                "acceptance_rate": stats.acceptance_rate,
                "stddev_requests": stats.stddev_requests if stats.stddev_requests else 0
            })
            
            print(f"Window: {window_size}s - Acceptance: {stats.acceptance_rate:.2%} - StdDev: {stats.stddev_requests:.2f}")
        
        # Find optimal (highest acceptance rate with lowest variance)
        results_df = spark.createDataFrame(results)
        
        optimal = results_df.orderBy(
            desc("acceptance_rate"),
            "stddev_requests"
        ).first()
        
        print(f"\n✓ Optimal window size: {optimal.window_size} seconds")
        print(f"  Acceptance rate: {optimal.acceptance_rate:.2%}")
        print(f"  Request variance: {optimal.stddev_requests:.2f}")
        
        return optimal.window_size

class RateLimitingTestSuite:
    """
    Comprehensive test suite for rate limiting patterns.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def run_all_tests():
        """Run all validation tests."""
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("RUNNING COMPREHENSIVE TEST SUITE")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        test_results = []
        
        # Test 1: Fixed Window Correctness
        print("\n[TEST 1] Fixed Window Correctness")
        test_df = generate_sample_data(200)
        fixed_window = FixedWindowPattern(window_size_seconds=10, max_requests=5)
        fixed_result = fixed_window.process_with_fixed_window(test_df)
        
        validation = RateLimitingValidator.validate_fixed_window(fixed_result, 10, 5)
        test_results.append(("Fixed Window Correctness", validation["passed"]))
        
        # Test 2: Sliding Window Correctness
        print("\n[TEST 2] Sliding Window Correctness")
        sliding_window = SlidingWindowPattern(window_size_seconds=10, max_requests=5)
        sliding_result = sliding_window.process_with_sliding_window(test_df)
        
        validation = RateLimitingValidator.validate_sliding_window(sliding_result, 10, 5)
        test_results.append(("Sliding Window Correctness", validation["passed"]))
        
        # Test 3: Rate Consistency
        print("\n[TEST 3] Rate Limiting Consistency")
        validation = RateLimitingValidator.validate_rate_consistency(sliding_result)
        test_results.append(("Rate Consistency", validation["passed"]))
        
        # Test 4: Token Bucket Behavior
        print("\n[TEST 4] Token Bucket Behavior")
        token_bucket = TokenBucketPattern(capacity=20, refill_rate=10)
        token_result = token_bucket.process_with_token_bucket(test_df.limit(30))
        
        # Verify all requests eventually get processed
        accepted_count = token_result.filter(col("accepted") == True).count()
        test_results.append(("Token Bucket Processing", accepted_count > 0))
        
        # Test 5: Performance Benchmark
        print("\n[TEST 5] Performance Benchmark")
        start_time = time.time()
        _ = sliding_window.process_with_sliding_window(test_df).count()
        processing_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Should process 200 records in reasonable time (< 5 seconds for sliding window)
        performance_ok = processing_time < 5.0
        test_results.append(("Performance (<5s for 200 records)", performance_ok))
        print(f"Processing time: {processing_time:.2f}s - {'PASS' if performance_ok else 'FAIL'}")
        
        # Print summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("TEST SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        passed = sum(1 for _, result in test_results if result)
        total = len(test_results)
        
        for test_name, result in test_results:
            status = "✓ PASS" if result else "✗ FAIL"
            print(f"{status} - {test_name}")
        
        print(f"\nTotal: {passed}/{total} tests passed ({passed/total*100:.1f}%)")
        
        return all(result for _, result in test_results)

SCENARIO 1: Basic API Rate Limiting
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

# Initialize Spark
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("RateLimiting").getOrCreate()

# Load your data (must have: user_id, timestamp columns)
df = spark.read.parquet("path/to/requests")

# Apply sliding window rate limiting (100 requests per minute)
from rate_limiting_patterns import SlidingWindowPattern

limiter = SlidingWindowPattern(window_size_seconds=60, max_requests=100)
result = limiter.process_with_sliding_window(df)

# Filter accepted requests
accepted = result.filter(col("accepted") == True)
accepted.write.parquet("path/to/output/accepted")

# Filter rejected requests
rejected = result.filter(col("accepted") == False)
rejected.write.parquet("path/to/output/rejected")


SCENARIO 2: Multi-Tier Rate Limiting (Free/Premium Users)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

from rate_limiting_patterns import PriorityBasedRateLimiter

# Define limits by tier (must have 'priority' column in DataFrame)
limits = {
    "free": (60, 100),      # 100 requests per minute
    "premium": (60, 1000),  # 1000 requests per minute
    "enterprise": (60, 10000)  # 10000 requests per minute
}

limiter = PriorityBasedRateLimiter(limits)
result = limiter.process_with_priority_limiting(df)

# Analyze by tier
result.groupBy("priority", "accepted").count().show()


SCENARIO 3: Streaming Data with Backpressure

    max_queue_size=10000,
    min_rate=100,
    max_rate=5000
)

# Apply in streaming context
def process_batch(batch_df, batch_id):
    limited = limiter.process_with_backpressure(batch_df)
    limited.write.mode("append").parquet(f"output/batch_{batch_id}")

streaming_df.writeStream.foreachBatch(process_batch).start()

# COMMAND LINE INTERFACE

def create_cli():
    """
    Create command-line interface for rate limiting operations.
    """
    
    import argparse
    
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='PySpark Rate Limiting Patterns',
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="""
Examples:
  # Run demonstrations
  python rate_limiting_patterns.py --demo
  
  # Run specific pattern
  python rate_limiting_patterns.py --pattern sliding_window --input data.parquet --output result
  
  # Run tests
  python rate_limiting_patterns.py --test
  
  # Show quick start guide
  python rate_limiting_patterns.py --quick-start
  
  # List available scenarios
  python rate_limiting_patterns.py --list-scenarios
        """
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--demo',
        action='store_true',
        help='Run full demonstration of all patterns'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--test',
        action='store_true',
        help='Run test suite'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--quick-start',
        action='store_true',
        help='Show quick start guide'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--list-scenarios',
        action='store_true',
        help='List available pre-configured scenarios'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--pattern',
        choices=['throttling', 'backpressure', 'token_bucket', 'leaky_bucket', 
                 'fixed_window', 'sliding_window', 'hybrid', 'priority', 'distributed', 'adaptive'],
        help='Specific pattern to apply'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--input',
        type=str,
        help='Input data path (parquet format)'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--output',
        type=str,
        help='Output path for results'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--scenario',
        type=str,
        help='Pre-configured scenario name'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--window-seconds',
        type=int,
        default=60,
        help='Window size in seconds (default: 60)'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--max-requests',
        type=int,
        default=1000,
        help='Maximum requests per window (default: 1000)'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--validate',
        action='store_true',
        help='Validate rate limiting correctness'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--metrics',
        action='store_true',
        help='Generate comprehensive metrics report'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--alerts',
        action='store_true',
        help='Check for violations and anomalies'
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        '--optimize',
        action='store_true',
        help='Optimize rate limiting configuration'
    )
    
    return parser


def execute_cli_command(args):
    """
    Execute command based on CLI arguments.
    """
    
    if args.demo:
        print("Running full demonstration...")
        main()
        return
    
    if args.test:
        print("Running test suite...")
        success = RateLimitingTestSuite.run_all_tests()
        exit(0 if success else 1)
    
    if args.quick_start:
        quick_start_guide()
        return
    
    if args.list_scenarios:
        RateLimitingConfigManager.list_scenarios()
        return
    
    # Pattern-specific execution
    if args.pattern and args.input:
        print(f"Applying {args.pattern} pattern to {args.input}")
        
        # Load input data
        input_df = spark.read.parquet(args.input)
        print(f"Loaded {input_df.count()} records")
        
        # Apply pattern based on selection
        if args.scenario:
            result_df = RateLimitingConfigManager.apply_config(input_df, args.scenario)
        else:
            result_df = apply_pattern(input_df, args.pattern, args.window_seconds, args.max_requests)
        
        # Validate if requested
        if args.validate:
            print("\nValidating results...")
            if args.pattern in ['fixed_window']:
                RateLimitingValidator.validate_fixed_window(
                    result_df, args.window_seconds, args.max_requests
                )
            elif args.pattern in ['sliding_window']:
                RateLimitingValidator.validate_sliding_window(
                    result_df, args.window_seconds, args.max_requests
                )
            RateLimitingValidator.validate_rate_consistency(result_df)
        
        # Generate metrics if requested
        if args.metrics:
            print("\nGenerating metrics...")
            metrics = RateLimitingMetrics.calculate_comprehensive_metrics(result_df)
            RateLimitingMetrics.generate_metrics_report(metrics)
        
        # Check alerts if requested
        if args.alerts:
            print("\nChecking for alerts...")
            RateLimitingAlerts.generate_alert_report(result_df)
        
        # Optimize if requested
        if args.optimize:
            print("\nOptimizing configuration...")
            RateLimitingOptimizer.recommend_limits(input_df)
            RateLimitingOptimizer.optimize_window_size(input_df)
        
        # Save output
        if args.output:
            print(f"\nSaving results to {args.output}")
            result_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(args.output)
            print(f"✓ Results saved successfully")
        else:
            print("\nPreview of results:")
            result_df.show(20)
    
    elif args.pattern or args.input:
        print("Error: Both --pattern and --input are required for processing")
        exit(1)
    else:
        print("No action specified. Use --help for usage information")


def apply_pattern(df, pattern_name, window_seconds, max_requests):
    """
    Apply specific rate limiting pattern.
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        pattern_name: Name of pattern to apply
        window_seconds: Window size in seconds
        max_requests: Maximum requests per window
        
    Returns:
        DataFrame with rate limiting applied
    """
    
    if pattern_name == 'throttling':
        limiter = ThrottlingPattern(requests_per_second=max_requests/window_seconds)
        return limiter.process_with_throttling(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'backpressure':
        limiter = BackpressurePattern(
            max_queue_size=max_requests,
            min_rate=int(max_requests * 0.1),
            max_rate=max_requests
        )
        return limiter.process_with_backpressure(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'token_bucket':
        limiter = TokenBucketPattern(
            capacity=max_requests,
            refill_rate=max_requests/window_seconds
        )
        return limiter.process_with_token_bucket(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'leaky_bucket':
        limiter = LeakyBucketPattern(
            bucket_size=max_requests,
            leak_rate=max_requests/window_seconds
        )
        return limiter.process_with_leaky_bucket(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'fixed_window':
        limiter = FixedWindowPattern(
            window_size_seconds=window_seconds,
            max_requests=max_requests
        )
        return limiter.process_with_fixed_window(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'sliding_window':
        limiter = SlidingWindowPattern(
            window_size_seconds=window_seconds,
            max_requests=max_requests
        )
        return limiter.process_with_sliding_window(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'hybrid':
        limiter = HybridRateLimiter()
        return limiter.process_with_hybrid_limiting(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'distributed':
        limiter = DistributedRateLimiter(
            global_limit=max_requests,
            window_seconds=window_seconds
        )
        return limiter.process_with_distributed_limiting(df)
    
    elif pattern_name == 'adaptive':
        limiter = AdaptiveRateLimiter(
            base_limit=max_requests,
            window_seconds=window_seconds
        )
        return limiter.process_with_adaptive_limiting(df)
    
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown pattern: {pattern_name}")

1. INTRODUCTION
═══════════════

Rate limiting is essential for:
• Protecting system resources
• Ensuring fair usage
• Preventing abuse
• Managing costs
• Maintaining SLA compliance

This library provides 6 core patterns plus advanced variations for
comprehensive rate limiting in PySpark applications.


2. PATTERN DESCRIPTIONS
════════════════════════

2.1 THROTTLING PATTERN
   Purpose: Simple rate control with delays
   Best for: Batch processing, protecting downstream systems
   Complexity: Low
   Performance: Medium
   
   Key Parameters:
   - requests_per_second: Target processing rate
   
   Example:
   throttler = ThrottlingPattern(requests_per_second=50)
   result = throttler.process_with_throttling(df)


2.2 BACKPRESSURE PATTERN
   Purpose: Adaptive rate control based on system load
   Best for: Streaming, variable load conditions
   Complexity: Medium
   Performance: High
   
   Key Parameters:
   - max_queue_size: Maximum queue depth
   - min_rate: Minimum processing rate
   - max_rate: Maximum processing rate
   
   Example:
   backpressure = BackpressurePattern(
       max_queue_size=1000,
       min_rate=10,
       max_rate=100
   )
   result = backpressure.process_with_backpressure(df)


2.3 TOKEN BUCKET PATTERN
   Purpose: Allow bursts while maintaining average rate
   Best for: APIs with bursty traffic
   Complexity: Medium
   Performance: High
   
   Key Parameters:
   - capacity: Maximum burst size
   - refill_rate: Token replenishment rate
   
   Example:
   token_bucket = TokenBucketPattern(capacity=100, refill_rate=50)
   result = token_bucket.process_with_token_bucket(df)


2.4 LEAKY BUCKET PATTERN
   Purpose: Smooth bursty traffic to constant rate
   Best for: Network traffic shaping
   Complexity: Medium
   Performance: Medium
   
   Key Parameters:
   - bucket_size: Queue capacity
   - leak_rate: Processing
```python
   - leak_rate: Processing rate (requests/second)
   
   Example:
   leaky_bucket = LeakyBucketPattern(bucket_size=500, leak_rate=100)
   result = leaky_bucket.process_with_leaky_bucket(df)


2.5 FIXED WINDOW PATTERN
   Purpose: Simple time-based quotas
   Best for: Clear billing periods, simple quotas
   Complexity: Low
   Performance: High
   
   Key Parameters:
   - window_size_seconds: Window duration
   - max_requests: Maximum requests per window
   
   Example:
   fixed_window = FixedWindowPattern(
       window_size_seconds=60,
       max_requests=1000
   )
   result = fixed_window.process_with_fixed_window(df)


2.6 SLIDING WINDOW PATTERN
   Purpose: Smooth rate limiting without edge effects
   Best for: Precise rate limiting, fair distribution
   Complexity: Medium
   Performance: Medium
   
   Key Parameters:
   - window_size_seconds: Sliding window duration
   - max_requests: Maximum requests in window
   
   Example:
   sliding_window = SlidingWindowPattern(
       window_size_seconds=60,
       max_requests=1000
   )
   result = sliding_window.process_with_sliding_window(df)

4. CONFIGURATION GUIDE
══════════════════════

4.1 Input DataFrame Requirements
   
   Minimum required columns:
   • id or request_id (IntegerType) - Unique identifier
   • user_id (StringType) - User/client identifier
   • timestamp (TimestampType) - Request timestamp
   
   Optional columns:
   • priority (StringType) - For priority-based limiting
   • error (BooleanType) - For adaptive limiting
   • endpoint (StringType) - For endpoint-specific limits


4.2 Pre-configured Scenarios
   
   Available scenarios:
   • api_gateway_free_tier: 100 req/min
   • api_gateway_premium_tier: 10,000 req/min
   • streaming_ingestion: Adaptive backpressure
   • microservices_internal: Token bucket (1000 capacity)
   • public_api: Leaky bucket (500 size, 100 rate)
   • batch_processing: Throttling (50 req/sec)
   
   Usage:
   RateLimitingConfigManager.apply_config(df, "api_gateway_premium_tier")


4.3 Custom Configuration
   
   Example custom configuration:
   
   config = {
       "pattern": "sliding_window",
       "window_seconds": 60,
       "max_requests": 5000,
       "description": "Custom high-volume API"
   }


5. PERFORMANCE TUNING
══════════════════════

5.1 Partitioning Strategy
   
   • Repartition by user_id for user-level limiting
   • Use coalesce() to reduce shuffle overhead
   • Monitor partition skew
   
   Example:
   df = df.repartition(100, "user_id")


5.2 Caching Strategy
   
   • Cache DataFrames used multiple times
   • Use appropriate storage level
   • Unpersist when done
   
   Example:
   df.cache()
   # ... processing ...
   df.unpersist()


5.3 Window Size Selection
   
   Smaller windows:
   + More precise rate limiting
   + Better fairness
   - Higher computational overhead
   - More memory usage
   
   Larger windows:
   + Better performance
   + Lower memory usage
   - Less precise
   - Potential unfairness
   
   Recommendation:
   • Start with 60 seconds
   • Adjust based on requirements
   • Use optimizer to find optimal size


5.4 Broadcast Variables
   
   For configuration data:
   
   config_broadcast = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(config_dict)
   # Use config_broadcast.value in UDFs


6. TROUBLESHOOTING
══════════════════

6.1 Common Issues

   Issue: High rejection rate
   Causes:
   • Limits set too low
   • Traffic spike
   • Incorrect window size
   
   Solutions:
   • Use RateLimitingOptimizer.recommend_limits()
   • Increase limits gradually
   • Use adaptive limiting
   • Check for anomalies


   Issue: Poor performance
   Causes:
   • Too many partitions
   • Small window sizes
   • Excessive shuffling
   
   Solutions:
   • Optimize partition count
   • Increase window size
   • Use appropriate pattern
   • Enable caching


   Issue: Inconsistent results
   Causes:
   • Clock skew
   • Partition imbalance
   • Incorrect timestamp handling
   
   Solutions:
   • Validate timestamps
   • Check partition distribution
   • Use distributed limiting
   • Run validation tests


   Issue: Memory errors
   Causes:
   • Large window sizes
   • High cardinality
   • Insufficient executor memory
   
   Solutions:
   • Reduce window size
   • Increase executor memory
   • Use sampling for testing
   • Optimize data types


6.2 Debugging Tips
   
   • Enable detailed logging:
     spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("INFO")
   
   • Check partition distribution:
     df.rdd.glom().map(len).collect()
   
   • Validate input data:
     df.select("timestamp").describe().show()
   
   • Monitor Spark UI for bottlenecks
   
   • Use .explain() to check query plans


7. FAQ
══════

Q: Which pattern should I use?
A: It depends on your requirements:
   • Simple quotas → Fixed Window
   • Precise limiting → Sliding Window
   • Allow bursts → Token Bucket
   • Smooth traffic → Leaky Bucket
   • Adaptive control → Backpressure
   • Simple protection → Throttling

Q: How do I handle multiple rate limits?
A: Use HybridRateLimiter or PriorityBasedRateLimiter

Q: Can I use this with Spark Streaming?
A: Yes! Use foreachBatch() to apply rate limiting to micro-batches

Q: How do I test my configuration?
A: Use RateLimitingTestSuite.run_all_tests()

Q: What's the performance impact?
A: Varies by pattern:
   • Fixed Window: Minimal (~5-10% overhead)
   • Sliding Window: Moderate (~15-25% overhead)
   • Token/Leaky Bucket: Low-Moderate (~10-20% overhead)

Q: How do I monitor in production?
A: Use RateLimitingMetrics and RateLimitingAlerts

Q: Can I customize rejection messages?
A: Yes, modify the rejection_reason column in results

Q: How do I handle distributed systems?
A: Use DistributedRateLimiter for global coordination

Q: What about time zones?
A: All timestamps should be in UTC for consistency

Q: How do I migrate from one pattern to another?
A: Test new pattern with historical data, compare metrics,
   gradually roll out with monitoring

"""
Purpose: Compare records between source and target systems to identify
         missing, extra, or mismatched records
"""

class SourceTargetReconciliation:
    """
    Reconciles data between source and target datasets
    Identifies: Missing records, Extra records, Matched records
    """
    
    def __init__(self, source_df, target_df, key_columns):
        """
        Initialize reconciliation with source and target dataframes
        
        Args:
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            target_df: Target DataFrame
            key_columns: List of columns that uniquely identify records
        """
        self.source_df = source_df
        self.target_df = target_df
        self.key_columns = key_columns
        
    def reconcile(self):
        """
        Perform full reconciliation between source and target
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing reconciliation results
        """
        # Add source indicators
        source_marked = self.source_df.withColumn("source_flag", lit(1))
        target_marked = self.target_df.withColumn("target_flag", lit(1))
        
        # Full outer join on key columns
        joined_df = source_marked.alias("src").join(
            target_marked.alias("tgt"),
            self.key_columns,
            "full_outer"
        )
        
        # Identify record types
        reconciliation_df = joined_df.withColumn(
            "reconciliation_status",
            when(col("src.source_flag").isNull(), "EXTRA_IN_TARGET")
            .when(col("tgt.target_flag").isNull(), "MISSING_IN_TARGET")
            .otherwise("MATCHED")
        )
        
        # Generate summary statistics
        summary = reconciliation_df.groupBy("reconciliation_status").count()
        
        # Get detailed results for each category
        missing_in_target = reconciliation_df.filter(
            col("reconciliation_status") == "MISSING_IN_TARGET"
        )
        
        extra_in_target = reconciliation_df.filter(
            col("reconciliation_status") == "EXTRA_IN_TARGET"
        )
        
        matched_records = reconciliation_df.filter(
            col("reconciliation_status") == "MATCHED"
        )
        
        return {
            "summary": summary,
            "missing_in_target": missing_in_target,
            "extra_in_target": extra_in_target,
            "matched_records": matched_records,
            "full_reconciliation": reconciliation_df
        }
    
    def generate_report(self, results):
        """Generate reconciliation report"""
        print("\nSource-Target Reconciliation Report:")
        print("=" * 60)
        results["summary"].show()
        
        total_source = self.source_df.count()
        total_target = self.target_df.count()
        
        print(f"\nTotal Source Records: {total_source}")
        print(f"Total Target Records: {total_target}")
        print(f"Difference: {total_source - total_target}")
        
        return results

"""
Purpose: Compare record counts across different dimensions and hierarchies
         to ensure data completeness
"""

class CountReconciliation:
    """
    Performs count-based reconciliation across multiple dimensions
    """
    
    def __init__(self, source_df, target_df):
        self.source_df = source_df
        self.target_df = target_df
        
    def overall_count_check(self):
        """Compare overall record counts"""
        source_count = self.source_df.count()
        target_count = self.target_df.count()
        
        return {
            "source_count": source_count,
            "target_count": target_count,
            "difference": source_count - target_count,
            "match_percentage": (min(source_count, target_count) / max(source_count, target_count) * 100) 
                               if max(source_count, target_count) > 0 else 0
        }
    
    def dimensional_count_check(self, group_columns):
        """
        Compare counts across specified dimensions
        
        Args:
            group_columns: List of columns to group by
        """
        # Get counts from source
        source_counts = self.source_df.groupBy(group_columns) \
            .agg(count("*").alias("source_count"))
        
        # Get counts from target
        target_counts = self.target_df.groupBy(group_columns) \
            .agg(count("*").alias("target_count"))
        
        # Join and compare
        comparison = source_counts.join(
            target_counts,
            group_columns,
            "full_outer"
        ).fillna(0, ["source_count", "target_count"])
        
        # Calculate differences
        comparison = comparison.withColumn(
            "count_difference",
            col("source_count") - col("target_count")
        ).withColumn(
            "match_status",
            when(col("count_difference") == 0, "MATCH")
            .when(col("count_difference") > 0, "SOURCE_HAS_MORE")
            .otherwise("TARGET_HAS_MORE")
        ).withColumn(
            "match_percentage",
            when(
                (col("source_count") == 0) & (col("target_count") == 0), 100.0
            ).otherwise(
                least(col("source_count"), col("target_count")) / 
                greatest(col("source_count"), col("target_count")) * 100
            )
        )
        
        return comparison
    
    def hierarchical_count_check(self, hierarchy_columns):
        """
        Perform count reconciliation at multiple hierarchy levels
        
        Args:
            hierarchy_columns: List of columns representing hierarchy (top to bottom)
        """
        results = {}
        
        for i in range(1, len(hierarchy_columns) + 1):
            level_columns = hierarchy_columns[:i]
            level_name = " -> ".join(level_columns)
            
            results[level_name] = self.dimensional_count_check(level_columns)
        
        return results
    
    def generate_count_report(self, overall_result, dimensional_results):
        """Generate comprehensive count reconciliation report"""
        print("\nCount Reconciliation Report:")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        print("\nOverall Count Summary:")
        print(f"Source Count: {overall_result['source_count']:,}")
        print(f"Target Count: {overall_result['target_count']:,}")
        print(f"Difference: {overall_result['difference']:,}")
        print(f"Match Percentage: {overall_result['match_percentage']:.2f}%")
        
        print("\nDimensional Count Comparison:")
        for dimension, result_df in dimensional_results.items():
            print(f"\n{dimension}:")
            result_df.orderBy("count_difference", ascending=False).show()

"""
Purpose: Compare aggregate sums of numeric columns to ensure data accuracy
         and identify discrepancies in financial or numerical data
"""

class SumReconciliation:
    """
    Performs sum-based reconciliation for numeric columns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, source_df, target_df, tolerance=0.01):
        """
        Initialize sum reconciliation
        
        Args:
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            target_df: Target DataFrame
            tolerance: Acceptable difference percentage (default 0.01 = 1%)
        """
        self.source_df = source_df
        self.target_df = target_df
        self.tolerance = tolerance
    
    def overall_sum_check(self, numeric_columns):
        """
        Compare overall sums for specified numeric columns
        
        Args:
            numeric_columns: List of numeric column names to sum
        """
        results = []
        
        for col_name in numeric_columns:
            source_sum = self.source_df.agg(
                sum(col(col_name)).alias("sum_value")
            ).collect()[0]["sum_value"] or 0
            
            target_sum = self.target_df.agg(
                sum(col(col_name)).alias("sum_value")
            ).collect()[0]["sum_value"] or 0
            
            difference = source_sum - target_sum
            diff_percentage = (abs(difference) / source_sum * 100) if source_sum != 0 else 0
            
            is_within_tolerance = diff_percentage <= (self.tolerance * 100)
            
            results.append({
                "column": col_name,
                "source_sum": float(source_sum),
                "target_sum": float(target_sum),
                "difference": float(difference),
                "diff_percentage": float(diff_percentage),
                "within_tolerance": is_within_tolerance,
                "status": "PASS" if is_within_tolerance else "FAIL"
            })
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(results)
    
    def dimensional_sum_check(self, group_columns, sum_columns):
        """
        Compare sums across dimensions
        
        Args:
            group_columns: Columns to group by
            sum_columns: Columns to sum
        """
        # Build aggregation expressions
        agg_exprs = [sum(col(c)).alias(f"{c}_sum") for c in sum_columns]
        
        # Calculate source sums
        source_sums = self.source_df.groupBy(group_columns).agg(*agg_exprs)
        
        # Calculate target sums
        target_sums = self.target_df.groupBy(group_columns).agg(*agg_exprs)
        
        # Rename target columns
        for col_name in sum_columns:
            target_sums = target_sums.withColumnRenamed(
                f"{col_name}_sum",
                f"{col_name}_sum_target"
            )
        
        # Join and compare
        comparison = source_sums.join(
            target_sums,
            group_columns,
            "full_outer"
        )
        
        # Calculate differences for each sum column
        for col_name in sum_columns:
            source_col = f"{col_name}_sum"
            target_col = f"{col_name}_sum_target"
            diff_col = f"{col_name}_difference"
            pct_col = f"{col_name}_diff_pct"
            status_col = f"{col_name}_status"
            
            comparison = comparison.fillna(0, [source_col, target_col])
            
            comparison = comparison.withColumn(
```python
                diff_col,
                col(source_col) - col(target_col)
            ).withColumn(
                pct_col,
                when(col(source_col) == 0, 0.0)
                .otherwise(abs(col(diff_col)) / col(source_col) * 100)
            ).withColumn(
                status_col,
                when(col(pct_col) <= (self.tolerance * 100), "PASS")
                .otherwise("FAIL")
            )
        
        return comparison
    
    def balance_check(self, debit_col, credit_col, group_columns=None):
        """
        Verify that debits equal credits (accounting balance check)
        
        Args:
            debit_col: Debit column name
            credit_col: Credit column name
            group_columns: Optional grouping columns
        """
        if group_columns:
            # Group-level balance check
            source_balance = self.source_df.groupBy(group_columns).agg(
                sum(col(debit_col)).alias("total_debit"),
                sum(col(credit_col)).alias("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "balance",
                col("total_debit") - col("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "is_balanced",
                abs(col("balance")) <= self.tolerance
            )
            
            target_balance = self.target_df.groupBy(group_columns).agg(
                sum(col(debit_col)).alias("total_debit"),
                sum(col(credit_col)).alias("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "balance",
                col("total_debit") - col("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "is_balanced",
                abs(col("balance")) <= self.tolerance
            )
        else:
            # Overall balance check
            source_balance = self.source_df.agg(
                sum(col(debit_col)).alias("total_debit"),
                sum(col(credit_col)).alias("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "balance",
                col("total_debit") - col("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "is_balanced",
                abs(col("balance")) <= self.tolerance
            ).withColumn(
                "source",
                lit("SOURCE")
            )
            
            target_balance = self.target_df.agg(
                sum(col(debit_col)).alias("total_debit"),
                sum(col(credit_col)).alias("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "balance",
                col("total_debit") - col("total_credit")
            ).withColumn(
                "is_balanced",
                abs(col("balance")) <= self.tolerance
            ).withColumn(
                "source",
                lit("TARGET")
            )
        
        return source_balance, target_balance
    
    def generate_sum_report(self, overall_results, dimensional_results=None):
        """Generate sum reconciliation report"""
        print("\nSum Reconciliation Report:")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        print("\nOverall Sum Comparison:")
        overall_results.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Check if any failures
        failures = overall_results.filter(col("status") == "FAIL").count()
        if failures > 0:
            print(f"\n⚠️  WARNING: {failures} column(s) failed tolerance check!")
        else:
            print("\n✓ All columns passed tolerance check")
        
        if dimensional_results:
            print("\nDimensional Sum Comparison:")
            dimensional_results.show(truncate=False)

# Example usage

# PATTERN 4: HASH-BASED RECONCILIATION PATTERN

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("4. HASH-BASED RECONCILIATION PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
"""
Purpose: Use cryptographic hashing to efficiently compare large datasets
         and identify changed records without comparing individual fields
"""

class HashBasedReconciliation:
    """
    Performs hash-based reconciliation for efficient data comparison
    """
    
    def __init__(self, source_df, target_df, key_columns, hash_columns=None):
        """
        Initialize hash-based reconciliation
        
        Args:
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            target_df: Target DataFrame
            key_columns: Columns that uniquely identify records
            hash_columns: Columns to include in hash (None = all columns)
        """
        self.source_df = source_df
        self.target_df = target_df
        self.key_columns = key_columns
        self.hash_columns = hash_columns or [
            c for c in source_df.columns if c not in key_columns
        ]
    
    def generate_hash(self, df, hash_method="md5"):
        """
        Generate hash for specified columns
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            hash_method: Hash algorithm (md5, sha1, sha256)
        """
        # Concatenate hash columns
        concat_expr = concat_ws("||", *[
            coalesce(col(c).cast("string"), lit("NULL")) 
            for c in self.hash_columns
        ])
        
        # Generate hash based on method
        if hash_method == "md5":
            hash_expr = md5(concat_expr)
        elif hash_method == "sha1":
            hash_expr = sha1(concat_expr)
        elif hash_method == "sha256":
            hash_expr = sha2(concat_expr, 256)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported hash method: {hash_method}")
        
        return df.withColumn("record_hash", hash_expr)
    
    def reconcile_by_hash(self, hash_method="md5"):
        """
        Perform reconciliation using hash comparison
        
        Args:
            hash_method: Hash algorithm to use
        """
        # Generate hashes for both datasets
        source_hashed = self.generate_hash(self.source_df, hash_method)
        target_hashed = self.generate_hash(self.target_df, hash_method)
        
        # Join on key columns
        joined = source_hashed.alias("src").join(
            target_hashed.alias("tgt"),
            self.key_columns,
            "full_outer"
        )
        
        # Classify records
        reconciled = joined.withColumn(
            "reconciliation_status",
            when(col("src.record_hash").isNull(), "MISSING_IN_SOURCE")
            .when(col("tgt.record_hash").isNull(), "MISSING_IN_TARGET")
            .when(col("src.record_hash") == col("tgt.record_hash"), "MATCHED")
            .otherwise("MODIFIED")
        )
        
        # Generate summary
        summary = reconciled.groupBy("reconciliation_status").count()
        
        # Get detailed results
        matched = reconciled.filter(col("reconciliation_status") == "MATCHED")
        modified = reconciled.filter(col("reconciliation_status") == "MODIFIED")
        missing_in_source = reconciled.filter(
            col("reconciliation_status") == "MISSING_IN_SOURCE"
        )
        missing_in_target = reconciled.filter(
            col("reconciliation_status") == "MISSING_IN_TARGET"
        )
        
        return {
            "summary": summary,
            "matched": matched,
            "modified": modified,
            "missing_in_source": missing_in_source,
            "missing_in_target": missing_in_target,
            "full_reconciliation": reconciled
        }
    
    def identify_changed_columns(self, modified_df):
        """
        For modified records, identify which columns changed
        
        Args:
            modified_df: DataFrame containing modified records
        """
        # Compare each hash column
        changed_columns_expr = []
        
        for col_name in self.hash_columns:
            src_col = f"src.{col_name}"
            tgt_col = f"tgt.{col_name}"
            
            changed_columns_expr.append(
                when(
                    coalesce(col(src_col), lit("NULL")) != 
                    coalesce(col(tgt_col), lit("NULL")),
                    col_name
                ).otherwise(None)
            )
        
        # Create array of changed columns
        result = modified_df.withColumn(
            "changed_columns",
            array_remove(array(*changed_columns_expr), None)
        )
        
        return result
    
    def incremental_hash_check(self, partition_column, partition_values=None):
        """
        Perform hash-based reconciliation on specific partitions
        
        Args:
            partition_column: Column to partition by
            partition_values: Specific partition values to check (None = all)
        """
        results = {}
        
        if partition_values is None:
            # Get all unique partition values from source
            partition_values = [
                row[partition_column] 
                for row in self.source_df.select(partition_column).distinct().collect()
            ]
        
        for partition_value in partition_values:
            # Filter both datasets for this partition
            source_partition = self.source_df.filter(
                col(partition_column) == partition_value
            )
            target_partition = self.target_df.filter(
                col(partition_column) == partition_value
            )
            
            # Create temporary reconciler for this partition
            partition_reconciler = HashBasedReconciliation(
                source_partition,
                target_partition,
                self.key_columns,
                self.hash_columns
            )
            
            # Reconcile partition
            results[partition_value] = partition_reconciler.reconcile_by_hash()
        
        return results
    
    def generate_hash_report(self, results):
        """Generate hash-based reconciliation report"""
        print("\nHash-Based Reconciliation Report:")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        print("\nReconciliation Summary:")
        results["summary"].show()
        
        # Calculate percentages
        total_records = sum([
            row["count"] for row in results["summary"].collect()
        ])
        
        print(f"\nTotal Records Compared: {total_records:,}")
        
        for row in results["summary"].collect():
            status = row["reconciliation_status"]
            count = row["count"]
            percentage = (count / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
            print(f"{status}: {count:,} ({percentage:.2f}%)")
        
        return results

print("5. ROW-BY-ROW COMPARISON PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
"""
Purpose: Perform detailed field-level comparison between source and target
         to identify exactly which fields differ for each record
"""

class RowByRowComparison:
    """
    Performs detailed row-by-row and column-by-column comparison
    """
    
    def __init__(self, source_df, target_df, key_columns):
        """
        Initialize row-by-row comparison
        
        Args:
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            target_df: Target DataFrame
            key_columns: Columns that uniquely identify records
        """
        self.source_df = source_df
        self.target_df = target_df
        self.key_columns = key_columns
        
        # Get columns to compare (excluding key columns)
        self.compare_columns = [
            c for c in source_df.columns if c not in key_columns
        ]
    
    def compare_all_columns(self):
        """
        Compare all columns and identify differences
        """
        # Join source and target
        joined = self.source_df.alias("src").join(
            self.target_df.alias("tgt"),
            self.key_columns,
            "inner"  # Only compare records that exist in both
        )
        
        # Create comparison columns for each field
        comparison_exprs = []
        
        for col_name in self.compare_columns:
            src_col = f"src.{col_name}"
            tgt_col = f"tgt.{col_name}"
            
            # Create a struct with comparison details
            comparison_exprs.append(
                struct(
                    lit(col_name).alias("column_name"),
                    col(src_col).alias("source_value"),
                    col(tgt_col).alias("target_value"),
                    when(
                        (col(src_col).isNull() & col(tgt_col).isNull()) |
                        (col(src_col) == col(tgt_col)),
                        lit("MATCH")
                    ).otherwise(lit("MISMATCH")).alias("status"),
                    when(
                        col(src_col).isNull() & col(tgt_col).isNotNull(),
                        lit("NULL_IN_SOURCE")
                    ).when(
                        col(src_col).isNotNull() & col(tgt_col).isNull(),
                        lit("NULL_IN_TARGET")
                    ).when(
                        col(src_col) != col(tgt_col),
                        lit("VALUE_DIFFERENCE")
                    ).otherwise(lit("EXACT_MATCH")).alias("difference_type")
                ).alias(f"cmp_{col_name}")
            )
        
        # Add comparison columns
        compared = joined.select(
            *[f"src.{k}" for k in self.key_columns],
            *comparison_exprs
        )
        
        return compared
    
    def get_mismatched_records(self, comparison_df):
        """
        Extract only records with mismatches
        """
        # Explode comparison structs into rows
        mismatches = comparison_df
        
        # Check each comparison column for mismatches
        mismatch_conditions = []
        for col_name in self.compare_columns:
            mismatch_conditions.append(
                col(f"cmp_{col_name}.status") == "MISMATCH"
            )
        
        # Filter records with any mismatch
        if mismatch_conditions:
            mismatched = mismatches.filter(
                reduce(lambda a, b: a | b, mismatch_conditions)
            )
            return mismatched
        
        return mismatches.filter(lit(False))  # Empty DataFrame
    
    def create_detailed_comparison_report(self, comparison_df):
        """
        Create a detailed comparison report with all differences
        """
        # Flatten comparison data
        detailed_rows = []
        
        for row in comparison_df.collect():
            key_values = {k: row[k] for k in self.key_columns}
            
            for col_name in self.compare_columns:
                cmp_data = row[f"cmp_{col_name}"]
                
                if cmp_data["status"] == "MISMATCH":
                    detailed_rows.append({
                        **key_values,
                        "column_name": cmp_data["column_name"],
                        "source_value": str(cmp_data["source_value"]),
                        "target_value": str(cmp_data["target_value"]),
                        "difference_type": cmp_data["difference_type"]
                    })
        
        if detailed_rows:
            return spark.createDataFrame(detailed_rows)
        else:
            # Return empty DataFrame with schema
            schema = StructType([
                StructField(k, StringType(), True) for k in self.key_columns
            ] + [
                StructField("column_name", StringType(), True),
                StructField("source_value", StringType(), True),
                StructField("target_value", StringType(), True),
                StructField("difference_type", StringType(), True)
            ])
            return spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
    
    def column_level_summary(self, comparison_df):
        """
        Generate summary statistics at column level
        """
        summary_data = []
        
        for col_name in self.compare_columns:
            # Count matches and mismatches
            match_count = comparison_df.filter(
                col(f"cmp_{col_name}.status") == "MATCH"
            ).count()
            
            mismatch_count = comparison_df.filter(
                col(f"cmp_{col_name}.status") == "MISMATCH"
            ).count()
            
            total = match_count + mismatch_count
            match_percentage = (match_count / total * 100) if total > 0 else 0
            
            summary_data.append({
                "column_name": col_name,
                "total_records": total,
                "matches": match_count,
                "mismatches": mismatch_count,
                "match_percentage": match_percentage
            })
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(summary_data)
    
    def side_by_side_comparison(self, record_keys):
        """
        Generate side-by-side comparison for specific records
        
        Args:
            record_keys: Dictionary of key column values
        """
        # Build filter condition
        filter_condition = reduce(
            lambda a, b: a & b,
            [col(k) == v for k, v in record_keys.items()]
        )
        
        # Get source record
        source_record = self.source_df.filter(filter_condition)
        
        # Get target record
        target_record = self.target_df.filter(filter_condition)
        
        # Create side-by-side view
        if source_record.count() > 0 and target_record.count() > 0:
            source_data = source_record.collect()[0].asDict()
            target_data = target_record.collect()[0].asDict()
            
            comparison_rows = []
            for col_name in self.source_df.columns:
                src_val = source_data.get(col_name)
                tgt_val = target_data.get(col_name)
                
                comparison_rows.append({
                    "column_name": col_name,
                    "source_value": str(src_val),
                    "target_value": str(tgt_val),
                    "match": src_val == tgt_val
                })
            
            return spark.createDataFrame(comparison_rows)
        
        return None
    
    def generate_comparison_report(self, comparison_df, detailed_df, summary_df):
        """Generate comprehensive row-by-row comparison report"""
        print("\nRow-by-Row Comparison Report:")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        total_records = comparison_df.count()
        mismatched_records = detailed_df.select(
            *self.key_columns
        ).distinct().count() if detailed_df.count() > 0 else 0
        
        print(f"\nTotal Records Compared: {total_records:,}")
        print(f"Records with Differences: {mismatched_records:,}")
        print(f"Match Rate: {((total_records - mismatched_records) / total_records * 100):.2f}%")
        
        print("\nColumn-Level Summary:")
        summary_df.orderBy("match_percentage").show(truncate=False)
        
        if detailed_df.count() > 0:
            print("\nDetailed Differences (Sample):")
            detailed_df.show(10, truncate=False)

"""
Purpose: Use statistical methods to validate data quality and identify
         anomalies, outliers, and distribution differences
"""

class StatisticalReconciliation:
    """
    Performs statistical analysis and reconciliation
    """
    
    def __init__(self, source_df, target_df):
        """
        Initialize statistical reconciliation
        
        Args:
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            target_df: Target DataFrame
        """
        self.source_df = source_df
        self.target_df = target_df
    
    def basic_statistics_comparison(self, numeric_columns):
        """
        Compare basic statistical measures
        
        Args:
            numeric_columns: List of numeric columns to analyze
        """
        results = []
        
        for col_name in numeric_columns:
            # Calculate statistics for source
            source_stats = self.source_df.select(
                mean(col(col_name)).alias("mean"),
                stddev(col(col_name)).alias("stddev"),
                min(col(col_name)).alias("min"),
                max(col(col_name)).alias("max"),
                expr(f"percentile_approx({col_name}, 0.25)").alias("q1"),
                expr(f"percentile_approx({col_name}, 0.50)").alias("median"),
                expr(f"percentile_approx({col_name}, 0.75)").alias("q3")
            ).collect()[0]
            
            # Calculate statistics for target
            target_stats = self.target_df.select(
                mean(col(col_name)).alias("mean"),
                stddev(col(col_name)).alias("stddev"),
                min(col(col_name)).alias("min"),
                max(col(col_name)).alias("max"),
                expr(f"percentile_approx({col_name}, 0.25)").alias("q1"),
                expr(f"percentile_approx({col_name}, 0.50)").alias("median"),
                expr(f"percentile_approx({col_name}, 0.75)").alias("q3")
            ).collect()[0]
            
            # Calculate differences
            results.append({
                "column": col_name,
                "metric": "mean",
                "source_value": float(source_stats["mean"]) if source_stats["mean"] else None,
                "target_value": float(target_stats["mean"]) if target_stats["mean"] else None,
                "difference": float(source_stats["mean"] - target_stats["mean"]) 
                             if source_stats["mean"] and target_stats["mean"] else None
            })
            
            results.append({
                "column": col_name,
                "metric": "stddev",
                "source_value": float(source_stats["stddev"]) if source_stats["stddev"] else None,
                "target_value": float(target_stats["stddev"]) if target_stats["stddev"] else None,
                "difference": float(source_stats["stddev"] - target_stats["stddev"]) 
                             if source_stats["stddev"] and target_stats["stddev"] else None
            })
```python
            
            results.append({
                "column": col_name,
                "metric": "min",

                "target_value": float(target_stats["min"]) if target_stats["min"] else None,
                "difference": float(source_stats["min"] - target_stats["min"]) 
                             if source_stats["min"] and target_stats["min"] else None
            })
