"""
Lambda Architecture:
Maintains both batch and speed layers for serving layer queries.
Batch layer: Comprehensive, accurate historical views
Speed layer: Real-time, incremental updates
Serving layer: Merges both for complete view
"""

class LambdaArchitecture:
    """
    Refined Lambda Architecture implementation for real-time analytics
    Use case: Real-time website analytics with historical reporting
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.batch_view_path = "/tmp/lambda/batch_view"
        self.speed_view_path = "/tmp/lambda/speed_view"
        self.serving_view_path = "/tmp/lambda/serving_view"
        
    # ========== BATCH LAYER ==========
    def batch_layer_processing(self, start_date: str, end_date: str):
        """
        Batch Layer: Process historical data for accurate, complete views
        """
        # Simulate reading historical clickstream data
        clickstream_schema = StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("session_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("page_url", StringType(), False),
            StructField("event_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("device_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("referrer", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Generate sample batch data
        batch_data = self.spark.range(0, 100000) \
            .withColumn("user_id", concat(lit("USER-"), (col("id") % 1000).cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("session_id", concat(lit("SESS-"), col("id").cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("page_url", concat(lit("/page/"), (col("id") % 100).cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("event_type", 
                       when(rand() > 0.7, "click")
                       .when(rand() > 0.4, "view")
                       .otherwise("purchase")) \
            .withColumn("timestamp", 
                       (unix_timestamp(lit(start_date)) + (rand() * 86400)).cast("timestamp")) \
            .withColumn("device_type",
                       when(rand() > 0.6, "mobile")
                       .when(rand() > 0.3, "desktop")
                       .otherwise("tablet")) \
            .withColumn("referrer", 
                       when(rand() > 0.5, concat(lit("ref-"), (col("id") % 10).cast("string")))
                       .otherwise(lit(None)))
        
        # Batch layer computations - comprehensive aggregations
        batch_view = batch_data.groupBy("user_id", "device_type") \
            .agg(
                countDistinct("session_id").alias("total_sessions"),
                count("*").alias("total_events"),
                sum(when(col("event_type") == "view", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("page_views"),
                sum(when(col("event_type") == "click", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("clicks"),
                sum(when(col("event_type") == "purchase", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("purchases"),
                countDistinct("page_url").alias("unique_pages"),
                min("timestamp").alias("first_seen"),
                max("timestamp").alias("last_seen")
            ) \
            .withColumn("engagement_score", 
                       (col("clicks") * 2 + col("purchases") * 10) / col("total_events")) \
            .withColumn("batch_processed_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("view_type", lit("batch"))
        
        # Write batch view
        batch_view.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("device_type") \
            .parquet(self.batch_view_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Batch layer processed: {batch_view.count()} user profiles")
        return batch_view
    
    # ========== SPEED LAYER ==========
    def speed_layer_processing(self):
        """
        Speed Layer: Process real-time incremental updates
        """
        # Setup streaming source
        speed_stream = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 100) \
            .load() \
            .withColumn("user_id", concat(lit("USER-"), (col("value") % 1000).cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("session_id", concat(lit("SESS-"), col("value").cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("page_url", concat(lit("/page/"), (col("value") % 100).cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("event_type",
                       when(rand() > 0.7, "click")
                       .when(rand() > 0.4, "view")
                       .otherwise("purchase")) \
            .withColumn("device_type",
                       when(rand() > 0.6, "mobile")
                       .when(rand() > 0.3, "desktop")
                       .otherwise("tablet"))
        
        # Speed layer - incremental aggregations with watermarking
        speed_view = speed_stream \
            .withWatermark("timestamp", "5 minutes") \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("timestamp"), "1 minute"),
                "user_id",
                "device_type"
            ) \
            .agg(
                countDistinct("session_id").alias("recent_sessions"),
                count("*").alias("recent_events"),
                sum(when(col("event_type") == "view", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("recent_views"),
                sum(when(col("event_type") == "click", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("recent_clicks"),
                sum(when(col("event_type") == "purchase", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("recent_purchases")
            ) \
            .withColumn("speed_processed_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("view_type", lit("speed")) \
            .withColumn("window_start", col("window.start")) \
            .withColumn("window_end", col("window.end")) \
            .drop("window")
        
        return speed_view
    
    # ========== SERVING LAYER ==========
    def serving_layer_merge(self, batch_df, speed_df):
        """
        Serving Layer: Merge batch and speed views for queries
        """
        # Read latest batch view
        batch_view = self.spark.read.parquet(self.batch_view_path)
        
        # Merge batch and speed layers
        serving_view = batch_view.alias("batch") \
            .join(
                speed_df.alias("speed"),
                (col("batch.user_id") == col("speed.user_id")) &
                (col("batch.device_type") == col("speed.device_type")),
                "left_outer"
            ) \
            .select(
                col("batch.user_id"),
                col("batch.device_type"),
                # Batch metrics
                col("batch.total_sessions"),
                col("batch.total_events"),
                col("batch.page_views"),
                col("batch.clicks"),
                col("batch.purchases"),
                col("batch.engagement_score"),
                # Speed metrics (recent activity)
                coalesce(col("speed.recent_sessions"), lit(0)).alias("recent_sessions"),
                coalesce(col("speed.recent_events"), lit(0)).alias("recent_events"),
                coalesce(col("speed.recent_views"), lit(0)).alias("recent_views"),
                coalesce(col("speed.recent_clicks"), lit(0)).alias("recent_clicks"),
                coalesce(col("speed.recent_purchases"), lit(0)).alias("recent_purchases"),
                # Combined metrics
                (col("batch.total_events") + coalesce(col("speed.recent_events"), lit(0)))
                    .alias("combined_total_events"),
                (col("batch.purchases") + coalesce(col("speed.recent_purchases"), lit(0)))
                    .alias("combined_purchases"),
                current_timestamp().alias("serving_timestamp")
            )
        
        return serving_view
    
    def run_lambda_architecture(self):
        """Execute complete Lambda Architecture"""
        # Process batch layer
        batch_df = self.batch_layer_processing("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02")
        
        # Start speed layer
        speed_df = self.speed_layer_processing()
        
        # Merge in serving layer and write
        serving_query = speed_df.writeStream \
            .foreachBatch(lambda batch_df, batch_id: 
                         self._process_serving_batch(batch_df, batch_id)) \
            .outputMode("update") \
            .option("checkpointLocation", "/tmp
```python
            .option("checkpointLocation", "/tmp/lambda/checkpoint") \
            .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        print("✓ Lambda Architecture pipeline started")
        return serving_query
    
    def _process_serving_batch(self, batch_df, batch_id):
        """Helper to process each micro-batch in serving layer"""
        if batch_df.count() > 0:
            batch_view = self.spark.read.parquet(self.batch_view_path)
            serving_view = self.serving_layer_merge(batch_view, batch_df)
            
            # Write to serving layer
            serving_view.write \
                .mode("append") \
                .partitionBy("device_type") \
                .parquet(f"{self.serving_view_path}/batch_{batch_id}")
            
            print(f"✓ Serving layer updated for batch {batch_id}")

# PATTERN 3: Kappa Architecture (Refined)
# ============================================================================
"""
Kappa Architecture:
Simplified architecture using only streaming processing.
All data (historical and real-time) flows through the same streaming pipeline.
Reprocessing is done by replaying the event log.
"""

class KappaArchitecture:
    """
    Refined Kappa Architecture - Everything is a stream
    Use case: IoT sensor data processing with reprocessing capabilities
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.event_log_path = "/tmp/kappa/event_log"
        self.materialized_view_path = "/tmp/kappa/views"
        self.checkpoint_path = "/tmp/kappa/checkpoint"
        
    def ingest_to_event_log(self):
        """
        Ingest all data into immutable event log (Kafka-like simulation)
        """
        # Simulate IoT sensor data stream
        sensor_stream = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \
            .load() \
            .withColumn("sensor_id", concat(lit("SENSOR-"), (col("value") % 100).cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("location", concat(lit("LOC-"), (col("value") % 20).cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("temperature", (rand() * 40 + 10).cast("double")) \
            .withColumn("humidity", (rand() * 100).cast("double")) \
            .withColumn("pressure", (rand() * 200 + 900).cast("double")) \
            .withColumn("event_time", col("timestamp")) \
            .withColumn("event_id", monotonically_increasing_id()) \
            .select("event_id", "sensor_id", "location", "temperature", 
                   "humidity", "pressure", "event_time")
        
        # Write to event log (immutable append-only log)
        event_log_query = sensor_stream.writeStream \
            .format("parquet") \
            .outputMode("append") \
            .option("path", self.event_log_path) \
            .option("checkpointLocation", f"{self.checkpoint_path}/event_log") \
            .partitionBy("sensor_id") \
            .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        print("✓ Event log ingestion started")
        return event_log_query
    
    def create_materialized_view_v1(self):
        """
        Version 1: Simple aggregations per sensor
        """
        # Read from event log as a stream
        event_stream = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("parquet") \
            .schema(StructType([
                StructField("event_id", LongType(), False),
                StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), False),
                StructField("location", StringType(), False),
                StructField("temperature", DoubleType(), False),
                StructField("humidity", DoubleType(), False),
                StructField("pressure", DoubleType(), False),
                StructField("event_time", TimestampType(), False)
            ])) \
            .load(self.event_log_path)
        
        # Materialized view: Sensor statistics
        view_v1 = event_stream \
            .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("event_time"), "5 minutes"),
                "sensor_id",
                "location"
            ) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("reading_count"),
                avg("temperature").alias("avg_temperature"),
                min("temperature").alias("min_temperature"),
                max("temperature").alias("max_temperature"),
                avg("humidity").alias("avg_humidity"),
                avg("pressure").alias("avg_pressure"),
                stddev("temperature").alias("temp_stddev")
            ) \
            .withColumn("view_version", lit("v1")) \
            .withColumn("materialized_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("window_start", col("window.start")) \
            .withColumn("window_end", col("window.end")) \
            .drop("window")
        
        return view_v1
    
    def create_materialized_view_v2(self):
        """
        Version 2: Enhanced view with anomaly detection
        This demonstrates reprocessing with new logic
        """
        # Read from same event log
        event_stream = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("parquet") \
            .schema(StructType([
                StructField("event_id", LongType(), False),
                StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), False),
                StructField("location", StringType(), False),
                StructField("temperature", DoubleType(), False),
                StructField("humidity", DoubleType(), False),
                StructField("pressure", DoubleType(), False),
                StructField("event_time", TimestampType(), False)
            ])) \
            .load(self.event_log_path)
        
        # Enhanced view with anomaly detection
        view_v2 = event_stream \
            .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("event_time"), "5 minutes"),
                "sensor_id",
                "location"
            ) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("reading_count"),
                avg("temperature").alias("avg_temperature"),
                min("temperature").alias("min_temperature"),
                max("temperature").alias("max_temperature"),
                avg("humidity").alias("avg_humidity"),
                avg("pressure").alias("avg_pressure"),
                stddev("temperature").alias("temp_stddev"),
                # New metrics for anomaly detection
                percentile_approx("temperature", 0.95).alias("temp_p95"),
                percentile_approx("temperature", 0.05).alias("temp_p05"),
                sum(when(col("temperature") > 35, 1).otherwise(0)).alias("high_temp_count"),
                sum(when(col("temperature") < 15, 1).otherwise(0)).alias("low_temp_count")
            ) \
            .withColumn("temp_range", col("max_temperature") - col("min_temperature")) \
            .withColumn("anomaly_score",
                       (col("high_temp_count") + col("low_temp_count")) / col("reading_count")) \
            .withColumn("is_anomalous", 
                       when(col("anomaly_score") > 0.3, True).otherwise(False)) \
            .withColumn("view_version", lit("v2")) \
            .withColumn("materialized_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("window_start", col("window.start")) \
            .withColumn("window_end", col("window.end")) \
            .drop("window")
        
        return view_v2
    
    def reprocess_event_log(self, view_version: str, start_time: str = None):
        """
        Reprocess the event log to create new/updated materialized views
        This is the key advantage of Kappa - easy reprocessing
        """
        print(f"🔄 Reprocessing event log for view version: {view_version}")
        
        if view_version == "v1":
            view_df = self.create_materialized_view_v1()
        elif view_version == "v2":
            view_df = self.create_materialized_view_v2()
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown view version: {view_version}")
        
        # Write materialized view
        query = view_df.writeStream \
            .format("parquet") \
            .outputMode("append") \
            .option("path", f"{self.materialized_view_path}/{view_version}") \
            .option("checkpointLocation", f"{self.checkpoint_path}/{view_version}") \
            .partitionBy("sensor_id") \
            .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        print(f"✓ Materialized view {view_version} processing started")
        return query
    
    def run_kappa_architecture(self):
        """Execute Kappa Architecture pipeline"""
        # Start event log ingestion
        event_log_query = self.ingest_to_event_log()
        
        # Create initial materialized view
        view_v1_query = self.reprocess_event_log("v1")
        
        # Later, can reprocess with new logic
        # view_v2_query = self.reprocess_event_log("v2")
        
        print("✓ Kappa Architecture pipeline started")
        return event_log_query, view_v1_query


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: Batch Reprocessing Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Batch Reprocessing Pattern:
Handles reprocessing of historical data when business logic changes
or data quality issues are discovered.
"""

class BatchReprocessingPattern:
    """
    Systematic approach to reprocessing batches of data
    Use case: Financial transaction processing with audit corrections
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.raw_data_path = "/tmp/reprocess/raw"
        self.processed_data_path = "/tmp/reprocess/processed"
        self.audit_log_path = "/tmp/reprocess/audit"
        
    def generate_raw_transactions(self, num_records: int = 10000):
        """Generate sample raw transaction data"""
        transactions = self.spark.range(0, num_records) \
            .withColumn("transaction_id", concat(lit("TXN-"), col("id").cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("account_id", concat(lit("ACC-"), (col("id") % 500).cast("string"))) \
            .withColumn("amount", (rand() * 10000 - 5000).cast("decimal(10,2)")) \
            .withColumn("transaction_type",
                       when(col("amount") > 0, "credit").otherwise("debit")) \
            .withColumn("currency", 
                       when(rand() > 0.7, "EUR")
                       .when(rand() > 0.4, "GBP")
                       .otherwise("USD")) \
            .withColumn("transaction_date", 
                       (unix_timestamp(lit("2024-01-01")) + (col("id") * 100)).cast("timestamp")) \
            .withColumn("status", lit("pending")) \
            .withColumn("processing_version", lit("v1")) \
            .select("transaction_id", "account_id", "amount", "transaction_type",
                   "currency", "transaction_date", "status", "processing_version")
        
        # Write raw data
        transactions.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("currency") \
            .parquet(self.raw_data_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Generated {num_records} raw transactions")
        return transactions
    
    def process_batch_v1(self, batch_date: str):
        """
        Version 1: Initial processing logic
        Simple currency conversion and categorization
        """
        # Read raw data
        raw_data = self.spark.read.parquet(self.raw_data_path)
        
        # V1 Processing logic
        processed_v1 = raw_data \
            .withColumn("amount_usd",
                       when(col("currency") == "EUR", col("amount") * 1.1)
                       .when(col("currency") == "GBP", col("amount") * 1.25)
                       .otherwise(col("amount"))) \
            .withColumn("category",
                       when(abs(col("amount")) < 100, "small")
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) < 1000, "medium")
                       .otherwise("large")) \
            .withColumn("risk_score",
                       when(abs(col("amount")) > 5000, lit(0.8))
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) > 1000, lit(0.5))
                       .otherwise(lit(0.2))) \
            .withColumn("processed_date", lit(batch_date)) \
            .withColumn("processing_version", lit("v1"))
        
        # Write processed data
        processed_v1.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("currency", "category") \
            .parquet(f"{self.processed_data_path}/v1")
        
        print(f"✓ Batch processed with V1 logic: {processed_v1.count()} records")
        return processed_v1
    
    def process_batch_v2(self, batch_date: str):
        """
        Version 2: Enhanced processing logic with corrections
        Updated currency rates and improved risk scoring
        """
        # Read raw data
        raw_data = self.spark.read.parquet(self.raw_data_path)
        
        # V2 Processing logic with corrections
        processed_v2 = raw_data \
            .withColumn("amount_usd",
                       # Updated exchange rates
                       when(col("currency") == "EUR", col("amount") * 1.08)
                       .when(col("currency") == "GBP", col("amount") * 1.27)
                       .otherwise(col("amount"))) \
            .withColumn("category",
                       # Updated categorization thresholds
                       when(abs(col("amount")) < 50, "micro")
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) < 500, "small")
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) < 2000, "medium")
                       .otherwise("large")) \
            .withColumn("risk_score",
                       # Enhanced risk scoring with multiple factors
                       when(abs(col("amount")) > 8000, lit(0.95))
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) > 5000, lit(0.75))
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) > 2000, lit(0.50))
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) > 500, lit(0.30))
                       .otherwise(lit(0.10))) \
            .withColumn("requires_review",
                       when(col("risk_score") > 0.7, True).otherwise(False)) \
            .withColumn("processed_date", lit(batch_date)) \
            .withColumn("processing_version", lit("v2"))
        
        # Write processed data
        processed_v2.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("currency", "category") \
            .parquet(f"{self.processed_data_path}/v2")
        
        print(f"✓ Batch reprocessed with V2 logic: {processed_v2
```python
.count()} records")
        return processed_v2
    
    def create_reprocessing_audit_log(self, v1_df, v2_df):
        """
        Create audit log comparing V1 and V2 processing results
        Identifies differences for reconciliation
        """
        # Join V1 and V2 results for comparison
        audit_log = v1_df.alias("v1") \
            .join(
                v2_df.alias("v2"),
                col("v1.transaction_id") == col("v2.transaction_id"),
                "inner"
            ) \
            .select(
                col("v1.transaction_id"),
                col("v1.account_id"),
                col("v1.amount"),
                col("v1.currency"),
                # V1 values
                col("v1.amount_usd").alias("v1_amount_usd"),
                col("v1.category").alias("v1_category"),
                col("v1.risk_score").alias("v1_risk_score"),
                # V2 values
                col("v2.amount_usd").alias("v2_amount_usd"),
                col("v2.category").alias("v2_category"),
                col("v2.risk_score").alias("v2_risk_score"),
                col("v2.requires_review")
            ) \
            .withColumn("amount_usd_changed",
                       col("v1_amount_usd") != col("v2_amount_usd")) \
            .withColumn("category_changed",
                       col("v1_category") != col("v2_category")) \
            .withColumn("risk_score_changed",
                       col("v1_risk_score") != col("v2_risk_score")) \
            .withColumn("amount_usd_diff",
                       col("v2_amount_usd") - col("v1_amount_usd")) \
            .withColumn("risk_score_diff",
                       col("v2_risk_score") - col("v1_risk_score")) \
            .withColumn("has_changes",
                       col("amount_usd_changed") | 
                       col("category_changed") | 
                       col("risk_score_changed")) \
            .withColumn("audit_timestamp", current_timestamp())
        
        # Write audit log
        audit_log.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(self.audit_log_path)
        
        # Summary statistics
        changes_summary = audit_log.agg(
            count("*").alias("total_records"),
            sum(when(col("has_changes"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("records_with_changes"),
            sum(when(col("amount_usd_changed"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("amount_changes"),
            sum(when(col("category_changed"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("category_changes"),
            sum(when(col("risk_score_changed"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("risk_score_changes"),
            avg("amount_usd_diff").alias("avg_amount_diff"),
            avg("risk_score_diff").alias("avg_risk_score_diff")
        )
        
        print("📊 Reprocessing Audit Summary:")
        changes_summary.show(truncate=False)
        
        return audit_log
    
    def incremental_reprocessing(self, start_date: str, end_date: str, partition_key: str):
        """
        Reprocess only specific partitions instead of full dataset
        More efficient for large datasets
        """
        print(f"🔄 Incremental reprocessing for {partition_key}")
        
        # Read only specific partition
        raw_data = self.spark.read \
            .parquet(self.raw_data_path) \
            .filter(col("currency") == partition_key)
        
        # Apply V2 processing logic
        reprocessed = raw_data \
            .withColumn("amount_usd",
                       when(col("currency") == "EUR", col("amount") * 1.08)
                       .when(col("currency") == "GBP", col("amount") * 1.27)
                       .otherwise(col("amount"))) \
            .withColumn("category",
                       when(abs(col("amount")) < 50, "micro")
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) < 500, "small")
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) < 2000, "medium")
                       .otherwise("large")) \
            .withColumn("risk_score",
                       when(abs(col("amount")) > 8000, lit(0.95))
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) > 5000, lit(0.75))
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) > 2000, lit(0.50))
                       .when(abs(col("amount")) > 500, lit(0.30))
                       .otherwise(lit(0.10))) \
            .withColumn("requires_review",
                       when(col("risk_score") > 0.7, True).otherwise(False)) \
            .withColumn("reprocessed_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("processing_version", lit("v2_incremental"))
        
        # Write back to same partition (overwrite mode for that partition)
        reprocessed.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("currency", "category") \
            .parquet(f"{self.processed_data_path}/v2_incremental")
        
        print(f"✓ Incremental reprocessing complete for {partition_key}: {reprocessed.count()} records")
        return reprocessed
    
    def run_reprocessing_pipeline(self):
        """Execute complete reprocessing pipeline"""
        # Generate raw data
        self.generate_raw_transactions(10000)
        
        # Initial processing with V1
        v1_df = self.process_batch_v1("2024-01-01")
        
        # Reprocess with V2 (corrected logic)
        v2_df = self.process_batch_v2("2024-01-01")
        
        # Create audit log
        audit_log = self.create_reprocessing_audit_log(v1_df, v2_df)
        
        # Demonstrate incremental reprocessing
        self.incremental_reprocessing("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02", "USD")
        
        print("✓ Batch reprocessing pipeline completed")


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: Late Binding Schema Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Late Binding Schema Pattern:
Schema is applied at read time rather than write time.
Allows flexibility in handling evolving data structures.
"""

class LateBindingSchemaPattern:
    """
    Late binding schema for flexible data processing
    Use case: Multi-tenant SaaS application with varying data structures
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.raw_data_path = "/tmp/late_binding/raw"
        self.schema_registry_path = "/tmp/late_binding/schemas"
        self.processed_data_path = "/tmp/late_binding/processed"
        
    def write_schema_agnostic_data(self):
        """
        Write data in schema-agnostic format (JSON with varying structures)
        Simulates data from different tenants with different schemas
        """
        # Tenant 1: E-commerce events
        tenant1_data = self.spark.range(0, 1000) \
            .withColumn("tenant_id", lit("tenant_1")) \
            .withColumn("event_type", lit("ecommerce")) \
            .withColumn("data", 
                       to_json(struct(
                           concat(lit("ORDER-"), col("id").cast("string")).alias("order_id"),
                           concat(lit("CUST-"), (col("id") % 100).cast("string")).alias("customer_id"),
                           (rand() * 1000).cast("decimal(10,2)").alias("amount"),
                           when(rand() > 0.5, "completed").otherwise("pending").alias("status"),
                           array(
                               concat(lit("PROD-"), (col("id") % 50).cast("string"))
                           ).alias("products")
                       ))) \
            .withColumn("ingested_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("schema_version", lit("1.0"))
        
        # Tenant 2: User activity events (different schema)
        tenant2_data = self.spark.range(0, 1000) \
            .withColumn("tenant_id", lit("tenant_2")) \
            .withColumn("event_type", lit("user_activity")) \
            .withColumn("data",
                       to_json(struct(
                           concat(lit("USER-"), col("id").cast("string")).alias("user_id"),
                           concat(lit("SESSION-"), col("id").cast("string")).alias("session_id"),
                           when(rand() > 0.6, "click")
                               .when(rand() > 0.3, "view")
                               .otherwise("scroll").alias("action"),
                           concat(lit("/page/"), (col("id") % 20).cast("string")).alias("page_url"),
                           (rand() * 300).cast("int").alias("duration_seconds")
                       ))) \
            .withColumn("ingested_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("schema_version", lit("1.0"))
        
        # Tenant 3: IoT sensor data (yet another schema)
        tenant3_data = self.spark.range(0, 1000) \
            .withColumn("tenant_id", lit("tenant_3")) \
            .withColumn("event_type", lit("iot_sensor")) \
            .withColumn("data",
                       to_json(struct(
                           concat(lit("DEVICE-"), (col("id") % 50).cast("string")).alias("device_id"),
                           (rand() * 40 + 10).cast("decimal(5,2)").alias("temperature"),
                           (rand() * 100).cast("decimal(5,2)").alias("humidity"),
                           struct(
                               (rand() * 180 - 90).cast("decimal(8,6)").alias("latitude"),
                               (rand() * 360 - 180).cast("decimal(9,6)").alias("longitude")
                           ).alias("location"),
                           when(rand() > 0.9, "alert").otherwise("normal").alias("status")
                       ))) \
            .withColumn("ingested_at", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("schema_version", lit("1.0"))
        
        # Union all tenant data
        all_data = tenant1_data.union(tenant2_data).union(tenant3_data)
        
        # Write in schema-agnostic format
        all_data.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("tenant_id", "event_type") \
            .parquet(self.raw_data_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Written {all_data.count()} schema-agnostic records")
        return all_data
    
    def register_schema(self, tenant_id: str, event_type: str, schema: StructType, version: str):
        """
        Register schema for a specific tenant and event type
        Schema registry for late binding
        """
        schema_info = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (tenant_id, event_type, schema.json(), version, datetime.now())
        ], ["tenant_id", "event_type", "schema_json", "version", "registered_at"])
        
        schema_info.write \
            .mode("append") \
            .partitionBy("tenant_id", "event_type") \
            .parquet(self.schema_registry_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Schema registered for {tenant_id}/{event_type} version {version}")
    
    def apply_late_binding_schema(self, tenant_id: str, event_type: str):
        """
        Apply schema at read time based on tenant and event type
        """
        # Read raw data for specific tenant
        raw_data = self.spark.read \
            .parquet(self.raw_data_path) \
            .filter((col("tenant_id") == tenant_id) & (col("event_type") == event_type))
        
        # Define schemas for different event types
        if event_type == "ecommerce":
            # Apply e-commerce schema
            parsed_data = raw_data \
                .withColumn("parsed", from_json(col("data"), 
                    StructType([
                        StructField("order_id", StringType()),
                        StructField("customer_id", StringType()),
                        StructField("amount", DecimalType(10, 2)),
                        StructField("status", StringType()),
                        StructField("products", ArrayType(StringType()))
                    ]))) \
                .select(
                    col("tenant_id"),
                    col("event_type"),
                    col("parsed.order_id"),
                    col("parsed.customer_id"),
                    col("parsed.amount"),
                    col("parsed.status"),
                    col("parsed.products"),
                    col("ingested_at"),
                    col("schema_version")
                ) \
                .withColumn("processing_type", lit("late_binding"))
            
        elif event_type == "user_activity":
            # Apply user activity schema
            parsed_data = raw_data \
                .withColumn("parsed", from_json(col("data"),
                    StructType([
                        StructField("user_id", StringType()),
                        StructField("session_id", StringType()),
                        StructField("action", StringType()),
                        StructField("page_url", StringType()),
                        StructField("duration_seconds", IntegerType())
                    ]))) \
                .select(
                    col("tenant_id"),
                    col("event_type"),
                    col("parsed.user_id"),
                    col("parsed.session_id"),
                    col("parsed.action"),
                    col("parsed.page_url"),
                    col("parsed.duration_seconds"),
                    col("ingested_at"),
                    col("schema_version")
                ) \
                .withColumn("processing_type", lit("late_binding"))
            
        elif event_type == "iot_sensor":
            # Apply IoT sensor schema
            parsed_data = raw_data \
                .withColumn("parsed", from_json(col("data"),
                    StructType([
                        StructField("device_id", StringType()),
                        StructField("temperature", DecimalType(5, 2)),
                        StructField("humidity", DecimalType(5, 2)),
                        StructField("location", StructType([
                            StructField("latitude", DecimalType(8, 6)),
                            StructField("longitude", DecimalType(9, 6))
                        ])),
                        StructField("status", StringType())
                    ]))) \
                .select(
                    col("tenant_id"),
                    col("event_type"),
                    col("parsed.device_id"),
                    col("parsed.temperature"),
                    col("parsed.humidity"),
                    col("parsed.location.latitude").alias("latitude"),
                    col("parsed.location.longitude").alias("longitude"),
                    col("parsed.status"),
                    col("ingested_at"),
                    col("schema_version")
                ) \
                .withColumn("processing_type", lit("late_binding"))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown event type: {event_type}")
        
        return parsed_data
    
    def process_with_schema_evolution(self, tenant_id: str, event_type: str, schema_version: str):
        
```python
        """
        Handle schema evolution by applying different schemas based on version
        """
        # Read raw data
        raw_data = self.spark.read \
            .parquet(self.raw_data_path) \
            .filter((col("tenant_id") == tenant_id) & (col("event_type") == event_type))
        
        if event_type == "ecommerce":
            if schema_version == "1.0":
                # Original schema
                schema = StructType([
                    StructField("order_id", StringType()),
                    StructField("customer_id", StringType()),
                    StructField("amount", DecimalType(10, 2)),
                    StructField("status", StringType()),
                    StructField("products", ArrayType(StringType()))
                ])
            elif schema_version == "2.0":
                # Evolved schema with additional fields
                schema = StructType([
                    StructField("order_id", StringType()),
                    StructField("customer_id", StringType()),
                    StructField("amount", DecimalType(10, 2)),
                    StructField("status", StringType()),
                    StructField("products", ArrayType(StringType())),
                    StructField("discount_code", StringType()),  # New field
                    StructField("shipping_address", StructType([  # New nested field
                        StructField("street", StringType()),
                        StructField("city", StringType()),
                        StructField("country", StringType())
                    ])),
                    StructField("payment_method", StringType())  # New field
                ])
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported schema version: {schema_version}")
            
            # Parse with appropriate schema
            parsed_data = raw_data \
                .withColumn("parsed", from_json(col("data"), schema)) \
                .select(
                    col("tenant_id"),
                    col("event_type"),
                    col("schema_version"),
                    col("parsed.*"),
                    col("ingested_at")
                )
        
        return parsed_data
    
    def dynamic_schema_inference(self, tenant_id: str, event_type: str):
        """
        Dynamically infer schema from data at runtime
        Useful when schema is completely unknown
        """
        # Read raw data
        raw_data = self.spark.read \
            .parquet(self.raw_data_path) \
            .filter((col("tenant_id") == tenant_id) & (col("event_type") == event_type))
        
        # Infer schema from JSON data
        sample_data = raw_data.limit(100).select("data").collect()
        
        if sample_data:
            # Use Spark's schema inference
            json_df = self.spark.read.json(
                self.spark.sparkContext.parallelize([row.data for row in sample_data])
            )
            
            inferred_schema = json_df.schema
            print(f"📋 Inferred schema for {tenant_id}/{event_type}:")
            print(inferred_schema.simpleString())
            
            # Apply inferred schema to all data
            parsed_data = raw_data \
                .withColumn("parsed", from_json(col("data"), inferred_schema)) \
                .select(
                    col("tenant_id"),
                    col("event_type"),
                    col("parsed.*"),
                    col("ingested_at"),
                    col("schema_version")
                )
            
            return parsed_data, inferred_schema
        else:
            raise ValueError("No data found for schema inference")
    
    def process_multi_tenant_data(self):
        """
        Process data from multiple tenants with different schemas
        using late binding pattern
        """
        results = {}
        
        # Process each tenant's data with appropriate schema
        tenants_config = [
            ("tenant_1", "ecommerce"),
            ("tenant_2", "user_activity"),
            ("tenant_3", "iot_sensor")
        ]
        
        for tenant_id, event_type in tenants_config:
            print(f"\n🔄 Processing {tenant_id}/{event_type}")
            
            # Apply late binding schema
            parsed_data = self.apply_late_binding_schema(tenant_id, event_type)
            
            # Write processed data
            parsed_data.write \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .partitionBy("tenant_id", "event_type") \
                .parquet(f"{self.processed_data_path}/{tenant_id}_{event_type}")
            
            results[f"{tenant_id}_{event_type}"] = parsed_data.count()
            print(f"✓ Processed {results[f'{tenant_id}_{event_type}']} records")
        
        return results
    
    def handle_schema_mismatch(self, tenant_id: str, event_type: str):
        """
        Handle cases where data doesn't match expected schema
        Implements fallback and error handling
        """
        raw_data = self.spark.read \
            .parquet(self.raw_data_path) \
            .filter((col("tenant_id") == tenant_id) & (col("event_type") == event_type))
        
        # Define expected schema
        expected_schema = StructType([
            StructField("order_id", StringType()),
            StructField("customer_id", StringType()),
            StructField("amount", DecimalType(10, 2)),
            StructField("status", StringType())
        ])
        
        # Try to parse with schema, capture errors
        parsed_data = raw_data \
            .withColumn("parsed", 
                       when(
                           from_json(col("data"), expected_schema).isNotNull(),
                           from_json(col("data"), expected_schema)
                       ).otherwise(lit(None))) \
            .withColumn("parse_success", col("parsed").isNotNull()) \
            .withColumn("error_reason",
                       when(col("parsed").isNull(), lit("Schema mismatch"))
                       .otherwise(lit(None)))
        
        # Separate successful and failed parses
        successful = parsed_data.filter(col("parse_success") == True) \
            .select(
                col("tenant_id"),
                col("event_type"),
                col("parsed.*"),
                col("ingested_at")
            )
        
        failed = parsed_data.filter(col("parse_success") == False) \
            .select(
                col("tenant_id"),
                col("event_type"),
                col("data"),
                col("error_reason"),
                col("ingested_at")
            )
        
        print(f"✓ Successful parses: {successful.count()}")
        print(f"✗ Failed parses: {failed.count()}")
        
        # Write failed records to error queue for investigation
        if failed.count() > 0:
            failed.write \
                .mode("append") \
                .parquet(f"{self.processed_data_path}/errors")
        
        return successful, failed
    
    def run_late_binding_pipeline(self):
        """Execute complete late binding schema pipeline"""
        # Write schema-agnostic data
        self.write_schema_agnostic_data()
        
        # Process multi-tenant data with late binding
        results = self.process_multi_tenant_data()
        
        # Demonstrate dynamic schema inference
        print("\n🔍 Dynamic Schema Inference Example:")
        inferred_data, schema = self.dynamic_schema_inference("tenant_1", "ecommerce")
        print(f"✓ Inferred and processed {inferred_data.count()} records")
        
        # Demonstrate schema mismatch handling
        print("\n⚠️ Schema Mismatch Handling Example:")
        successful, failed = self.handle_schema_mismatch("tenant_1", "ecommerce")
        
        print("\n✓ Late binding schema pipeline completed")
        return results

class StaticMasking:
    """
    Static masking replaces sensitive data with fixed masked values.
    Data is permanently masked and cannot be reversed.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def mask_ssn(ssn_col):
        """Mask SSN keeping only last 4 digits"""
        return concat(lit("XXX-XX-"), substring(ssn_col, -4, 4))
    
    @staticmethod
    def mask_email(email_col):
        """Mask email keeping domain"""
        return concat(
            lit("masked_"),
            md5(email_col),
            lit("@"),
            expr("split(email, '@')[1]")
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def mask_credit_card(cc_col):
        """Mask credit card showing only last 4 digits"""
        return concat(lit("XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-"), substring(cc_col, -4, 4))
    
    @staticmethod
    def mask_phone(phone_col):
        """Mask phone number"""
        return lit("XXX-XXXX")
    
    @staticmethod
    def mask_name(name_col):
        """Replace name with generic value"""
        return lit("MASKED")
    
    @staticmethod
    def mask_address(address_col):
        """Mask address completely"""
        return lit("XXX XXXXX XX")
    
    @staticmethod
    def mask_salary(salary_col):
        """Round salary to nearest 10000"""
        return (col(salary_col) / 10000).cast(IntegerType()) * 10000

# Apply static masking
static_masked_df = df.select(
    col("id"),
    StaticMasking.mask_name("first_name").alias("first_name"),

class DynamicMasking:
    """
    Dynamic masking applies different masking rules based on user roles.
    Masking happens at query time, original data remains unchanged.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def apply_role_based_masking(df, user_role):
        """
        Apply masking based on user role:
        - ADMIN: See all data
        - MANAGER: See partial masking
        - USER: See full masking
        """
        
        if user_role == "ADMIN":
            # Admin sees everything
            return df
        
        elif user_role == "MANAGER":
            # Manager sees partial data
            return df.select(
                col("id"),
                col("first_name"),
                col("last_name"),
                # Partial email masking
                concat(substring("email", 1, 3), lit("***@"), 
                       expr("split(email, '@')[1]")).alias("email"),
                # Show last 4 of SSN
                concat(lit("XXX-XX-"), substring("ssn", -4, 4)).alias("ssn"),
                col("phone"),
                # Partial address masking
                regexp_replace("address", r"\d+", "XXX").alias("address"),
                concat(lit("XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-"), 
                       substring("credit_card", -4, 4)).alias("credit_card"),
                # Salary range instead of exact
                when(col("salary") < 70000, lit("< 70K"))
                .when(col("salary") < 80000, lit("70K-80K"))
                .otherwise(lit("> 80K")).alias("salary"),
                col("hire_date")
            )
        
        else:  # USER or default
            # Regular user sees fully masked data
            return df.select(
                col("id"),
                lit("MASKED").alias("first_name"),
                lit("MASKED").alias("last_name"),
                lit("masked@email.com").alias("email"),
                lit("XXX-XX-XXXX").alias("ssn"),
                lit("XXX-XXXX").alias("phone"),
                lit("XXXXX").alias("address"),
                lit("XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX").alias("credit_card"),
                lit(0).alias("salary"),
                col("hire_date")
            )

# Demonstrate dynamic masking for different roles

class FormatPreservingEncryption:
    """
    FPE maintains the format of the original data while encrypting it.
    Useful when downstream systems expect specific data formats.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def fpe_numeric(value, key="secret_key_123"):
        """
        Format-preserving encryption for numeric values
        Maintains same number of digits
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        
        # Simple FPE simulation using hash
        hash_val = int(hashlib.sha256(f"{value}{key}".encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        num_str = str(value).replace("-", "")
        num_digits = len(num_str)
        
        # Generate number with same length
        encrypted = str(hash_val)[:num_digits]
        
        # Restore format (e.g., XXX-XX-XXXX for SSN)
        if "-" in str(value):
            parts = str(value).split("-")
            result = ""
            pos = 0
            for i, part in enumerate(parts):
                result += encrypted[pos:pos+len(part)]
                if i < len(parts) - 1:
                    result += "-"
                pos += len(part)
            return result
        
        return encrypted
    
    @staticmethod
    def fpe_alpha(value, key="secret_key_123"):
        """
        Format-preserving encryption for alphabetic values
        Maintains case and length
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        
        result = ""
        hash_obj = hashlib.sha256(f"{value}{key}".encode())
        hash_bytes = hash_obj.digest()
        
        for i, char in enumerate(value):
            if char.isalpha():
                # Use hash to determine new character
                shift = hash_bytes[i % len(hash_bytes)] % 26
                if char.isupper():
                    result += chr((ord(char) - ord('A') + shift) % 26 + ord('A'))
                else:
                    result += chr((ord(char) - ord('a') + shift) % 26 + ord('a'))
            else:
                result += char
        
        return result

# UDFs for FPE
fpe_numeric_udf = udf(FormatPreservingEncryption.fpe_numeric, StringType())
fpe_alpha_udf = udf(FormatPreservingEncryption.fpe_alpha, StringType())

# Apply FPE

    col("id"),
    fpe_alpha_udf("first_name").alias("first_name"),

class SubstitutionMasking:
    """
    Substitution masking replaces real data with realistic synthetic data.
    Maintains data characteristics and relationships.
    """
    
    # Lookup tables for substitution
    FIRST_NAMES = ["Alex", "Sam", "Jordan", "Taylor", "Morgan", "Casey", "Riley"]
    LAST_NAMES = ["Anderson", "Baker", "Carter", "Davis", "Evans", "Foster", "Garcia"]
    DOMAINS = ["example.com", "test.com", "demo.com", "sample.com"]
    STREETS = ["100 First St", "200 Second Ave", "300 Third Blvd", 
               "400 Fourth Rd", "500 Fifth Ln"]
    
    @staticmethod
    def substitute_name(name, seed, name_list):
        """Consistently substitute name based on hash"""
        if name is None:
            return None
        hash_val = int(hashlib.md5(f"{name}{seed}".encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        return name_list[hash_val % len(name_list)]
    
    @staticmethod
    def substitute_email(first, last, domain_list):
        """Generate substitute email"""
        if first is None or last is None:
            return None
        hash_val = int(hashlib.md5(f"{first}{last}".encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        domain = domain_list[hash_val % len(domain_list)]
        return f"{first.lower()}.{last.lower()}@{domain}"
    
    @staticmethod
    def substitute_ssn(original_ssn):
        """Generate fake but valid-looking SSN"""
        if original_ssn is None:
            return None
        hash_val = int(hashlib.md5(original_ssn.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        # Generate 9 digits
        fake_ssn = str(hash_val)[:9]
        return f"{fake_ssn[:3]}-{fake_ssn[3:5]}-{fake_ssn[5:9]}"
    
    @staticmethod
    def substitute_phone(original_phone):
        """Generate fake phone number"""
        if original_phone is None:
            return None
        hash_val = int(hashlib.md5(original_phone.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        fake_phone = str(hash_val)[:7]
        return f"555-{fake_phone[:4]}"
    
    @staticmethod
    def substitute_credit_card(original_cc):
        """Generate fake credit card"""
        if original_cc is None:
            return None
        hash_val = int(hashlib.md5(original_cc.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        fake_cc = str(hash_val)[:16]
        return f"4532-{fake_cc[:4]}-{fake_cc[4:8]}-{

class ShufflingMasking:
    """
    Shuffling pattern randomizes values within columns while preserving
    the overall distribution and statistical properties.
    Breaks the relationship between columns.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def shuffle_column(df, column_name, seed=42):
        """
        Shuffle values in a specific column
        """
        # Add random value for shuffling
        shuffled = df.withColumn("shuffle_key", rand(seed))
        
        # Create window for row numbering
        window_original = Window.orderBy("id")
        window_shuffled = Window.orderBy("shuffle_key")
        
        # Get original and shuffled row numbers
        shuffled = shuffled.withColumn("original_row", row_number().over(window_original))
        shuffled = shuffled.withColumn("shuffled_row", row_number().over(window_shuffled))
        
        # Create mapping of shuffled values
        value_mapping = shuffled.select(
            col("shuffled_row").alias("row_num"),
            col(column_name).alias(f"shuffled_{column_name}")
        )
        
        # Join back to get shuffled values
        result = shuffled.join(
            value_mapping,
            shuffled.original_row == value_mapping.row_num,
            "left"
        ).select(
            df.columns + [f"shuffled_{column_name}"]
        )
        
        return result

# Apply shuffling to multiple columns
print("\nOriginal Data:")
df.select("id", "first_name", "last_name", "email", "ssn", "salary").show()

# Shuffle first names
shuffled_df = ShufflingMasking.shuffle_column(df, "first_name", seed=42)

# PATTERN 6: VARIANCE MASKING PATTERN
# Description: Adds random variance/noise to numerical data
# Use Case: Statistical analysis while protecting individual values
# =============================================================================

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PATTERN 6: VARIANCE MASKING PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)

class VarianceMasking:
    """
    Variance masking adds controlled random noise to numerical data.
    Preserves aggregate statistics while protecting individual values.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def add_percentage_variance(value, variance_percent=10, seed=None):
        """
        Add random variance as percentage of original value
        variance_percent: percentage of variance (e.g., 10 for ±10%)
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        
        # Generate consistent random variance based on value
        if seed:
            random.seed(seed)
        
        variance = value * (variance_percent / 100.0)
        noise = random.uniform(-variance, variance)
        return round(value + noise, 2)
    
    @staticmethod
    def add_fixed_variance(value, variance_amount=1000, seed=None):
        """
        Add fixed random variance
        variance_amount: fixed amount of variance
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        
        if seed:
            random.seed(seed)
        
        noise = random.uniform(-variance_amount, variance_amount)
        return round(value + noise, 2)
    
    @staticmethod
    def add_gaussian_noise(value, std_dev=5000, seed=None):
        """
        Add Gaussian (normal distribution) noise
        std_dev: standard deviation of noise
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        
        if seed:
            random.seed(seed)
        
        noise = random.gauss(0, std_dev)
        return round(value + noise, 2)
    
    @staticmethod
    def add_laplace_noise(value, scale=3000, seed=None):
        """
        Add Laplace noise (differential privacy)
        scale: scale parameter (sensitivity/epsilon)
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        
        if seed:
            random.seed(seed)
        
        # Laplace distribution
        u = random.uniform(-0.5, 0.5)
        noise = -scale * (1 if u > 0 else -1) * math.log(1 - 2 * abs(u))
        return round(value + noise, 2)

import math

# Create UDFs for variance masking
add_percentage_variance_udf = udf(
    lambda x: VarianceMasking.add_percentage_variance(x, 10, hash(x) % 10000),
    DoubleType()
)

add_fixed_variance_udf = udf(
    lambda x: VarianceMasking.add_fixed_variance(x, 5000, hash(x) % 10000),
    DoubleType()
)

add_gaussian_noise_udf = udf(
    lambda x: VarianceMasking.add_gaussian_noise(x, 3000, hash(x) % 10000),
    DoubleType()
)

add_laplace_noise_udf = udf(
    lambda x: VarianceMasking.add_laplace_noise(x, 2000, hash(x) % 10000),
    DoubleType()
)

# Apply different variance masking techniques
variance_masked_df = df.select(
    col("id"),
    col("first_name"),
    col("last_name"),
    col("salary").alias("original_salary"),
    add_percentage_variance_udf("salary").alias("salary_10pct_variance"),
    add_fixed_variance_udf("salary").alias("salary_fixed_variance"),
    add_gaussian_noise_udf("salary").alias("salary_gaussian_noise"),
    add_laplace_noise_udf("salary").alias("salary_laplace_noise")
)

print("\nVariance Masked Salaries:")
print("(Different noise addition techniques)")
variance_masked_df.show(truncate=False)

class HybridMasking:
    """
    Combine multiple masking patterns for comprehensive data protection
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def apply_hybrid_masking(df, strategy="balanced"):
        """
        Apply combination of masking techniques based on data sensitivity
        
        Strategies:
        - conservative: Maximum protection (static + substitution)
        - balanced: Mix of techniques (default)
        - analytical: Preserve statistics (shuffling + variance)
        """
        
        if strategy == "conservative":
            # Maximum protection - static masking + substitution
            result = df.select(
                col("id"),
                substitute_first_name_udf("first_name").alias("first_name"),
                substitute_last_name_udf("last_name").alias("last_name"),
                concat(lit("masked_"), md5("email"), lit("@example.com")).alias("email"),
                substitute_ssn_udf("ssn").alias("ssn"),
                substitute_phone_udf("phone").alias("phone"),
                lit("XXX XXXXX XX").alias("address"),
                substitute_cc_udf("credit_card").alias("credit_card"),
                (col("salary") / 10000).cast(IntegerType()) * 10000).alias("salary"),
                col("hire_date")
            )
            
        elif strategy == "analytical":
            # Preserve analytics - shuffling + variance
            temp_df = ShufflingMasking.shuffle_column(df, "first_name", 100)
            temp_df = ShufflingMasking.shuffle_column(temp_df, "last_name", 101)
            temp_df = ShufflingMasking.shuffle_column(temp_df, "ssn", 102)
            
            result = temp_df.select(
                col("id"),
                col("shuffled_first_name").alias("first_name"),
                col("shuffled_last_name").alias("last_name"),
                col("email"),
                col("shuffled_ssn").alias("ssn"),
                col("phone"),
                col("address"),
                col("credit_card"),
                add_gaussian_noise_udf("salary").alias("salary"),
                col("hire_date")
            )
            
        else:  # balanced
            # Balanced approach - mix of techniques
            result = df.select(
                col("id"),
                # Substitution for names
                substitute_first_name_udf("first_name").alias("first_name"),
                substitute_last_name_udf("last_name").alias("last_name"),
                # FPE for email (keep format)
                concat(substring(md5("email"), 1, 8), lit("@"), 
                       expr("split(email, '@')[1]")).alias("email"),
                # Static masking for SSN
                concat(lit("XXX-XX-"), substring("ssn", -4, 4)).alias("ssn"),
                # Substitution for phone
                substitute_phone_udf("phone").alias("phone"),
                # Static for address
                regexp_replace("address", r"\d+", "XXX").alias("address"),
                # FPE for credit card
                concat(lit("XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-"), substring("credit_card", -4, 4)).alias("credit_card"),
                # Variance for salary
                add_percentage_variance_udf("salary").alias("salary"),
                col("hire_date")
            )
        
        return result

# Demonstrate different hybrid strategies
print("\nOriginal Data:")
df.show(truncate=False)

print("\n1. CONSERVATIVE Strategy (Maximum Protection):")
conservative_masked = HybridMasking.apply_hybrid_masking(df, "conservative")
conservative_masked.show(truncate=False)

print("\n2. ANALYTICAL Strategy (Preserve Statistics):")
analytical_masked = HybridMasking.apply_hybrid_masking(df, "analytical")
analytical_masked.show(truncate=False)

print("\n3. BALANCED Strategy (Mixed Techniques):")
balanced_masked = HybridMasking.apply_hybrid_masking(df, "balanced")
balanced_masked.show(truncate=False)

def benchmark_masking(name, masking_function):
    """Benchmark a masking function"""
    start_time = time.time()
    result = masking_function()
    result.count()  # Trigger execution
    end_time = time.time()
    duration = end_time - start_time
    print(f"{name:30s}: {duration:.3f} seconds")
    return duration

class MaskingValidator:
    """
    Validate masked data quality and compliance
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_no_pii_leakage(original_df, masked_df, pii_columns):
        """Check that PII is not present in masked data"""
        print("\nPII Leakage Check:")
        print("-" * 50)
        
        for col_name in pii_columns:
            # Get original values
            original_values = set([row[col_name] for row in original_df.select(col_name).collect()])
            masked_values = set([row[col_name] for row in masked_df.select(col_name).collect()])
            
            # Check for intersection
            leakage = original_values.intersection(masked_values)
            
            if leakage:
                print(f"⚠ WARNING: {col_name} - {len(leakage)} values leaked")
            else:
                print(f"✓ PASS: {col_name} - No PII leakage detected")
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_format_preservation(original_df, masked_df, format_columns):
        """Validate that format is preserved"""
        print("\nFormat Preservation Check:")
        print("-" * 50)
        
        for col_name in format_columns:
            original_sample = original_df.select(col_name).first()[0]
            masked_sample = masked_df.select(col_name).first()[0]
            
            # Check length preservation
            if len(str(original_sample)) == len(str(masked_sample)):
                print(f"✓ PASS: {col_name} - Length preserved")
            else:
                print(f"⚠ WARNING: {col_name} - Length changed")
            
            # Check pattern preservation (e.g., XXX-XX-XXXX)
            original_pattern = re.sub(r'\d', 'X', str(original_sample))
            original_pattern = re.sub(r'[a-zA-Z]', 'A', original_pattern)
            masked_pattern = re.sub(r'\d', 'X', str(masked_sample))
            masked_pattern = re.sub(r'[a-zA-Z]', 'A', masked_pattern)
            
            if original_pattern == masked_pattern:
                print(f"  ✓ Pattern preserved: {original_pattern}")
            else:
                print(f"  ⚠ Pattern changed: {original_pattern} -> {masked_pattern}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_statistical_properties(original_df, masked_df, numeric_columns):
        """Validate statistical properties are preserved"""
        print("\nStatistical Properties Check:")
        print("-" * 50)
        
        for col_name in numeric_columns:
            orig_stats = original_df.select(col_name).describe().collect()
            masked_stats = masked_df.select(col_name).describe().collect()
            
            # Compare means
            orig_mean = float(orig_stats[1][1])
            masked_mean = float(masked_stats[1][1])
            mean_diff_pct = abs((masked_mean - orig_mean) / orig_mean * 100)
            
            print(f"\n{col_name}:")
            print(f"  Original Mean: {orig_mean:.2f}")
            print(f"  Masked Mean:   {masked_mean:.2f}")
            print(f"  Difference:    {mean_diff_pct:.2f}%")
            
            if mean_diff_pct < 5:
                print(f"  ✓ PASS: Mean preserved within 5%")
            else:
                print(f"  ⚠ INFO: Mean changed by {mean_diff_pct:.2f}%")

# Run validation
print("\nValidating BALANCED Hybrid Masking:")
MaskingValidator.validate_no_pii_leakage(
    df, balanced_masked, 
    ["first_name", "last_name", "email", "ssn"]
)

MaskingValidator.validate_format_preservation(
    df, balanced_masked,
    ["ssn", "phone", "credit_card"]
)

MaskingValidator.validate_statistical_properties(
    df, balanced_masked,
    ["salary"]
)

# MASKING CONFIGURATION FRAMEWORK
# =============================================================================

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("MASKING CONFIGURATION FRAMEWORK")
print("=" * 80)

class MaskingConfig:
    """
    Configuration-driven masking framework
    Define masking rules in configuration and apply them dynamically
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.rules = {}
    
    def add_rule(self, column_name, masking_type, **kwargs):
        """
        Add a masking rule for a column
        
        Args:
            column_name: Name of the column to mask
            masking_type: Type of masking (static, fpe, substitution, etc.)
            **kwargs: Additional parameters for the masking function
        """
        self.rules[column_name] = {
            'type': masking_type,
            'params': kwargs
        }
        return self
    
    def apply_masking(self, df):
        """Apply all configured masking rules to dataframe"""
        result_df = df
        
        for col_name, rule in self.rules.items():
            masking_type = rule['type']
            params = rule['params']
            
            if masking_type == 'static':
                mask_char = params.get('mask_char', 'X')
                show_last = params.get('show_last', 0)
                
                if show_last > 0:
                    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                        col_name,
                        concat(
                            lit(mask_char * 10),
                            substring(col(col_name), -show_last, show_last)
                        )
                    )
                else:
                    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                        col_name,
                        lit(mask_char * 10)
                    )
            
            elif masking_type == 'hash':
                hash_func = params.get('hash_function', 'md5')
                if hash_func == 'md5':
                    result_df = result_df.withColumn(col_name, md5(col(col_name)))
                elif hash_func == 'sha256':
                    result_df = result_df.withColumn(col_name, sha2(col(col_name), 256))
            
            elif masking_type == 'fpe':
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                    col_name,
                    fpe_alpha_udf(col(col_name))
                )
            
            elif masking_type == 'substitution':
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                    col_name,
                    substitute_first_name_udf(col(col_name))
                )
            
            elif masking_type == 'variance':
                variance_pct = params.get('variance_percent', 10)
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                    col_name,
                    add_percentage_variance_udf(col(col_name))
                )
            
            elif masking_type == 'nullify':
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(col_name, lit(None))
            
            elif masking_type == 'truncate':
                keep_chars = params.get('keep_chars', 0)
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                    col_name,
                    substring(col(col_name), 1, keep_chars)
                )
        
        return result_df
    
    def export_config(self):
        """Export configuration as dictionary"""
        return self.rules
    
    def import_config(self, config_dict):
        """Import configuration from dictionary"""
        self.rules = config_dict
        return self

# Example usage of configuration framework
print("\nConfiguration-Driven Masking Example:")

from datetime import datetime

class MaskingAuditor:
    """
    Audit trail for masking operations
    Track what was masked, when, by whom, and how
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.audit_logs = []
    
    def log_masking_operation(self, operation_type, columns_masked, 
                             record_count, user, additional_info=None):
        """Log a masking operation"""
        log_entry = {
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'operation_type': operation_type,
            'columns_masked': columns_masked,
            'record_count': record_count,
            'user': user,
            'additional_info': additional_info or {}
        }
        self.audit_logs.append(log_entry)
        return log_entry
    
    def get_audit_trail(self):
        """Get all audit logs"""
        return self.audit_logs
    
    def export_audit_trail(self, spark_session):
        """Export audit trail as DataFrame"""
        if not self.audit_logs:
            return None
        
        return spark_session.createDataFrame(self.audit_logs)

    elif environment == "staging":
        # Staging: Substitution for realistic testing
        masked_df = source_df.select(

class DifferentialPrivacy:
    """
    Implement differential privacy using Laplace mechanism
    Provides mathematical privacy guarantees
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def add_laplace_noise_dp(value, sensitivity, epsilon):
        """
        Add Laplace noise for differential privacy
        
        Args:
            value: Original value
            sensitivity: Global sensitivity of the query
            epsilon: Privacy budget (smaller = more privacy)
        
        Returns:
            Noisy value with DP guarantee
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        
        scale = sensitivity / epsilon
        # Laplace distribution
        u = random.uniform(-0.5, 0.5)
        noise = -scale * (1 if u > 0 else -1) * math.log(1 - 2 * abs(u))
        
        return round(value + noise, 2)
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_sensitivity(df, column_name, query_type="count"):
        """
        Calculate sensitivity for different query types
        """
        if query_type == "count":
            return 1  # Adding/removing one record changes count by 1
        elif query_type == "sum":
            # Maximum value that can be contributed by one record
            max_val = df.agg({column_name: "max"}).collect()[0][0]
            return max_val
        elif query_type == "avg":
            # For average, sensitivity depends on range and count
            stats = df.agg({column_name: "max", column_name: "min"}).collect()[0]
            range_val = stats[0] - stats[1]
            count = df.count()
            return range_val / count
        
        return 1

# Apply differential privacy
epsilon_values = [0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0]  # Different privacy budgets

print("\nDifferential Privacy with Different Epsilon Values:")
print("(Smaller epsilon = More privacy, More noise)")
print("-" * 70)

for epsilon in epsilon_values:
    sensitivity = DifferentialPrivacy.calculate_sensitivity(df, "salary", "sum")
    
    dp_udf = udf(
        lambda x: DifferentialPrivacy.add_laplace_noise_dp(x, sensitivity, epsilon),
        DoubleType()
    )
    
    dp_df = df.select(
        col("id"),
        col("first_name"),
        col("salary").alias("original_salary"),
        dp_udf("salary").alias(f"dp_salary_eps_{epsilon}")
    )
    
    print(f"\nEpsilon = {epsilon} (Privacy Budget)")
    dp_df.show()
    
    # Calculate privacy loss
    original_sum = df.agg({"salary": "sum"}).collect()[0][0]
    noisy_sum = dp_df.agg({f"dp_salary_eps_{epsilon}": "sum"}).collect()[0][0]
    error_pct = abs((noisy_sum - original_sum) / original_sum * 100)
    
    print(f"  Original Sum: ${original_sum:,.2f}")
    print(f"  Noisy Sum:    ${noisy_sum:,.2f}")
    print(f"  Error:        {error_pct:.2f}%")

class MaskingMetadata:
    """
    Generate metadata and documentation for masked datasets
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_metadata(original_df, masked_df, masking_rules):
        """Generate comprehensive metadata"""
        
        metadata = {
            'dataset_info': {
                'original_record_count': original_df.count(),
                'masked_record_count': masked_df.count(),
                'original_columns': original_df.columns,
                'masked_columns': masked_df.columns,
                'masking_timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
            },
            'column_metadata': {},
            'masking_rules': masking_rules,
            'data_quality': {}
        }
        
        # Column-level metadata
        for col_name in original_df.columns:
            if col_name in masked_df.columns:
                orig_null_count = original_df.filter(col(col_name).isNull()).count()
                masked_null_count = masked_df.filter(col(col_name).isNull()).count()
                
                metadata['column_metadata'][col_name] = {
                    'original_null_count': orig_null_count,
                    'masked_null_count': masked_null_count,
                    'data_type': str(original_df.schema[col_name].dataType),
                    'masked': col_name in masking_rules
                }
        
        return metadata
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_data_dictionary(masked_df, masking_config):
        """Generate data dictionary for masked dataset"""
        
        data_dict = []
        
        for col_name in masked_df.columns:
            col_info = {
                'column_name': col_name,
                'data_type': str(masked_df.schema[col_name].dataType),
                'nullable': masked_df.schema[col_name].nullable,
                'masked': 'Yes' if col_name in masking_config else 'No',
                'masking_method': masking_config.get(col_name, {}).get('type', 'None'),
                'description': f'Masked using {masking_config.get(col_name, {}).get("type", "N/A")}'
            }
            data_dict.append(col_info)
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(data_dict)
