print("\n\n6. COMPOSITE KEY JOIN PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
print("Description: Joins using multiple columns as composite keys")
print("Use Case: Multi-dimensional data, fact-dimension joins")

# Create multi-dimensional sales data
sales_facts = [
    ("2024-01", "USA", "Electronics", "Laptop", 10, 12000),
    ("2024-01", "USA", "Electronics", "Phone", 25, 15000),
    ("2024-01", "UK", "Electronics", "Laptop", 5, 6000),
    ("2024-01", "UK", "Clothing", "Shirt", 50, 2500),
    ("2024-02", "USA", "Electronics", "Laptop", 12, 14400),
    ("2024-02", "USA", "Clothing", "Pants", 30, 3000),
    ("2024-02", "UK", "Electronics", "Phone", 15, 9000),
    ("2024-02", "UK", "Clothing", "Shirt", 40, 2000)
]

region_targets = [
    ("2024-01", "USA", 25000, 0.10),
    ("2024-01", "UK", 15000, 0.12),
    ("2024-02", "USA", 30000, 0.10),
    ("2024-02", "UK", 18000, 0.12)
]

category_targets = [
    ("2024-01", "Electronics", 30000, 0.08),
    ("2024-01", "Clothing", 5000, 0.15),
    ("2024-02", "Electronics", 35000, 0.08),
    ("2024-02", "Clothing", 6000, 0.15)
]

product_info = [
    ("Electronics", "Laptop", "High-end", 1200),
    ("Electronics", "Phone", "Mid-range", 600),
    ("Clothing", "Shirt", "Casual", 50),
    ("Clothing", "Pants", "Formal", 100)
]

sales_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    sales_facts,
    ["month", "region", "category", "product", "quantity", "revenue"]
)

region_targets_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    region_targets,
    ["month", "region", "target_revenue", "commission_rate"]
)

category_targets_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    category_targets,
    ["month", "category", "category_target", "bonus_rate"]
)

product_info_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    product_info,
    ["category", "product", "segment", "unit_price"]
)

# Composite Key Join 1: Two-column composite key (month + region)
print("\nComposite Key Join 1: Month + Region")

composite_region = sales_df \
    .join(
        region_targets_df,
        ["month", "region"],  # Composite key
        "inner"
    ) \
    .select(
        "month",
        "region",
        "category",
        "product",
        "revenue",
        "target_revenue",
        (col("revenue") / col("target_revenue") * 100).alias("achievement_pct"),
        (col("revenue") * col("commission_rate")).alias("commission")
    )

print("\nRegion Performance with Composite Key:")
composite_region.show(truncate=False)

# Composite Key Join 2: Three-column composite key
print("\nComposite Key Join 2: Month + Category + Product")

composite_product = sales_df \
    .join(
        category_targets_df,
        ["month", "category"],  # First composite key
        "inner"
    ) \
    .join(
        product_info_df,
        ["category", "product"],  # Second composite key
        "inner"
    ) \
    .select(
        "month",
        "region",
        "category",
        "product",
        "segment",
        "quantity",
        "revenue",
        "unit_price",
        "category_target",
        (col("revenue") * col("bonus_rate")).alias("bonus")
    )

print("\nProduct Performance with Multiple Composite Keys:")
composite_product.show(truncate=False)

# Composite Key Join 3: Aggregated composite key join
print("\nComposite Key Join 3: Aggregated Composite Keys")

# Aggregate sales by month and category
category_sales = sales_df \
    .groupBy("month", "category") \
    .agg(
        sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue"),
        sum("quantity").alias("total_quantity"),
        count("*").alias("num_products")
    )

# Join with category targets using composite key
composite_agg = category_sales \
    .join(
        category_targets_df,
        ["month", "category"],
        "inner"
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "target_achievement",
        (col("total_revenue") / col("category_target") * 100)
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "bonus_earned",
        when(col("target_achievement") >= 100, 
             col("total_revenue") * col("bonus_rate"))
        .otherwise(0)
    ) \
    .select(
        "month",
        "category",
        "total_revenue",
        "category_target",
        round("target_achievement", 2).alias("achievement_pct"),
        "num_products",
        round("bonus_earned", 2).alias("bonus")
    ) \
    .orderBy("month", "category")

print("\nAggregated Category Performance:")
composite_agg.show(truncate=False)

# Composite Key Join 4: Complex multi-level composite key
print("\nComposite Key Join 4: Multi-Level Composite Key Analysis")

# Create dimension hierarchy
region_hierarchy = [
    ("USA", "North America", "Americas"),
    ("UK", "Europe", "EMEA")
]

category_hierarchy = [
    ("Electronics", "Technology", "Hard Goods"),
    ("Clothing", "Apparel", "Soft Goods")
]

region_hier_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    region_hierarchy,
    ["region", "sub_continent", "continent"]
)

category_hier_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    category_hierarchy,
    ["category", "dept", "division"]
)

# Multi-level join with composite keys
multi_level = sales_df \
    .join(region_hier_df, "region", "inner") \
    .join(category_hier_df, "category", "inner") \
    .join(product_info_df, ["category", "product"], "inner") \
    .groupBy("month", "continent", "division") \
    .agg(
        sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue"),
        sum("quantity").alias("total_quantity"),
        countDistinct("region").alias("num_regions"),
        countDistinct("category").alias("num_categories")
    ) \
    .orderBy("month", "continent", "division")

print("\nMulti-Level Hierarchy Analysis:")
multi_level.show(truncate=False)

# Create comprehensive e-commerce dataset
customers_ecom = [

    (1002, "Bob Smith", "Standard", "2023-03-20", "bob@email.com"),
    (1003, "Carol White", "Premium", "2023-05-10", "carol@email.com"),
    (1004, "David Brown", "Basic", "2023-07-01", "david@email.com")
]

orders_ecom = [
    (5001, 1001, "2024-01-10 10:30:00", 350.00, "Completed"),
    (5002, 1002, "2024-01-11 14:20:00", 125.00, "Shipped"),
    (5003, 1001, "2024-01-12 09:15:00", 275.00, "Processing"),
    (5004, 1003, "2024-01-13 16:45:00", 450.00, "Completed"),
    (5005, 1004, "2024-01-14 11:00:00", 80.00, "Cancelled")
]

order_items = [
    (5001, "PROD-101", 2, 150.00),
    (5001, "PROD-102", 1, 50.00),
    (5002, "PROD-103", 1, 125.00),
    (5003, "PROD-101", 1, 150.00),
    (5003, "PROD-104", 1, 125.00),
    (5004, "PROD-105", 3, 150.00),
    (5005, "PROD-102", 1, 50.00),
    (5005, "PROD-106", 1, 30.00)
]

products_ecom = [
    ("PROD-101", "Laptop", "Electronics", 1500.00, "2023-01-01", "9999-12-31"),
    ("PROD-102", "Mouse", "Electronics", 50.00, "2023-01-01", "2024-01-31"),
    ("PROD-102", "Mouse Pro", "Electronics", 75.00, "2024-02-01", "9999-12-31"),
    ("PROD-103", "Keyboard", "Electronics", 125.00, "2023-01-01", "9999-12-31"),
    ("PROD-104", "Monitor", "Electronics", 300.00, "2023-01-01", "9999-12-31"),
    ("PROD-105", "Headphones", "Electronics", 150.00, "2023-01-01", "9999-12-31"),
    ("PROD-106", "Cable", "Accessories", 30.00, "2023-01-01", "9999-12-31")
]

tier_benefits = [
    ("Premium", 0.15, 100, "Free"),
    ("Standard", 0.10, 50, "Standard"),
    ("Basic", 0.05, 25, "Economy")
]

shipping_tracking = [
    (5001, "2024-01-11", "NYC", "Delivered", "2024-01-13"),
    (5002, "2024-01-12", "LA", "In Transit", None),
    (5003, "2024-01-13", "Chicago", "Pending", None),
    (5004, "2024-01-14", "Boston", "Delivered", "2024-01-16")
]

payment_methods = [
    (5001, "Credit Card", "VISA-1234", "2024-01-10 10:35:00"),
    (5002, "PayPal", "paypal@bob.com", "2024-01-11 14:25:00"),
    (5003, "Credit Card", "AMEX-5678", "2024-01-12 09:20:00"),
    (5004, "Debit Card", "MC-9012", "2024-01-13 16:50:00"),
    (5005, "Credit Card", "VISA-3456", "2024-01-14 11:05:00")

# Create DataFrames
customers_ecom_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    customers_ecom,
    ["customer_id", "customer_name", "tier", "join_date", "email"]
)

orders_ecom_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    orders_ecom,
    ["order_id", "customer_id", "order_timestamp", "order_amount", "order_status"]
)

order_items_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    order_items,
    ["order_id", "product_id", "quantity", "item_price"]
)

    products_ecom,
    ["product_id", "product_name", "category", "price", "valid_from", "valid_to"]

    tier_benefits,
    ["tier", "discount_rate", "reward_points_multiplier", "shipping_type"]
)

shipping_tracking_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    shipping_tracking,
    ["order_id", "ship_date", "destination", "ship_status", "delivery_date"]
)

payment_methods_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    payment_methods,
    ["order_id", "payment_type", "payment_details", "payment_timestamp"]
)

# COMPREHENSIVE JOIN PIPELINE
print("\nBuilding comprehensive order analysis pipeline...")
print("Combining: Multi-way + Temporal + Composite Key + Theta joins\n")

# Step 1: Temporal join to get correct product info at order time
orders_with_date = orders_ecom_df.withColumn(
    "order_date",
    to_date(col("order_timestamp"))
)

# Step 2: Multi-way join - Orders + Items + Products (temporal) + Customers + Tier Benefits
comprehensive_result = orders_with_date \
    .join(
        order_items_df,
        "order_id",
        "inner"
    ) \
    .join(
        products_ecom_df,
        (order_items_df.product_id == products_ecom_df.product_id) &
        (orders_with_date.order_date >= products_ecom_df.valid_from) &
        (orders_with_date.order_date <= products_ecom_df.valid_to),
        "inner"
    ) \
    .join(
        customers_ecom_df,
        orders_with_date.customer_id == customers_ecom_df.customer_id,
        "inner"
    ) \
    .join(
        tier_benefits_df,
        customers_ecom_df.tier == tier_benefits_df.tier,
        "inner"
    ) \
    .join(
        shipping_tracking_df,
        orders_with_date.order_id == shipping_tracking_df.order_id,
        "left"
    ) \
    .join(
        payment_methods_df,
        orders_with_date.order_id == payment_methods_df.order_id,
        "left"
    )

# Step 3: Calculate derived metrics
final_analysis = comprehensive_result \
    .withColumn(
        "line_total",
        col("quantity") * col("item_price")
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "discount_amount",
        col("line_total") * col("discount_rate")
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "final_price",
        col("line_total") - col("discount_amount")
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "reward_points",
        (col("final_price") * col("reward_points_multiplier")).cast("int")
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "days_to_delivery",
        when(col("delivery_date").isNotNull(),
             datediff(col("delivery_date"), col("ship_date")))
        .otherwise(None)
    ) \
    .select(
        orders_with_date.order_id,
        "customer_name",
        customers_ecom_df.tier,
        "order_timestamp",
        products_ecom_df.product_name,
        "category",
        "quantity",
        "item_price",
        round("discount_amount", 2).alias("discount"),
        round("final_price", 2).alias("final_price"),
        "reward_points",
        "payment_type",
        "ship_status",
        "days_to_delivery",
        "order_status"
    )

print("Comprehensive Order Analysis Results:")
final_analysis.orderBy("order_id").show(50, truncate=False)

# Aggregate analysis by customer
print("\nCustomer-Level Aggregation:")
customer_summary = final_analysis \
    .groupBy("customer_name", "tier") \
    .agg(
        count("order_id").alias("num_orders"),
        sum("final_price").alias("total_spent"),
        sum("reward_points").alias("total_points"),
        avg("days_to_delivery").alias("avg_delivery_days"),
        collect_set("category").alias("categories_purchased")
    ) \
    .orderBy(col("total_spent").desc())

customer_summary.show(truncate=False)

# Category performance analysis
print("\nCategory Performance Analysis:")
category_performance = final_analysis \
    .groupBy("category") \
    .agg(
        sum("final_price").alias("revenue"),
        sum("quantity").alias("units_sold"),
        countDistinct(orders_with_date.order_id).alias("num_orders"),
        avg("discount").alias("avg_discount"),
        avg("days_to_delivery").alias("avg_delivery")
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "avg_order_value",
        round(col("revenue") / col("num_orders"), 2)
    ) \
    .orderBy(col("revenue").desc())

category_performance.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# ADVANCED PATTERN: SELF-JOIN WITH COMPOSITE KEYS
# ============================================================================
print("\n\n" + "=" * 80)
print("ADVANCED PATTERN: PRODUCT RECOMMENDATION (SELF-JOIN)")
print("=" * 80)
print("Finding products frequently bought together")

# Create order pairs for market basket analysis
order_pairs = order_items_df.alias("oi1").join(
    order_items_df.alias("oi2"),
    (col("oi1.order_id") == col("oi2.order_id")) &
    (col("oi1.product_id") < col("oi2.product_id")),  # Avoid duplicates
    "inner"
).select(
    col("oi1.product_id").alias("product_a"),
    col("oi2.product_id").alias("product_b"),
    col("oi1.order_id")
)

# Aggregate and join with product names
product_affinity = order_pairs \
    .groupBy("product_a", "product_b") \
    .agg(
        count("*").alias("times_bought_together")
    ) \
    .join(
        products_ecom_df.select("product_id", "product_name").alias("pa"),
        col("product_a") == col("pa.product_id"),
        "inner"
    ) \
    .join(
        products_ecom_df.select("product_id", "product_name").alias("pb"),
        col("product_b") == col("pb.product_id"),
        "inner"
    ) \
    .select(
        col("pa.product_name").alias("product_1"),
        col("pb.product_name").alias("product_2"),
        "times_bought_together"
    ) \
    .orderBy(col("times_bought_together").desc())

print("\nProduct Affinity Analysis:")
product_affinity.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# WINDOW FUNCTIONS WITH JOINS
# ============================================================================
print("\n\n" + "=" * 80)
print("WINDOW FUNCTIONS WITH JOINS")
print("=" * 80)
print("Ranking and analytics across joined datasets")

# Customer ranking by spending within tier
window_tier = Window.partitionBy("tier").orderBy(col("total_spent").desc())

customer_ranking = customer_summary \
    .withColumn(
        "rank_in_tier",
        row_number().over(window_tier)
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "percentile_in_tier",
        percent_rank().over(window_tier)
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "running_total_in_tier",
        sum("total_spent").over(window_tier.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0))
    ) \
    .select(
        "customer_name",
        "tier",
        "num_orders",
        round("total_spent", 2).alias("total_spent"),
        "rank_in_tier",
        round("percentile_in_tier", 3).alias("percentile"),
        round("running_total_in_tier", 2).alias("running_total")
    )

print("\nCustomer Ranking Within Tier:")
customer_ranking.show(truncate=False)

# CROSS JOIN WITH FILTERS (CARTESIAN PRODUCT)
# ============================================================================
print("\n\n" + "=" * 80)
print("CROSS JOIN PATTERN (Controlled Cartesian Product)")
print("=" * 80)
print("Use Case: Generating all possible combinations with filters")

# Create promotion compatibility matrix
promotions = [
    ("PROMO-A", "Electronics", 0.10),
    ("PROMO-B", "Electronics", 0.15),
    ("PROMO-C", "Accessories", 0.20),
    ("PROMO-D", "All Categories", 0.05)
]

customer_segments = [
    ("Premium", 1000),
    ("Standard", 500),
    ("Basic", 100)
]

promotions_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    promotions,
    ["promo_code", "applicable_category", "discount_pct"]
)

segments_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    customer_segments,
    ["segment", "min_spend"]
)

# Cross join to create all promotion-segment combinations
print("\nGenerating Promotion-Segment Compatibility Matrix:")
promo_segment_matrix = promotions_df.crossJoin(segments_df) \
    .withColumn(
        "max_discount_value",
        col("min_spend") * col("discount_pct")
    ) \
    .select(
        "promo_code",
        "applicable_category",
        "segment",
        "min_spend",
        (col("discount_pct") * 100).alias("discount_pct"),
        round("max_discount_value", 2).alias("max_discount")
    ) \
    .orderBy("segment", "promo_code")

promo_segment_matrix.show(truncate=False)

# Filtered Cross Join: Only valid combinations
print("\nFiltered Cross Join: Products eligible for each promotion:")
product_promo_eligibility = products_ecom_df \
    .filter(col("valid_to") == "9999-12-31") \
    .select("product_id", "product_name", "category", "price") \
    .crossJoin(promotions_df) \
    .filter(
        (col("applicable_category") == col("category")) |
        (col("applicable_category") == "All Categories")
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "discounted_price",
        round(col("price") * (1 - col("discount_pct")), 2)
    ) \
    .withColumn(
        "savings",
        round(col("price") * col("discount_pct"), 2)
    ) \
    .select(
        "product_name",
        "category",
        "price",
        "promo_code",
        "discounted_price",
        "savings"
    ) \
    .orderBy("product_name", col("savings").desc())

product_promo_eligibility.show(30, truncate=False)

]

    .filter(col("valid_to") == "9999-12-31") \

    pricing_tiers_df.alias("t2"),
    (col("t1.tier_name") < col("t2.tier_name")) &  # Avoid duplicates
    (col("t1.max_price") >= col("t2.min_price")) &
    (col("t1.min_price") <= col("t2.max_price")),
    "inner"
).select(
    col("t1.tier_name").alias("tier_1"),
    col("t1.min_price").alias("t1_min"),
    col("t1.max_price").alias("t1_max"),
    col("t2.tier_name").alias("tier_2"),
    col("t2.min_price").alias("t2_min"),
    col("t2.max_price").alias("t2_max"),
    greatest(col("t1.min_price"), col("t2.min_price")).alias("overlap_start"),
    least(col("t1.max_price"), col("t2.max_price")).alias("overlap_end")
)

print("Overlapping Price Tiers:")
tier_overlaps.show(truncate=False)

# Create data with gaps
primary_customer_info = [
    (1001, "Alice Johnson", "alice@email.com", None),
    (1002, "Bob Smith", None, "555-0102"),
    (1003, None, "carol@email.com", "555-0103")
]

secondary_customer_info = [
    (1001, None, "alice.j@backup.com", "555-0101"),
    (1002, "Robert Smith", "bob@backup.com", None),
    (1004, "David Brown", "david@backup.com", "555-0104")
]

    primary_customer_info,
    ["customer_id", "name", "email", "phone"]

    secondary_customer_info,
    ["customer_id", "name", "email", "phone"]
)

# Coalesce join to merge data with fallback
print("\nMerging customer data with fallback values:")
merged_customers = primary_df.join(
    secondary_df,
    "customer_id",
    "full_outer"
).select(
    coalesce(primary_df.customer_id, secondary_df.customer_id).alias("customer_id"),
    coalesce(primary_df.name, secondary_df.name).alias("name"),
    coalesce(primary_df.email, secondary_df.email).alias("email"),
    coalesce(primary_df.phone, secondary_df.phone).alias("phone"),
    when(primary_df.customer_id.isNotNull() & secondary_df.customer_id.isNotNull(), "Both")
    .when(primary_df.customer_id.isNotNull(), "Primary Only")
    .otherwise("Secondary Only").alias("source")
)

print("\nMerged Customer Data:")
merged_customers.show(truncate=False)

# Technique 2: Salting for skewed keys
print("\n2. Salting technique for heavily skewed key (customer_id=1001):")

# Identify skewed keys
skew_threshold = 50
skewed_keys = skewed_orders_df.groupBy("customer_id") \
    .count() \
    .filter(col("count") > skew_threshold) \
    .select("customer_id")

# Add salt to skewed keys
salt_factor = 5
salted_
```python
salted_orders = skewed_orders_df.join(
    skewed_keys.withColumn("is_skewed", lit(True)),
    "customer_id",
    "left"
).withColumn(
    "salt",
    when(col("is_skewed"), (rand() * salt_factor).cast("int")).otherwise(lit(0))
).withColumn(
    "salted_customer_id",
    concat(col("customer_id"), lit("_"), col("salt"))
)

# Replicate customer records for skewed keys
salted_customers = customers_ecom_df.join(
    skewed_keys.withColumn("is_skewed", lit(True)),
    "customer_id",
    "left"
).withColumn(
    "replicate_count",
    when(col("is_skewed"), lit(salt_factor)).otherwise(lit(1))
)

# Explode to create replicas
from pyspark.sql.functions import explode, sequence

salted_customers = salted_customers.withColumn(
    "salt",
    explode(sequence(lit(0), col("replicate_count") - 1))
).withColumn(
    "salted_customer_id",
    concat(col("customer_id"), lit("_"), col("salt"))
)

# Join on salted keys
salted_join_result = salted_orders.join(
    salted_customers,
    "salted_customer_id",
    "inner"
).select(
    salted_orders.order_id,
    salted_orders.customer_id,
    salted_customers.customer_name,
    salted_orders.order_date,
    salted_orders.amount
)

print(f"\nSalted join result count: {salted_join_result.count()}")
print("Sample of salted join results:")
salted_join_result.show(10, truncate=False)

]

incremental_sales = [
    (4, "PROD-101", "2024-01-04", 1200),  # New record
    (5, "PROD-104", "2024-01-05", 800),   # New record
    (2, "PROD-102", "2024-01-02", 550)    # Updated record
]

historical_df = spark.createDataFrame(

    ["sale_id", "product_id", "sale_date", "amount"]

new_records = incremental_df.join(
    historical_df.select("sale_id"),
    "sale_id",
    "left_anti"

    col("hist.amount").alias("old_amount"),
    col("inc.sale_date")
)

print("\nUpdated Records:")
updated_records.show(truncate=False)

merged_incremental = new_records.union(
    updated_records.select(
        "sale_id", "new_product_id", "sale_date", "new_amount"
    ).withColumnRenamed("new_product_id", "product_id")
    .withColumnRenamed("new_amount", "amount")
)

print("\nMerged Incremental Changes:")
merged_incremental.show(truncate=False)

# Join with product dimension
incremental_with_product = merged_incremental.join(

    "product_id",
    "inner"

# CONDITIONAL JOIN PATTERN
# ============================================================================
print("\n\n" + "=" * 80)
print("CONDITIONAL JOIN PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("Different join logic based on conditions")

# Create customer segments with different join rules
vip_customers = [
    (1001, "VIP"),
    (1003, "VIP")
]

regular_customers = [
    (1002, "Regular"),
    (1004, "Regular")
]

vip_df = spark.createDataFrame(vip_customers, ["customer_id", "segment"])
regular_df = spark.createDataFrame(regular_customers, ["customer_id", "segment"])

# VIP customers get special pricing (different product table)
vip_pricing = [
    ("PROD-101", 1350.00),  # 10% discount
    ("PROD-103", 112.50),
    ("PROD-105", 135.00)
]

vip_pricing_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    vip_pricing,
    ["product_id", "vip_price"]
)

# Conditional join based on customer segment
print("\nConditional Join: Different pricing for VIP vs Regular customers")

# Tag orders with segment
orders_with_segment = orders_ecom_df.join(
    vip_df.union(regular_df),
    "customer_id",
    "left"
).withColumn(
    "segment",
    coalesce(col("segment"), lit("Regular"))
)

# Join orders with items
orders_items_segment = orders_with_segment.join(
    order_items_df,
    "order_id",
    "inner"
)

# Conditional join with pricing
conditional_pricing = orders_items_segment.join(
    vip_pricing_df,
    (orders_items_segment.product_id == vip_pricing_df.product_id) &
    (orders_items_segment.segment == "VIP"),
    "left"
).join(
    products_ecom_df.filter(col("valid_to") == "9999-12-31")
        .select(col("product_id").alias("prod_id"), "product_name", "price"),
    orders_items_segment.product_id == col("prod_id"),
    "inner"
).select(
    orders_items_segment.order_id,
    orders_items_segment.customer_id,
    "segment",
    orders_items_segment.product_id,
    "product_name",
    "quantity",
    "price",
    "vip_price",
    when(col("vip_price").isNotNull(), col("vip_price"))
        .otherwise(col("price")).alias("final_price")
).withColumn(
    "line_total",
    col("quantity") * col("final_price")
).withColumn(
    "savings",
    when(col("vip_price").isNotNull(), 
         col("quantity") * (col("price") - col("vip_price")))
    .otherwise(lit(0))
)

print("\nConditional Pricing Results:")
conditional_pricing.orderBy("order_id").show(30, truncate=False)

# Summary by segment
print("\nSummary by Customer Segment:")
segment_summary = conditional_pricing.groupBy("segment").agg(
    countDistinct("customer_id").alias("num_customers"),
    count("order_id").alias("num_orders"),
    sum("line_total").alias("total_revenue"),
    sum("savings").alias("total_savings"),
    avg("line_total").alias("avg_order_line")
)

segment_summary.show(truncate=False)

# RECURSIVE JOIN PATTERN (Hierarchical Data)
# ============================================================================
print("\n\n" + "=" * 80)
print("RECURSIVE JOIN PATTERN - HIERARCHICAL DATA")
print("=" * 80)
print("Finding all levels in organizational hierarchy")

# Organizational hierarchy
org_hierarchy = [
    (1, "CEO", None, 1),
    (2, "CTO", 1, 2),
    (3, "CFO", 1, 2),
    (4, "VP Engineering", 2, 3),
    (5, "VP Product", 2, 3),
    (6, "Controller", 3, 3),
    (7, "Engineering Manager", 4, 4),
    (8, "Product Manager", 5, 4),
    (9, "Senior Engineer", 7, 5),
    (10, "Engineer", 7, 5)
]

org_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    org_hierarchy,
    ["emp_id", "emp_name", "manager_id", "level"]
)

print("\nOrganization Structure:")
org_df.orderBy("level", "emp_id").show(truncate=False)

# Recursive join to find all subordinates
print("\nFinding all subordinates for each manager (recursive):")

# Level 1: Direct reports
level1 = org_df.alias("mgr").join(
    org_df.alias("emp"),
    col("mgr.emp_id") == col("emp.manager_id"),
    "inner"
).select(
    col("mgr.emp_id").alias("manager_id"),
    col("mgr.emp_name").alias("manager_name"),
    col("emp.emp_id").alias("subordinate_id"),
    col("emp.emp_name").alias("subordinate_name"),
    lit(1).alias("levels_down")
)

# Level 2: Reports of reports
level2 = level1.alias("l1").join(
    org_df.alias("emp"),
    col("l1.subordinate_id") == col("emp.manager_id"),
    "inner"
).select(
    col("l1.manager_id"),
    col("l1.manager_name"),
    col("emp.emp_id").alias("subordinate_id"),
    col("emp.emp_name").alias("subordinate_name"),
    lit(2).alias("levels_down")
)

# Level 3: Three levels down
level3 = level2.alias("l2").join(
    org_df.alias("emp"),
    col("l2.subordinate_id") == col("emp.manager_id"),
    "inner"
).select(
    col("l2.manager_id"),
    col("l2.manager_name"),
    col("emp.emp_id").alias("subordinate_id"),
    col("emp.emp_name").alias("subordinate_name"),
    lit(3).alias("levels_down")
)

# Union all levels
all_subordinates = level1.union(level2).union(level3)

print("\nAll Manager-Subordinate Relationships:")
all_subordinates.orderBy("manager_id", "levels_down", "subordinate_id").show(50, truncate=False)

# Count subordinates per manager
print("\nSubordinate Count by Manager:")
subordinate_count = all_subordinates.groupBy("manager_id", "manager_name").agg(
    countDistinct("subordinate_id").alias("total_subordinates"),
    count(when(col("levels_down") == 1, 1)).alias("direct_reports"),
    count(when(col("levels_down") == 2, 1)).alias("level_2_reports"),
    count(when(col("levels_down") == 3, 1)).alias("level_3_reports")
).orderBy("manager_id")

subordinate_count.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PERFORMANCE COMPARISON AND BEST PRACTICES
# ============================================================================
print("\n\n" + "=" * 80)
print("JOIN PERFORMANCE BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY")
print("=" * 80)

best_practices = """
1. MULTI-WAY JOINS:
   - Join smallest tables first
   - Use broadcast hints for tables < 10MB
   - Consider bucketing for repeated joins
   
2. CHAINED JOINS:
   - Cache intermediate results if reused
   - Filter early to reduce data volume
   - Use appropriate join types (inner vs left)

3. THETA JOINS:
   - Avoid if possible (expensive)
   - Filter before theta join
   - Consider bucketing on range columns

4. FUZZY JOINS:
   - Use blocking/indexing to reduce comparisons
   - Implement in stages (exact -> approximate)
   - Consider Soundex or other phonetic algorithms

5. TEMPORAL JOINS:
   - Index on date columns
   - Partition by time periods
   - Use appropriate date granularity

6. COMPOSITE KEY JOINS:
   - Join on all key columns simultaneously
   - Order matters for performance
   - Consider bucketing on composite keys

7. SKEWED DATA:
   - Use salting for hot keys
   - Broadcast small tables
   - Enable adaptive query execution

8. GENERAL:
   - Prefer broadcast joins when applicable
   - Use appropriate join types
   - Enable statistics collection
   - Monitor shuffle operations
   - Cache frequently accessed data
"""

print(best_practices)

from pyspark.sql.functions import *

# PATTERN 1: SMALL FILE COMPACTION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Combine many small files into larger files to improve read performance
# Use Case: When you have thousands of small files from streaming or incremental loads

class SmallFileCompactionPattern:
    """
    Compacts small files into larger files based on configurable thresholds.
    Reduces metadata overhead and improves query performance.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, target_file_size_mb: int = 128):
        """
        Initialize Small File Compaction Pattern
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
            target_file_size_mb: Target size for compacted files in MB
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.target_file_size_mb = target_file_size_mb
        
    def analyze_file_distribution(self, path: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Analyze the current file distribution in the given path
        
        Args:
            path: Path to analyze
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with file statistics
        """
        # Get file information using Hadoop FileSystem API
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(hadoop_conf)
        path_obj = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(path)
        
        files = []
        if fs.exists(path_obj):
            file_status = fs.listStatus(path_obj)
            for status in file_status:
                if not status.isDirectory() and status.getPath().getName().endswith('.parquet'):
                    files.append({
                        'name': status.getPath().getName(),
                        'size_mb': status.getLen() / (1024 * 1024)
                    })
        
        if not files:
            return {'total_files': 0, 'total_size_mb': 0, 'avg_size_mb': 0, 'small_files': 0}
        
        total_size = sum(f['size_mb'] for f in files)
        small_files = sum(1 for f in files if f['size_mb'] < self.target_file_size_mb / 2)
        
        return {
            'total_files': len(files),
            'total_size_mb': total_size,
            'avg_size_mb': total_size / len(files),
            'small_files': small_files,
            'small_file_percentage': (small_files / len(files)) * 100
        }
    
    def compact_small_files(self, 
                           input_path: str, 
                           output_path: str,
                           partition_cols: List[str] = None,
                           compact_threshold_mb: float = 10.0) -> Dict:
        """
        Compact small files into larger files
        
        Args:
            input_path: Source path with small files
            output_path: Destination path for compacted files
            partition_cols: Columns to partition by (optional)
            compact_threshold_mb: Files smaller than this will be compacted
            
        Returns:
            Compaction statistics
        """
        print(f"Starting small file compaction from {input_path}")
        
        # Analyze before compaction
        before_stats = self.analyze_file_distribution(input_path)
        print(f"Before compaction: {before_stats}")
        
        # Read the data
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(input_path)
        
        # Calculate optimal number of partitions based on data size and target file size
        total_size_mb = before_stats['total_size_mb']
        num_partitions = max(1, int(total_size_mb / self.target_file_size_mb))
        
        print(f"Repartitioning to {num_partitions} partitions")
        
        # Repartition and write
        if partition_cols:
            # Repartition by partition columns first, then coalesce within partitions
            df.repartition(num_partitions, *partition_cols) \
                .write \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .partitionBy(*partition_cols) \
                .parquet(output_path)
        else:
            # Simple coalesce for non-partitioned data
            df.coalesce(num_partitions) \
                .write \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .parquet(output_path)
        
        # Analyze after compaction
        after_stats = self.analyze_file_distribution(output_path)
        print(f"After compaction: {after_stats}")
        
        return {
            'before': before_stats,
            'after': after_stats,
            'reduction_percentage': ((before_stats['total_files'] - after_stats['total_files']) / 
                                    before_stats['total_files'] * 100) if before_stats['total_files'] > 0 else 0
        }

# PATTERN 2: BIN-PACKING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Optimally pack data into bins (files) to maximize storage efficiency
# Use Case: When you need to optimize storage for variable-sized records

class BinPackingPattern:
    """
    Implements bin-packing algorithm to optimize file sizes and reduce waste.
    Uses First-Fit Decreasing (FFD) algorithm for optimal packing.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, bin_size_mb: int = 128):
        """
        Initialize Bin-Packing Pattern
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
            bin_size_mb: Target bin (file) size in MB
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.bin_size_mb = bin_size_mb
        self.bin_size_bytes = bin_size_mb * 1024 * 1024
        
    def estimate_record_size(self, df: DataFrame, sample_fraction: float = 0.01) -> float:
        """
        Estimate average record size in bytes
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to analyze
            sample_fraction: Fraction of data to sample
            
        Returns:
            Average record size in bytes
        """
        # Sample data and estimate size
        sample_df = df.sample(fraction=sample_fraction, seed=42)
        count = sample_df.count()
        
        if count == 0:
            return 0
        
        # Write sample to temporary location to measure size
        temp_path = f"/tmp/size_estimate_{datetime.now().timestamp()}"
        sample_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(temp_path)
        
        # Measure size
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(hadoop_conf)
        path_obj = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(temp_path)
        
        total_size = 0
        if fs.exists(path_obj):
            content_summary = fs.getContentSummary(path_obj)
            total_size = content_summary.getLength()
        
        # Cleanup
        fs.delete(path_obj, True)
        
        return total_size / count if count > 0 else 0
    
    def assign_bins(self, df: DataFrame, partition_col: str = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Assign records to bins using First-Fit Decreasing algorithm
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            partition_col: Optional partition column for grouping
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with bin assignments
        """
        # Estimate record size
        avg_record_size = self.estimate_record_size(df)
        records_per_bin = int(self.bin_size_bytes / avg_record_size) if avg_record_size > 0 else 1000
        
        print(f"Average record size: {avg_record_size:.2f} bytes")
        print(f"Records per bin: {records_per_bin}")
        
        # Add bin assignment using row_number
        if partition_col:
            # Assign bins within each partition
            window_spec = Window.partitionBy(partition_col).orderBy(monotonically_increasing_id())
            df_with_bins = df.withColumn(
                "bin_id",
                concat(
                    col(partition_col).cast("string"),
                    lit("_bin_"),
                    (row_number().over(window_spec) / records_per_bin).cast("int").cast("string")
                )
            )
        else:
            # Global bin assignment
            window_spec = Window.orderBy(monotonically_increasing_id())
            df_with_bins = df.withColumn(
                "bin_id",
                concat(
                    lit("bin_"),
                    (row_number().over(window_spec) / records_per_bin).cast("int").cast("string")
                )
            )
        
        return df_with_bins
    
    def pack_and_write(self, 
                       df: DataFrame, 
                       output_path: str,
                       partition_col: str = None) -> Dict:
        """
        Pack data into optimally sized bins and write
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            output_path: Output path
            partition_col: Optional partition column
            
        Returns:
            Packing statistics
        """
        print("Starting bin-packing operation")
        
        # Assign bins
        df_with_bins = self.assign_bins(df, partition_col)
        
        # Count bins
        num_bins = df_with_bins.select("bin_id").distinct().count()
        total_records = df.count()
        
        print(f"Total records: {total_records}")
        print(f"Number of bins: {num_bins}")
        
        # Write partitioned by bin_id
        df_with_bins.repartition("bin_id") \
            .drop("bin_id") \
            .write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(output_path)
        
        return {
            'total_records': total_records,
            'num_bins': num_bins,
            'avg_records_per_bin': total_records / num_bins if num_bins > 0 else 0,
            'target_bin_size_mb': self.bin_size_mb
        }

# PATTERN 3: MERGE-ON-READ PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Maintain base files and delta files, merging on read
# Use Case: Optimized for write-heavy workloads with occasional reads

class MergeOnReadPattern:
    """
    Implements Merge-on-Read (MOR) pattern for update-heavy workloads.
    Writes go to delta files, reads merge base + delta files.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize Merge-on-Read Pattern
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
        """
        self.spark = spark
        
    def write_base_data(self, df: DataFrame, base_path: str, partition_cols: List[str] = None):
        """
        Write initial base data
        
        Args:
            df: Base DataFrame
            base_path: Path for base data
            partition_cols: Partition columns
        """
        print(f"Writing base data to {base_path}")
        
        writer = df.write.mode("overwrite")
        
        if partition_cols:
            writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_cols)
        
        writer.parquet(base_path)
        print("Base data written successfully")
    
    def write_delta(self, 
                    df: DataFrame, 
                    delta_path: str, 
                    version: str = None,
                    partition_cols: List[str] = None):
        """
        Write delta (incremental) data
        
        Args:
            df: Delta DataFrame
            delta_path: Path for delta data
            version: Version identifier (timestamp if None)
            partition_cols: Partition columns
        """
        if version is None:
            version = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
        
        versioned_path = f"{delta_path}/version={version}"
        print(f"Writing delta data to {versioned_path}")
        
        # Add metadata columns
        df_with_meta = df.withColumn("_delta_version", lit(version)) \
                        .withColumn("_delta_timestamp", current_timestamp())
        
        writer = df_with_meta.write.mode("append")
        
        if partition_cols:
            writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_cols)
        
        writer.parquet(versioned_path)
        print(f"Delta version {version} written successfully")
    
    def read_merged_data(self, 
                         base_path: str, 
                         delta_path: str,
                         key_cols: List[str],
                         merge_strategy: str = "latest") -> DataFrame:
        """
        Read and merge base + delta data
        
        Args:
            base_path: Path to base data
            delta_path: Path to delta data
            key_cols: Key columns for merging
            merge_strategy: 'latest' or 'all_versions'
            
        Returns:
            Merged DataFrame
        """
        print("Reading and merging base + delta data")
        
        # Read base data
        base_df = self.spark.read.parquet(base_path)
        print(f"Base records: {base_df.count()}")
        
        # Read delta data
        try:
            delta_df = self.spark.read.parquet(delta_path)
            print(f"Delta records: {delta_df.count()}")
            
            if merge_strategy == "latest":
                # Keep only latest version for each key
                window_spec = Window.partitionBy(*key_cols).orderBy(col("_delta_timestamp").desc())
                delta_latest = delta_df.withColumn("rn", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
                                      .filter(col("rn") == 1) \
                                      .drop("rn", "_delta_version", "_delta_timestamp")
                
                # Union and deduplicate
                merged_df = base_df.unionByName(delta_latest, allowMissingColumns=True)
                
                # Keep latest record for each key
                window_spec_final = Window.partitionBy(*key_cols).orderBy(lit(1))
                result_df = merged_df.withColumn("rn", row_number().over(window_spec_final)) \
                                    .filter(col("rn") == 1) \
                                    .drop("rn")
            else:
                # Return all versions
                result_df = base_df.unionByName(
                    delta_df.drop("_delta_version", "_delta_timestamp"), 
                    allowMissingColumns=True
                )
            
            print(f"Merged records: {
```python
result_df.count()}")
            return result_df
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"No delta data found or error reading delta: {e}")
            return base_df
    
    def compact_deltas(self, 
                       base_path: str, 
                       delta_path: str,
                       key_cols: List[str],
                       partition_cols: List[str] = None):
        """
        Compact delta files into base (periodic maintenance)
        
        Args:
            base_path: Path to base data
            delta_path: Path to delta data
            key_cols: Key columns for merging
            partition_cols: Partition columns
        """
        print("Starting delta compaction")
        
        # Read merged data
        merged_df = self.read_merged_data(base_path, delta_path, key_cols, "latest")
        
        # Write back to base
        self.write_base_data(merged_df, base_path, partition_cols)
        
        # Archive or delete old deltas
        # In production, you might want to archive instead of delete
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(hadoop_conf)
        delta_path_obj = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(delta_path)
        
        if fs.exists(delta_path_obj):
            fs.delete(delta_path_obj, True)
            print("Delta files cleaned up")
        
        print("Delta compaction completed")

# PATTERN 4: COPY-ON-WRITE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Create new copies of files when updating, maintaining immutability
# Use Case: Read-heavy workloads where data consistency is critical

class CopyOnWritePattern:
    """
    Implements Copy-on-Write (COW) pattern for ACID compliance.
    Every update creates a new version of the entire dataset.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize Copy-on-Write Pattern
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
        """
        self.spark = spark
        
    def write_version(self, 
                      df: DataFrame, 
                      base_path: str, 
                      version: int = None,
                      partition_cols: List[str] = None) -> int:
        """
        Write a new version of the dataset
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to write
            base_path: Base path for versioned data
            version: Version number (auto-increment if None)
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            
        Returns:
            Version number written
        """
        # Determine version number
        if version is None:
            version = self._get_latest_version(base_path) + 1
        
        versioned_path = f"{base_path}/v{version:05d}"
        print(f"Writing version {version} to {versioned_path}")
        
        # Add version metadata
        df_with_version = df.withColumn("_version", lit(version)) \
                           .withColumn("_version_timestamp", current_timestamp())
        
        # Write complete dataset
        writer = df_with_version.write.mode("overwrite")
        
        if partition_cols:
            writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_cols)
        
        writer.parquet(versioned_path)
        
        # Update latest pointer (metadata file)
        self._update_latest_version(base_path, version)
        
        print(f"Version {version} written successfully")
        return version
    
    def read_version(self, base_path: str, version: int = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Read a specific version of the dataset
        
        Args:
            base_path: Base path for versioned data
            version: Version to read (latest if None)
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame for the specified version
        """
        if version is None:
            version = self._get_latest_version(base_path)
        
        if version == 0:
            raise ValueError("No versions available")
        
        versioned_path = f"{base_path}/v{version:05d}"
        print(f"Reading version {version} from {versioned_path}")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(versioned_path)
        return df.drop("_version", "_version_timestamp")
    
    def update_records(self, 
                       base_path: str,
                       updates_df: DataFrame,
                       key_cols: List[str],
                       partition_cols: List[str] = None) -> int:
        """
        Update records by creating a new version
        
        Args:
            base_path: Base path for versioned data
            updates_df: DataFrame with updates
            key_cols: Key columns for matching
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            
        Returns:
            New version number
        """
        print("Performing copy-on-write update")
        
        # Read latest version
        current_df = self.read_version(base_path)
        
        # Create update key for joining
        update_key = "_update_key"
        current_with_key = current_df.withColumn(
            update_key, 
            concat_ws("||", *[col(c) for c in key_cols])
        )
        updates_with_key = updates_df.withColumn(
            update_key, 
            concat_ws("||", *[col(c) for c in key_cols])
        )
        
        # Get keys that will be updated
        update_keys = updates_with_key.select(update_key).distinct()
        
        # Filter out records that will be updated
        unchanged_df = current_with_key.join(
            update_keys, 
            on=update_key, 
            how="left_anti"
        ).drop(update_key)
        
        # Union unchanged records with updates
        updated_df = unchanged_df.unionByName(
            updates_with_key.drop(update_key), 
            allowMissingColumns=True
        )
        
        # Write new version
        new_version = self.write_version(updated_df, base_path, partition_cols=partition_cols)
        
        print(f"Update completed. New version: {new_version}")
        return new_version
    
    def delete_records(self,
                       base_path: str,
                       delete_condition: str,
                       partition_cols: List[str] = None) -> int:
        """
        Delete records by creating a new version
        
        Args:
            base_path: Base path for versioned data
            delete_condition: SQL condition for deletion
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            
        Returns:
            New version number
        """
        print(f"Performing copy-on-write delete with condition: {delete_condition}")
        
        # Read latest version
        current_df = self.read_version(base_path)
        
        # Filter out records to delete
        filtered_df = current_df.filter(f"NOT ({delete_condition})")
        
        records_before = current_df.count()
        records_after = filtered_df.count()
        records_deleted = records_before - records_after
        
        print(f"Records deleted: {records_deleted}")
        
        # Write new version
        new_version = self.write_version(filtered_df, base_path, partition_cols=partition_cols)
        
        return new_version
    
    def _get_latest_version(self, base_path: str) -> int:
        """Get the latest version number"""
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(hadoop_conf)
        base_path_obj = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(base_path)
        
        if not fs.exists(base_path_obj):
            return 0
        
        # Look for version directories
        file_status = fs.listStatus(base_path_obj)
        versions = []
        for status in file_status:
            if status.isDirectory():
                dir_name = status.getPath().getName()
                if dir_name.startswith('v') and dir_name[1:].isdigit():
                    versions.append(int(dir_name[1:]))
        
        return max(versions) if versions else 0
    
    def _update_latest_version(self, base_path: str, version: int):
        """Update metadata file with latest version"""
        metadata_path = f"{base_path}/_latest_version"
        metadata_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            [(version, datetime.now())],
            ["version", "timestamp"]
        )
        metadata_df.coalesce(1).write.mode("overwrite").parquet(metadata_path)
    
    def cleanup_old_versions(self, base_path: str, keep_versions: int = 5):
        """
        Clean up old versions, keeping only the specified number
        
        Args:
            base_path: Base path for versioned data
            keep_versions: Number of recent versions to keep
        """
        print(f"Cleaning up old versions, keeping last {keep_versions}")
        
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(hadoop_conf)
        base_path_obj = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(base_path)
        
        if not fs.exists(base_path_obj):
            return
        
        # Get all version directories
        file_status = fs.listStatus(base_path_obj)
        versions = []
        for status in file_status:
            if status.isDirectory():
                dir_name = status.getPath().getName()
                if dir_name.startswith('v') and dir_name[1:].isdigit():
                    versions.append((int(dir_name[1:]), status.getPath()))
        
        # Sort versions and identify old ones
        versions.sort(reverse=True)
        
        if len(versions) <= keep_versions:
            print("No old versions to clean up")
            return
        
        # Delete old versions
        for version, path in versions[keep_versions:]:
            print(f"Deleting version {version}")
            fs.delete(path, True)
        
        print(f"Cleanup completed. Kept versions: {[v[0] for v in versions[:keep_versions]]}")


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: ADAPTIVE COMPACTION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Automatically adjust compaction strategy based on workload patterns
# Use Case: Dynamic workloads with varying read/write patterns

class AdaptiveCompactionPattern:
    """
    Implements adaptive compaction that adjusts strategy based on:
    - File size distribution
    - Read/write patterns
    - Data freshness requirements
    - Resource availability
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize Adaptive Compaction Pattern
        
        Args:
            spark: SparkSession instance
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.metrics_history = []
        
    def analyze_workload(self, path: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Analyze workload characteristics to determine optimal compaction strategy
        
        Args:
            path: Path to analyze
            
        Returns:
            Workload metrics
        """
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(hadoop_conf)
        path_obj = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(path)
        
        if not fs.exists(path_obj):
            return {'file_count': 0, 'recommendation': 'no_action'}
        
        # Collect file statistics
        file_status = fs.listStatus(path_obj)
        file_sizes = []
        total_size = 0
        
        for status in file_status:
            if not status.isDirectory() and status.getPath().getName().endswith('.parquet'):
                size_mb = status.getLen() / (1024 * 1024)
                file_sizes.append(size_mb)
                total_size += size_mb
        
        if not file_sizes:
            return {'file_count': 0, 'recommendation': 'no_action'}
        
        # Calculate metrics
        file_count = len(file_sizes)
        avg_size = total_size / file_count
        min_size = min(file_sizes)
        max_size = max(file_sizes)
        
        # Calculate variance
        variance = sum((x - avg_size) ** 2 for x in file_sizes) / file_count
        std_dev = variance ** 0.5
        
        # Count small files (< 10MB)
        small_files = sum(1 for s in file_sizes if s < 10)
        small_file_ratio = small_files / file_count
        
        # Calculate fragmentation score (0-1, higher = more fragmented)
        fragmentation_score = min(1.0, (std_dev / avg_size) if avg_size > 0 else 0)
        
        metrics = {
            'file_count': file_count,
            'total_size_mb': total_size,
            'avg_size_mb': avg_size,
            'min_size_mb': min_size,
            'max_size_mb': max_size,
            'std_dev_mb': std_dev,
            'small_files': small_files,
            'small_file_ratio': small_file_ratio,
            'fragmentation_score': fragmentation_score
        }
        
        # Determine recommendation
        metrics['recommendation'] = self._determine_strategy(metrics)
        
        # Store metrics for trend analysis
        self.metrics_history.append({
            'timestamp': datetime.now(),
            'metrics': metrics
        })
        
        return metrics
    
    def _determine_strategy(self, metrics: Dict) -> str:
        """
        Determine optimal compaction strategy based on metrics
        
        Args:
            metrics: Workload metrics
            
        Returns:
            Recommended strategy
        """
        file_count = metrics['file_count']
        small_file_ratio = metrics['small_file_ratio']
        fragmentation_score = metrics['fragmentation_score']
        avg_size = metrics['avg_size_mb']
        
        # Decision tree for strategy selection
        if file_count < 10:
            return 'no_action'
        
        # High fragmentation with many small files -> aggressive compaction
        if small_file_ratio > 0.7 and file_count > 100:
            return 'aggressive_compaction'
        
        # Moderate fragmentation -> standard compaction
        if small_file_ratio > 0.3 or fragmentation_score > 0.5:
            return 'standard_compaction'
        
        # Large files with low fragmentation -> bin packing
        if avg_size > 200 and fragmentation_score < 0.3:
            return 'bin_packing'
        
        # Mixed workload -> adaptive merge
        if fragmentation_score > 0.3:
            return 'adaptive_merge'
        
        return 'no_action'
    
    def execute_adaptive_compaction(self,
                                    input_path: str,
                                    output_path: str,
                                    partition_cols: List[str] = None,
                                    force_strategy: str = None) -> Dict:
        """
        Execute adaptive compaction based on workload analysis
        
        Args:
            input_path: Source path
            output_path: Destination path
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            force_strategy: Force a specific strategy (for testing)
            
        Returns:
```python
            Compaction results
        """
        print("Starting adaptive compaction analysis")
        
        # Analyze workload
        metrics = self.analyze_workload(input_path)
        strategy = force_strategy if force_strategy else metrics['recommendation']
        
        print(f"Workload metrics: {metrics}")
        print(f"Selected strategy: {strategy}")
        
        # Read data
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(input_path)
        total_records = df.count()
        
        start_time = datetime.now()
        
        # Execute strategy-specific compaction
        if strategy == 'no_action':
            print("No compaction needed")
            result = {
                'strategy': strategy,
                'action_taken': False,
                'metrics': metrics
            }
        
        elif strategy == 'aggressive_compaction':
            # Compact to very few large files
            print("Executing aggressive compaction")
            target_partitions = max(1, int(metrics['total_size_mb'] / 256))  # 256MB files
            
            if partition_cols:
                df.repartition(target_partitions, *partition_cols) \
                    .write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .partitionBy(*partition_cols) \
                    .parquet(output_path)
            else:
                df.coalesce(target_partitions) \
                    .write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .parquet(output_path)
            
            result = {
                'strategy': strategy,
                'action_taken': True,
                'target_partitions': target_partitions,
                'target_file_size_mb': 256
            }
        
        elif strategy == 'standard_compaction':
            # Standard compaction to 128MB files
            print("Executing standard compaction")
            target_partitions = max(1, int(metrics['total_size_mb'] / 128))
            
            if partition_cols:
                df.repartition(target_partitions, *partition_cols) \
                    .write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .partitionBy(*partition_cols) \
                    .parquet(output_path)
            else:
                df.coalesce(target_partitions) \
                    .write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .parquet(output_path)
            
            result = {
                'strategy': strategy,
                'action_taken': True,
                'target_partitions': target_partitions,
                'target_file_size_mb': 128
            }
        
        elif strategy == 'bin_packing':
            # Use bin packing for optimal distribution
            print("Executing bin-packing compaction")
            bin_packer = BinPackingPattern(self.spark, bin_size_mb=128)
            partition_col = partition_cols[0] if partition_cols else None
            pack_result = bin_packer.pack_and_write(df, output_path, partition_col)
            
            result = {
                'strategy': strategy,
                'action_taken': True,
                'bin_packing_result': pack_result
            }
        
        elif strategy == 'adaptive_merge':
            # Adaptive merge based on data characteristics
            print("Executing adaptive merge")
            
            # Analyze data skew
            if partition_cols:
                partition_stats = df.groupBy(*partition_cols).count()
                partition_counts = partition_stats.collect()
                
                # Calculate partition-specific targets
                total_count = sum(row['count'] for row in partition_counts)
                avg_count = total_count / len(partition_counts)
                
                # Repartition with skew handling
                df.repartition(*partition_cols) \
                    .write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .partitionBy(*partition_cols) \
                    .parquet(output_path)
            else:
                # Use adaptive coalesce
                target_partitions = max(1, int(metrics['total_size_mb'] / 128))
                df.coalesce(target_partitions) \
                    .write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .parquet(output_path)
            
            result = {
                'strategy': strategy,
                'action_taken': True,
                'adaptive_merge': True
            }
        
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown strategy: {strategy}")
        
        # Calculate execution time
        execution_time = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds()
        
        # Analyze results
        after_metrics = self.analyze_workload(output_path)
        
        result.update({
            'before_metrics': metrics,
            'after_metrics': after_metrics,
            'total_records': total_records,
            'execution_time_seconds': execution_time,
            'improvement_score': self._calculate_improvement(metrics, after_metrics)
        })
        
        print(f"Adaptive compaction completed in {execution_time:.2f} seconds")
        print(f"Improvement score: {result['improvement_score']:.2f}")
        
        return result
    
    def _calculate_improvement(self, before: Dict, after: Dict) -> float:
        """
        Calculate improvement score (0-100)
        
        Args:
            before: Metrics before compaction
            after: Metrics after compaction
            
        Returns:
            Improvement score
        """
        if before['file_count'] == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        # File count reduction (weight: 40%)
        file_reduction = (before['file_count'] - after['file_count']) / before['file_count']
        file_score = min(100, file_reduction * 100) * 0.4
        
        # Fragmentation reduction (weight: 40%)
        frag_reduction = before['fragmentation_score'] - after['fragmentation_score']
        frag_score = min(100, (frag_reduction / before['fragmentation_score'] * 100) 
                        if before['fragmentation_score'] > 0 else 0) * 0.4
        
        # Small file ratio improvement (weight: 20%)
        small_file_improvement = before['small_file_ratio'] - after['small_file_ratio']
        small_file_score = min(100, (small_file_improvement / before['small_file_ratio'] * 100)
                              if before['small_file_ratio'] > 0 else 0) * 0.2
        
        total_score = file_score + frag_score + small_file_score
        return max(0, min(100, total_score))
    
    def schedule_compaction(self,
                           input_path: str,
                           output_path: str,
                           threshold_score: float = 30.0,
                           partition_cols: List[str] = None) -> Dict:
        """
        Decide whether to run compaction based on threshold
        
        Args:
            input_path: Source path
            output_path: Destination path
            threshold_score: Minimum fragmentation score to trigger compaction
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            
        Returns:
            Scheduling decision and results
        """
        metrics = self.analyze_workload(input_path)
        
        # Calculate need score (0-100)
        need_score = (
            metrics['fragmentation_score'] * 50 +
            metrics['small_file_ratio'] * 30 +
            min(1.0, metrics['file_count'] / 1000) * 20
        )
        
        should_compact = need_score >= threshold_score
        
        result = {
            'should_compact': should_compact,
            'need_score': need_score,
            'threshold_score': threshold_score,
            'metrics': metrics
        }
        
        if should_compact:
            print(f"Compaction triggered (need score: {need_score:.2f} >= threshold: {threshold_score})")
            compaction_result = self.execute_adaptive_compaction(
                input_path, 
                output_path, 
                partition_cols
            )
            result['compaction_result'] = compaction_result
        else:
            print(f"Compaction skipped (need score: {need_score:.2f} < threshold: {threshold_score})")
        
        return result
    
    def get_metrics_trend(self, window_size: int = 10) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Get trend of metrics over time
        
        Args:
            window_size: Number of recent metrics to return
            
        Returns:
            List of historical metrics
        """
        return self.metrics_history[-window_size:]

def create_sample_data(spark: SparkSession, num_records: int = 10000) -> DataFrame:
    """
    Create sample data for testing compaction patterns
    
    Args:
        spark: SparkSession instance
        num_records: Number of records to generate
        
    Returns:
        Sample DataFrame
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, randn
    
    return spark.range(num_records) \
        .withColumn("category", (rand() * 10).cast("int").cast("string")) \
        .withColumn("value", randn() * 100) \
        .withColumn("timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("status", 
                   when(rand() > 0.5, "active").otherwise("inactive")) \
        .withColumn("description", 
                   concat(lit("Record_"), col("id").cast("string")))

def demo_merge_on_read():
    """Demonstrate Merge-on-Read Pattern"""
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("DEMO 3: MERGE-ON-READ PATTERN")
    print("="*80 + "\n")
    
    base_path = "/tmp/mor_base"
    delta_path = "/tmp/mor_delta"
    
    # Create and write base data
    base_df = create_sample_data(spark, 10000)
    
    mor = MergeOnReadPattern(spark)
    mor.write_base_data(base_df, base_path, partition_cols=["category"])
    
    print("Base data written")
    
    # Create and write delta updates
    delta_df = spark.range(5000, 15000) \
        .withColumn("category", (rand() * 10).cast("int").cast("string")) \
        .withColumn("value", randn() * 200) \
        .withColumn("timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("status", lit("updated")) \
        .withColumn("description", concat(lit("Updated_"), col("id").cast("string")))
    
    mor.write_delta(delta_df, delta_path, version="v1", partition_cols=["category"])
    
    print("Delta data written")
    
    # Read merged data
    merged_df = mor.read_merged_data(base_path, delta_path, ["id"], merge_strategy="latest")
    
    print(f"\nMerged data count: {merged_df.count()}")
    print("\nSample merged data:")
    merged_df.show(5)
    
    # Compact deltas
    print("\nCompacting deltas...")
    mor.compact_deltas(base_path, delta_path, ["id"], partition_cols=["category"])
    print("Delta compaction completed")

        .withColumn("category", lit("5")) \

        .withColumn("timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("status", lit("updated")) \
        .withColumn("description", lit("Updated record"))
    
    v2 = cow.update_records(base_path, updates_df, ["id"], partition_cols=["category"])

    # Perform delete
    v3 = cow.delete_records(base_path, "status = 'inactive'", partition_cols=["category"])
    print(f"Version {v3} written after delete")
    
    # Read different versions
    print("\nReading version 1:")
    v1_df = cow.read_version(base_path, version=1)
    print(f"  Record count: {v1_df.count()}")
    
    print("\nReading version 3 (latest):")
    v3_df = cow.read_version(base_path)
    print(f"  Record count: {v3_df.count()}")
    
    # Cleanup old versions
    print("\n
```python
Cleaning up old versions...")
    cow.cleanup_old_versions(base_path, keep_versions=2)


def demo_adaptive_compaction():
    """Demonstrate Adaptive Compaction Pattern"""
    print("\n" + "="*80)

    print("="*80 + "\n")
    
    # Create test scenarios with different characteristics
    
    # Scenario 1: Many small files

    output_path1 = "/tmp/adaptive_scenario1_output"
    
    df1.repartition(300).write.mode("overwrite").parquet(input_path1)
    
    adaptive = AdaptiveCompactionPattern(spark)
    result1 = adaptive.execute_adaptive_compaction(
        input_path1,
        output_path1,
        partition_cols=["category"]
    )
    
    print(f"\n  Strategy selected: {result1['strategy']}")

    print(f"  Files after: {result1['after_metrics']['file_count']}")
    print(f"  Improvement score: {result1['improvement_score']:.2f}")
    print(f"  Execution time: {result1['execution_time_seconds']:.2f} seconds")
    
    # Scenario 2: Large files with good distribution
    print("\n\nScenario 2: Well-distributed large files")
    df2 = create_sample_data(spark, 100000)
    input_path2 = "/tmp/adaptive_scenario2_input"
    output_path2 = "/tmp/adaptive_scenario2_output"
    
    df2.repartition(5).write.mode("overwrite").parquet(input_path2)
    
    result2 = adaptive.execute_adaptive_compaction(
        input_path2,
        output_path2,
        partition_cols=["category"]
    )
    
    print(f"\n  Strategy selected: {result2['strategy']}")
    print(f"  Files before: {result2['before_metrics']['file_count']}")
    print(f"  Files after: {result2['after_metrics']['file_count']}")
    print(f"  Improvement score: {result2['improvement_score']:.2f}")
    
    # Scenario 3: Using scheduled compaction
    print("\n\nScenario 3: Scheduled compaction with threshold")
    df3 = create_sample_data(spark, 75000)
    input_path3 = "/tmp/adaptive_scenario3_input"
    output_path3 = "/tmp/adaptive_scenario3_output"
    
    df3.repartition(150).write.mode("overwrite").parquet(input_path3)
    
    schedule_result = adaptive.schedule_compaction(
        input_path3,

    print(f"  Threshold: {schedule_result['threshold_score']}")
    
    if schedule_result['should_compact']:
        comp_result = schedule_result['compaction_result']
        print(f"  Strategy used: {comp_result['strategy']}")
        print(f"  Improvement: {comp_result['improvement_score']:.2f}")
    
    # Show metrics trend
    print("\n\nMetrics Trend (last 3 analyses):")
    trend = adaptive.get_metrics_trend(window_size=3)
    for i, entry in enumerate(trend, 1):
        metrics = entry['metrics']
        print(f"\n  Analysis {i}:")
        print(f"    File count: {metrics['file_count']}")
        print(f"    Fragmentation score: {metrics['fragmentation_score']:.3f}")
        print(f"    Small file ratio: {metrics['small_file_ratio']:.3f}")
        print(f"    Recommendation: {metrics['recommendation']}")


def demo_comparison_all_patterns():

          f"{results['small_file_compaction']['files_after']}")
    print(f"  Reduction: {results['small_file_compaction']['reduction']:.2f}%")

    print(f"  Execution time: {results['bin_packing']['time']:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Number of bins: {results['bin_packing']['bins']}")
    print(f"  Records per bin: {results['bin_packing']['records_per_bin']:.0f}")
    
    print("\nAdaptive Compaction:")
    print(f"  Execution time: {results['adaptive_compaction']['time']:.2f}s")
    print(f"  Strategy selected: {results['adaptive_compaction']['strategy']}")
    print(f"  Files: {results['adaptive_compaction']['files_before']} → "
          f"{results['adaptive_compaction']['files_after']}")
    print(f"  Improvement score: {results['adaptive_compaction']['improvement_score']:.2f}")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)


def demo_real_world_scenario():
    """Demonstrate a real-world incremental data pipeline scenario"""
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REAL-WORLD SCENARIO: INCREMENTAL DATA PIPELINE")
    print("="*80 + "\n")
    
    print("Simulating a daily incremental data pipeline with compaction...")
    
    base_path = "/tmp/realworld_base"
    delta_path = "/tmp/realworld_delta"
    compacted_path = "/tmp/realworld_compacted"
    
    # Day 1: Initial load
    print("\nDay 1: Initial data load")
    day1_df = create_sample_data(spark, 50000)
    mor = MergeOnReadPattern(spark)
    mor.write_base_data(day1_df, base_path, partition_cols=["category"])
    print(f"  Loaded {day1_df.count()} records")
    
    # Days 2-7: Incremental updates
    for day in range(2, 8):
        print(f"\nDay {day}: Incremental update")
        
        # Simulate daily incremental data (updates and new records)
        start_id = (day - 1) * 10000
        end_id = start_id + 15000
        
        daily_df = spark.range(start_id, end_id) \
            .withColumn("category", (rand() * 10).cast("int").cast("string")) \
            .withColumn("value", randn() * 100) \
            .withColumn("timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("status", 
                       when(rand() > 0.7, "updated").otherwise("active")) \
            .withColumn("description", 
                       concat(lit(f"Day{day}_"), col("id").cast("string")))
        
        mor.write_delta(daily_df, delta_path, version=f"day{day}", 
                       partition_cols=["category"])
        print(f"  Added {daily_df.count()} records to delta")
        
        # Analyze delta accumulation
        adaptive = AdaptiveCompactionPattern(spark)
        delta_metrics = adaptive.analyze_workload(delta_path)
        print(f"  Delta files: {delta_metrics['file_count']}")
        print(f"  Fragmentation score: {delta_metrics['fragmentation_score']:.3f}")
    
    # Week-end: Compact deltas
    print("\nWeek-end: Compacting accumulated deltas")
    mor.compact_deltas(base_path, delta_path, ["id"], partition_cols=["category"])
    
    # Final compaction for optimal read performance
    print("\nFinal optimization: Adaptive compaction")
    adaptive = AdaptiveCompactionPattern(spark)
    final_result = adaptive.execute_adaptive_compaction(
        base_path,
        compacted_path,
        partition_cols=["category"]
    )
    
    print(f"\nFinal Results:")
    print(f"  Strategy: {final_result['strategy']}")
    print(f"  Total records: {final_result['total_records']}")
    print(f"  Files: {final_result['before_metrics']['file_count']} → "
          f"{final_result['after_metrics']['file_count']}")
    print(f"  Improvement score: {final_result['improvement_score']:.2f}")
    print(f"  Total execution time: {final_result['execution_time_seconds']:.2f}s")
    
    # Verify data integrity
    print("\nVerifying data integrity...")
    final_df = spark.read.parquet(compacted_path)
    final_count = final_df.count()
    distinct_count = final_df.select("id").distinct().count()
    
    print(f"  Total records: {final_count}")
    print(f"  Distinct IDs: {distinct_count}")
    print(f"  Data integrity: {'✓ PASSED' if final_count == distinct_count else '✗ FAILED'}")
